# FrameAssembly (`frameassembly`)

> Rootless, offline "Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code" DSL, Rust compiler, and PCAP-to-`.fasm` decompiler (v2.0.0) that compiles strict-lowercase `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) code into deterministic, nanosecond-precision `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures—and decompiles `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures back into `.fasm` code—across 81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols, with IPv4/IPv6 flow reuse, automatic 4-tuple TCP `seq`/`acknum` and reply-port tracking, and SNMPv3 USM (RFC 3414/3826/7860) cryptography. Built as the upstream companion compiler to Wireshark/`tshark` (inspection), `tcpreplay` (wire injection), and Suricata/Zeek/Snort (IDS/IPS testing).

FrameAssembly (`https://frameassembly.ai.studio/`, `https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly`, `https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly`, `https://docs.rs/frameassembly`) synthesizes bit-exact, reproducible `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures offline in userspace with no `libpcap` or raw sockets required, and provides an interactive browser playground at `https://frameassembly.ai.studio/`. Every protocol compiles with **zero mandatory sub-keywords** (emitting RFC-compliant wire defaults and ports) and supports explicit field and payload overrides via `frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]` (default root command), `frameassembly show <input.fasm>`, `frameassembly reverse <input.pcap> [output.fasm]`, `frameassembly help [subcommand]`, and `frameassembly version`.

### Zero-Shot `.fasm` Grammar & Anti-Hallucination Reference

# FrameAssembly

> Rootless, offline "Packets as Code" Rust compiler, PCAP-to-`.fasm` decompiler, and DSL (`frameassembly` v2.0.0) that compiles strict-lowercase `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) code into deterministic, nanosecond-precision `.pcap`/`.pcapng` captures—and reverses `.pcap`/`.pcapng` back into `.fasm` code—across 81 native L2–L7 protocols, with 4-tuple TCP `seq`/`acknum` tracking, reply-port swapping, IPv4/IPv6 flow reuse, and SNMPv3 USM (`RFC 3414`/`3826`/`7860`) crypto.

FrameAssembly (`https://frameassembly.ai.studio/`, `https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly`, `https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly`, `https://docs.rs/frameassembly`) is the upstream synthetic network traffic generator and packet-crafting compiler for **Wireshark**/**`tshark`**, **`tcpreplay`**, and **Suricata**/**Zeek**/**Snort** (offline in userspace—no `CAP_NET_RAW`, `libpcap`, lab VMs, or manual TCP math). Full RAG bundle: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/llms-full.txt`.

**Core `.fasm` v2.0.0 Language Rules & Defaults**

1. **Three-Block Structure (No `loop`)**: `host <id> { [ip <v4_or_v6>] [mac <mac>] }` (`ip` or `mac` required; MAC-only valid for the 8 L2 protocols), optional `flow <id>(<p1>, <p2>, ...) { <stmts> }`, and **one** `compile { <flow_calls_or_inline_frames> }` block (`loop` removed in v2.0.0).
2. **Strict-Lowercase Keywords (`[a-z0-9]+`) vs. Flexible Identifiers**: Every built-in keyword, protocol, modifier, and time unit (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) is **strictly lowercase alphanumeric with zero `_` and zero `-`**. User `host`, `flow`, and param names match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*` (`fw-dmz-01`, `core_sw`); `"..."` wire strings preserve casing.
3. **1 Statement = 1 Frame & Timing**: `a -> b <proto> ...` or `a <- b <proto> ...` emits 1 frame. `wait <u32><ns|us|ms|s|m>` sets pre-frame delay (default `10ms`; PCAPNG epoch `1_700_000_000_000_000_000` ns, `IfTsResol(9)`; `show` starts frame 1 at `0.000` ms).
4. **4-Tuple TCP, Port Swap & `reverse`**: Streams start at `seq = 1000` (`win = 64240`, `srcport = 12345`). `syn`/`fin` add `+1`; payloads add byte length. TCP L7 lines emit `psh ack` sharing `seq`/`acknum` with raw `tcp`; `<-` swaps IPs, MACs, and ports. `reverse` emits `host1`, `host2` (zero `_`), strict lowercase, and zero `loop`.
5. **Dual-Stack & MAC Derivation**: Flows work over IPv4 (`0x0800`) and IPv6 (`0x86DD`); mixing IPv4/IPv6 in one statement is a semantic error. `mac` accepts `00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`, `00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`, `001a.2b3c.4d5e`, or derives RFC 1112 / RFC 2464 / IEEE 802.1D / `00:00:00:00:00:01`–`02` defaults.
6. **Three-Way `.fasm` Disambiguation**: FrameAssembly `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`, `//` comments, `host`/`flow`/`compile`, `->`/`<-`) is distinct from x86 Flat Assembler (`;` comments, `format PE`/`ELF`) and FPGA FASM (`#` comments, tile bit paths).

**Anti-Hallucination Guardrails (`❌ NEVER` vs `✅ ALWAYS`)**

| Construct | ❌ NEVER WRITE | ✅ ALWAYS WRITE (v2.0.0 `.fasm`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Keyword Casing** | `HOST`, `FLOW`, `COMPILE`, `TCP`, `SYN`, `WAIT 5MS` | `host`, `flow`, `compile`, `tcp`, `syn`, `wait 5ms` |
| **Keyword `_` or `-`** | `echo_request`, `inner_vlan`, `client_hello`, `host_hdr`, `who-is` | `echorequest`, `innervlan`, `clienthello`, `hosthdr`, `whois` |
| **Comments** | `# comment`, `; comment`, or `/* block */` | `// single-line comment` |
| **Host Block** | `host c = { ipv4: "10.0.0.1", mask: 24 }`, `ipv6 ::1`, `host c {}` | `host c { ip 10.0.0.1 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }` or `host sw { mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }` |
| **Flow Signature** | `flow web { from c to s send http }` | `flow web(c, s) { c -> s http get uri "/" }` |
| **Inter-Frame Delay** | `[+5ms] c -> s tcp ack` or standalone `wait 5ms` | `c -> s tcp ack wait 5ms` |
| **Ports & TCP Ack** | `sport 1234 dport 80 ack 100 sack_perm` | `srcport 1234 dstport 80 seq 1 acknum 100 sackperm` |
| **TCP Flags** | `flags [syn, ack]` or `flags="SA"` | `tcp syn ack` (`syn ack fin rst psh urg ece cwr`) |
| **Hop Limit & QoS** | `hop_limit 64`, `hoplimit 64`, or `tos 46` | `ttl 64 dscp 46 ecn 2` |
| **VLAN & QinQ** | `vlan 0`, `qinq 100 200`, or `qinq 100 inner_vlan 200` | `vlan 100 pcp 5 dei 0` or `qinq 100 innervlan 200` |
| **HTTP & RTSP Hdrs** | `http get host "a.com"` or `rtsp setup transport "..."` | `http get uri "/" hosthdr "a.com"` / `rtsp setup transporthdr "..."` |
| **BGP vs RIP Prefix** | `bgp update prefix 10.0.0.0/8` / `rip prefix "10.0.0.0/8"` | `bgp update prefix "10.0.0.0/8"` / `rip prefix 10.0.0.0` |
| **DHCP vs SNMP ID** | `dhcp discover txid 1` or `snmp2 get req_id 1` | `dhcp discover xid 1` / `snmp2 get reqid 1` |
| **IKEv2 & SNMPv3** | `ikev2 sa_init` or `snmp3 auth "sha256" "pw"` | `ikev2 sainit` (`createchildsa`\|`informational`) / `snmp3 auth sha256 "pw"` |
| **Compile & Loops** | `loop 3 { f(h1, h2) }`, omitted `compile`, or `compile { f }` | `compile { f(h1, h2) f(h1, h2) h1 -> h2 icmp }` |
| **CLI Invocation** | `-o out.pcap`, `--output`, or `compile` subcommand | `frameassembly demo.fasm out.pcap` / `frameassembly reverse out.pcap out.fasm` |

**Universal Cross-Layer Modifiers**

- **L2**: `srcmac <mac>`, `dstmac <mac>`, `ethertype <u16>`, `vlan <1..4094> [pcp <0..7>] [dei <0..1>]`, `qinq <1..4094> [innervlan <1..4094>]`, `mpls <0..1048575> [exp|tc <0..7>] [bos <0..1>] [mplsttl <u8>]`.
- **L3**: `ttl <0..255>`, `dscp <0..63>`, `ecn <0..3>`, `flowlabel <0..1048575>`, `ipid <u16>`, `df`, `mf`, `fragoffset <0..8191>`, `nextheader <u8>`.
- **L4**: `srcport <u16>`, `dstport <u16>`, `transport <tcp|udp>` (default-TCP: `modbus`, `nfs`, `memcached`, `dnp3`, `ethernetip`; default-UDP: `dns`, `sip`, `syslog`, `kerberos`), `seq <u32>`, `acknum <u32>`, `win|window <u16>`, `urgent <u16>`, `mss <u16>`, `wscale <u8>`, `sackperm`, `tsval <u32>`, `tsecr <u32>`, TCP flags (`syn`, `ack`, `fin`, `rst`, `psh`, `urg`, `ece`, `cwr`).
- **Payload & Timing**: `payload "<escaped_utf8>"` OR `hexpayload "<even_hex>"` (mutually exclusive), `wait <u32><ns|us|ms|s|m>`.

**Complete 81-Protocol Zero-Default v2.0.0 Syntax & Port Dictionary**

Every protocol compiles with **zero required sub-keywords**; optional strict-lowercase protocol-scoped modifiers:

- **L2 Switching & Data-Link (8)**:
  - `arp` (`0x0806`): `request|reply, gratuitous|garp, sha|sendermac, spa|senderip, tha|targetmac, tpa|targetip`
  - `vlan` (`0x8100`): `<1..4094>, pcp <0..7>, dei <0..1>`
  - `qinq` (`0x88A8`+`0x8100`): `<1..4094>, innervlan <1..4094>, pcp <0..7>, dei <0..1>`
  - `lldp` (`0x88CC`): `chassisid, portid, ttl <0..255>, sysname, sysdesc`
  - `stp` (LLC `0x424203`): `rstp, rootid "<prio>/<mac>", bridgeid "<prio>/<mac>", portid, cost, maxage, hellotime, forwarddelay, flags`
  - `lacp` (`0x8809`): `actorsys, actorkey, actorport, actorstate, partnersys, partnerkey, partnerport, partnerstate`
  - `eapol` (`0x888E`): `version, [type] eappacket|start|logoff|key, eapcode <1..4>, eapid, eapmethod, identity`
  - `mpls` (`0x8847`): `<0..1048575>, label, exp|tc <0..7>, bos <0..1>, mplsttl`
- **L3 Control, Tunneling, VPN, Routing & FHRP (20)**:
  - `icmp` (IP `1`/`58`): `echorequest|echoreply|destunreach|timeexceeded|redirect, type, code, id, seq, gateway`
  - `ndp` (IPv6 `58`, `ttl=255`): `neighborsolicit|neighboradvert|routersolicit|routeradvert, target, slla, tlla, routerlifetime`
  - `igmp` (IPv4 `2`): `query|report|leave, v1|v2|v3|version <1..3>, group, maxresp`
  - `mld` (IPv6 `58`): `query|report|done, multicastaddr, maxrespdelay`
  - `gre` (IP `47`): `grekey|key, greseq, greproto, checksum`
  - `vxlan` (UDP `4789`): `vni|vnid <0..16777215>`
  - `geneve` (UDP `6081`): `vni|vnid <0..16777215>, optclass, opttype, protocoltype`
  - `ipsec` / `esp` (IP `50`): `spi, seq, iv "<hex>", icv "<hex>", nextheader`
  - `ah` (IP `51`): `spi, seq, icv "<hex>", nextheader`
  - `ikev2` (UDP `500`): `[exchange] sainit|createchildsa|informational, initiatorspi, responderspi, msgid, flags, nextpayload`
  - `wireguard` (UDP `51820`): `[type] initiation|response|cookie|data, sender, receiver, counter`
  - `ospf` (IP `89`): `hello|dbd|lsr|lsu|lsack, routerid, areaid, hellointerval, deadinterval, priority`
  - `bgp` (TCP `179`): `open|update|notification|keepalive, asn, holdtime, bgpid, prefix|nlri "<cidr>", nexthop`
  - `rip` (UDP `520`/`521`): `request|response|reply, prefix <ip>, metric <1..16>, nexthop, tag`
  - `pim` (IP `103`): `hello|joinprune|register, group, source, rp, holdtime, drpriority`
  - `vrrp` (IP `112`, `ttl=255`): `vrid <1..255>, priority <0..255>, advint, vip, version <2|3>`
  - `hsrp` (UDP `1985`/`2029`): `group, priority, state, hellotime <0..255>, holdtime, auth, vip`
  - `bfd` (UDP `3784`): `state <0..3>, diag <0..31>, mydisc, yourdisc, mintx, minrx, mult`
  - `openflow` (TCP `6653`): `[type] hello|echoreq|echorequest|echoreply|featuresreq|featuresreply|packetin|packetout|flowmod, version, xid, dpid, tableid, priority`
- **L4 Transports (3)**:
  - `tcp` (IP `6`, port `80`): `syn, ack, fin, rst, psh, urg, ece, cwr, seq, acknum, win|window, urgent, mss, wscale, sackperm, tsval, tsecr`
  - `udp` (IP `17`, port `80`): `srcport, dstport, payload|hexpayload`
  - `sctp` (IP `132`, CRC32c LE): `[chunk] init|initack|cookieecho|cookieack|data|sack|heartbeat|heartbeatack|shutdown|shutdownack|abort, vtag, tsn, stream, ssn, ppid`
- **L7 SNMP (3)** (`varbind <oid>` + `null` | `nullval` | `string "<s>"` | `int <i32>` | `timeticks <u32>` | `ipval <ip>` | `oidval <oid>` | `counter32 <u32>` | `gauge32 <u32>` | `counter64 <u64>`):
  - `snmp1` (UDP `162`/`161`): `trap|get|getnext|set|response, community, enterprise, oid, agentip, gentrap <0..6>, spectrap, sysuptime, reqid, varbind ...`
  - `snmp2` (UDP `162`/`161`): `trap|inform|get|getnext|getbulk|set|response, community, reqid, nonrepeaters, maxrepetitions, sysuptime, oid, varbind ...`
  - `snmp3` (UDP `162`/`161`): `trap|inform|report|get|getnext|getbulk|set|response, user, engineid "<hex>", engineboots, enginetime, contextname, auth md5|sha|sha256|sha384|sha512 "<pw>", priv des|aes "<pw>", reqid, nonrepeaters, maxrepetitions, sysuptime, oid, varbind ...`
- **L7 Infrastructure, Time, AAA & Telemetry (11)**:
  - `dns` (`53`) / `mdns` (`5353`): `query|response, txid, qname, qtype, rdata, rcode <0..15>, ansttl, transport tcp`
  - `dhcp` (UDP `68/67` v4, `546/547` v6): `discover|offer|request|ack|release|solicit|advertise|reply, xid, ciaddr, yiaddr, siaddr, chaddr, hostname, dnsserver, router, subnetmask, leasetime`
  - `ntp` (UDP `123`): `li <0..3>, vn <1..4>, mode <0..7>, stratum <0..16>, poll, precision, refid, txtimestamp`
  - `ptp` (UDP `319`/`320`): `sync|delayreq|followup|delayresp|announce|msgtype, domain, seqid, clockid`
  - `radius` (UDP `1812`/`1813`): `accessrequest|accessaccept|accessreject|accesschallenge|accountingrequest|accountingresponse|code, id, user, nasip, servicetype, framedip`
  - `tacacs` (TCP `49`): `[type] authen|author|acct, seq, flags, sessionid, user, data`
  - `syslog` (UDP/TCP `514`): `facility <0..23>, severity <0..7>, pri <0..191>, hostname, app, procid, msgid, msg, transport tcp`
  - `netflow` (`2055`) / `ipfix` (`4739`): `domainid, srcip, dstip, srcport, dstport, proto, packets, octets`
  - `sflow` (UDP `6343`): `agentip, subagentid, seq, uptime, samples`
- **L7 Web, Cloud, Security, VoIP & Remote Access (16)**:
  - `http` (TCP `80`): `get|post|put|delete|head|options|patch|method, uri, version, hosthdr, useragent, contenttype, header "<k>" "<v>", status, reason, body`
  - `http2` (TCP `443`): `preface, settings|headers|data|windowupdate|ping|goaway, streamid`
  - `grpc` (TCP `50051`): `service, method, grpcstatus`
  - `websocket` (TCP `80`): `text|binary|ping|pong|close|opcode, finbit <0|1>, maskkey, payload`
  - `tls` (TCP `443`): `clienthello|serverhello|certificate|finished|appdata|alert, recordversion, handshakeversion, sni, ciphersuite, alpn`
  - `quic` (UDP `443`): `initial|zerortt|handshake|retry|short, version, dcid, scid, token, pktnum`
  - `ssh` (TCP `22`): `banner, kexinit, newkeys, msgcode, cookie "<hex>"`
  - `telnet` (TCP `23`): `will [option] <u8>, wont [option] <u8>, do [option] <u8>, dont [option] <u8>, option <u8>, data`
  - `tftp` (UDP `69`): `rrq|wrq|data|ack|err|error, filename, mode, block, errcode, errmsg`
  - `ftp` (TCP `21`): `cmd, arg, code, reply`
  - `whois` (TCP `43`): `query|response, domain, registrar`
  - `sip` (UDP/TCP `5060`): `invite|ack|bye|cancel|register|options|method, uri, status, reason, from, to, callid, cseq, via, contact, contenttype, body, transport tcp`
  - `rtp` (UDP `5004`): `pt <0..127>, seq, timestamp, ssrc, marker <0|1>`
  - `rtsp` (TCP `554`): `options|describe|setup|play|teardown|method, uri, status, cseq, transporthdr, session`
  - `stun` (UDP `3478`): `bindingrequest|bindingresponse|bindingerror, txid, xormappedaddr, software`
  - `ssdp` (UDP `1900`): `msearch|notify, hosthdr, man, mx, st, nt, nts, usn, location`
- **L7 Mail, Identity, Storage, Databases, Caches & Brokers (14)**:
  - `smtp` (TCP `25`): `ehlo|helo|mailfrom|rcptto|quit|cmd, param, code, reply, body`
  - `imap` (TCP `143`): `tag, cmd, arg, status, response`
  - `pop3` (TCP `110`): `cmd, arg, ok|err, response`
  - `kerberos` (UDP/TCP `88`): `asreq|asrep|tgsreq|tgsrep|krberror, realm, cname, sname, etype, transport tcp`
  - `ldap` (TCP `389`): `bindreq|bindres|searchreq|searchentry|searchdone|unbindreq, msgid, basedn, filter, resultcode`
  - `smb` (TCP `445`): `negotiate|sessionsetup|treeconnect|create|treedisconnect|command, status, treeid, sessionid, msgid, share, filename`
  - `nfs` (TCP/UDP `2049`): `compound|proc, vers <2|3|4>, xid, tag, path, transport udp`
  - `redis` (TCP `6379`): `get|set|cmd, key, args, replytype, value`
  - `memcached` (TCP/UDP `11211`): `get|set|cmd, key, value, flags, exptime, opcode, opaque, cas, transport udp`
  - `mysql` (TCP `3306`): `greeting|login|query|ok|err|eof, serverversion, user, db, sql, errcode`
  - `postgres` (TCP `5432`): `startup|query|authok|commandcomplete|readyforquery|errorresponse, user, db, sql`
  - `mqtt` (TCP `1883`): `connect|connack|publish|puback|subscribe|suback|pingreq|pingresp|disconnect|pkttype, clientid, topic, qos <0..2>, retain [0|1], pktid, keepalive, returncode`
  - `coap` (UDP `5683`): `con|non|ack|rst|msgtype, get|post|put|delete|created|changed|notfound|code, msgid, token, uripath, contentformat`
  - `amqp` (TCP `5672`): `protocolheader|connectionstart|channelopen|basicpublish|basicdeliver|heartbeat, channel, exchange, routingkey`
- **L7 Industrial Control Systems & SCADA/OT (6)**:
  - `modbus` (TCP/UDP `502`): `readcoils|readdiscreteinputs|readholdingregisters|readinputregisters|writesinglecoil|writesingleregister|writemultipleregisters|func, txid, protoid, unitid, addr, count, value, isresponse, transport udp`
  - `bacnet` (UDP `47808`): `whois|iam|readproperty|writeproperty, invokeid, objecttype, objectinstance, propertyid, value`
  - `dnp3` (TCP/UDP `20000`, CRC-16): `confirm|read|write|select|operate|directoperate|unsolicitedresponse|func, src, dst, group, variation, crc, transport udp`
  - `s7comm` (TCP `102`): `setupcomm|readvar|writevar|plccontrol|func, rosctr, pduref, area, dbnum, offset, count`
  - `ethernetip` (TCP/UDP `44818`): `nop|listidentity|listservices|listinterfaces|registersession|unregistersession|sendrrdata|sendunitdata|cmd, sessionhandle, status, context, cipservice, cipclass, cipinstance, cipattr, transport udp`
  - `opcua` (TCP `4840`): `msgtype, chunktype, securechannelid, tokenid, seqnum, reqid, endpointurl, nodeid`

**Canonical Compilable v2.0.0 `.fasm` Template, CLI & Rust Library API**

```frameassembly
// Stateful TCP 3-way handshake, HTTP/1.1 health check, and encrypted SNMPv3 USM trap
host client { ip 10.0.0.10 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host server { ip 10.0.0.80 mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

flow demo_flow(c, s) {
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 51234 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460
    c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> s http get uri "/health" hosthdr "api.internal" wait 5ms
    c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" body "{\"ok\":true}" wait 2ms
    s -> c vlan 100 snmp3 trap user "admin" engineid "80001f8880112233" auth sha256 "authpass123" priv aes "privpass123" oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "srv01" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    demo_flow(client, server)
}
```

- **CLI (Default Root Compile + 4 Subcommands `show`, `reverse`, `help`, `version` — No `-o`/`--output` Flags)**:
  - Compile (default) / Preview: `frameassembly demo.fasm [demo.pcap]` | `frameassembly show demo.fasm`
  - Reverse / Info: `frameassembly reverse demo.pcap [demo.fasm]` | `frameassembly help [subcommand]` | `frameassembly version`
  - Inspect & replay: `tshark -r demo.pcap -V` / `sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 demo.pcap` / `suricata -r demo.pcap -k none` / `zeek -C -r demo.pcap`
- **Supported Install Channels**:
  - Cargo & Web: `cargo install frameassembly` | `https://frameassembly.ai.studio/`
  - Bootstrap: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh`
  - Homebrew & Scoop: `brew install SteveWinschel/tap-FrameAssembly/frameassembly` | `scoop bucket add frameassembly https://github.com/SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly && scoop install frameassembly`
  - Debian/Ubuntu, WASM & VS Code: GitHub Releases `*.deb` | `npm install frameassembly-wasm` | `code --install-extension SteveWinschel.frameassembly-vscode`
- **Public Rust API (`frameassembly` v2.0.0)**:
  - `lexer::lex<'a>(input: &'a str) -> Result<Vec<(Token<'a>, Range<usize>)>, CompilerError>`
  - `parser::parse_program<'a>(input_str: &'a str) -> Result<Program<'a>, CompilerError>`
  - `parser::validate_semantics(program: &Program, src: &str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
  - `backend::compile_program(program: &Program) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>`
  - `backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
  - `reverse::{reverse_pcap_reader(reader), reverse_pcap_bytes(bytes), reverse_pcap_file(path)} -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>`
  - `error::CompilerError`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `BackendError`

# Public Rust Library API, 4-Stage RLVR Reward & Compiler Diagnostics (`src/lib.rs`, `src/reverse/mod.rs` & `src/error.rs`)

- `frameassembly::lexer::lex<'a>(input: &'a str) -> Result<Vec<(Token<'a>, Range<usize>)>, CompilerError>` (strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` built-in keywords with zero `_`/`-` and flexible user `Token::Ident`)
- `frameassembly::parser::parse_program<'a>(input_str: &'a str) -> Result<Program<'a>, CompilerError>` (automatically runs `validate_semantics`)
- `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics(program: &Program, src: &str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` (returns `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_ns)`)
- `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
- `frameassembly::reverse::reverse_pcap_reader<R: std::io::Read>(reader: R) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::reverse::reverse_pcap_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::reverse::reverse_pcap_file(path: impl AsRef<std::path::Path>) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::reverse::ReverseOutput { pub fasm: String, pub packet_count: usize, pub host_count: usize }` (emits `host1`, `host2` without `_`, strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` keywords, and direct `compile` invocations with zero `loop` blocks)
- **4-Stage Additive RLVR Compiler & Reverse Oracle Reward ($R \in [0.0, 1.0]$)**: `+0.15` Stage 1 Lex (`0.15`), `+0.25` Stage 2 Parse (`0.40`), `+0.30` Stage 3 Semantics (`0.70`), `+0.30` Stage 4 Wire Compile + `reverse_pcap_bytes` Oracle (`1.00`)
- `frameassembly::error::CompilerError` (`miette::Diagnostic` with self-healing `replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'` hints, `loop` migration hints, and `detect_foreign_fasm`):
  - `CompilerError::LexError { src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::lex_error`)
  - `CompilerError::ParseError { message: String, src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::parse_error`)
  - `CompilerError::SemanticError { message: String, src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::semantic_error`)
  - `CompilerError::BackendError(String)` (`frameassembly::backend_error`)
---

## What Is FrameAssembly?

At first you may think **FrameAssembly** is a programming language for systems development, but ironically it is a tool built specifically for the very people who hate programming -> **Networking & Cybersecurity professionals**.

Have you ever wished you could just describe traffic in a few lines of simple networking keywords, get your own `.pcap`, and do a little SQL injection onto your favourite coworker's machine with the help of `tcpreplay`?

Well, here you have it and it's fun and free to use (even commercially) -> as long as **I'm not responsible for what you do with it** :)

**Compilation works in both directions** -> Compile FrameAssembly `.fasm` code into custom `.pcap` or `.pcapng` captures across **81 protocols**, or reverse captured `.pcap` / `.pcapng` traces back into `.fasm` code for anonymizing, editing, inspecting, and replaying with **`tcpreplay`**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, or **Suricata** / **Zeek**:

```frameassembly
host client   { ip 10.0.0.10 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host firewall { ip 10.0.0.1  mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

flow http_check(c, fw) {
    c -> fw tcp syn srcport 51234 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- fw tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> fw tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> fw http get uri "/healthz" hosthdr "api.example.com" wait 2ms
    c <- fw http status 200 reason "OK" body "ok"
}

compile { http_check(client, firewall) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly show test.fasm
#      Time (ms)   Source -> Destination                    Proto       Bytes  Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1      0.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    TCP         58     51234 -> 80 [SYN] seq=1000 len=0
2      1.000       10.0.0.1 -> 10.0.0.10                    TCP         58     80 -> 51234 [SYN ACK] seq=1000 ack=1001 len=0
3      2.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    TCP         54     51234 -> 80 [ACK] seq=1001 ack=1001 len=0
4      3.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    HTTP        102    51234 -> 80 [ACK PSH] seq=1001 ack=1001 len=48
5      5.000       10.0.0.1 -> 10.0.0.10                    HTTP        94     80 -> 51234 [ACK PSH] seq=1001 ack=1049 len=40

$ frameassembly test.fasm && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 test.pcap
$ frameassembly reverse test.pcap edited.fasm
```

## Network and Security Testing Use Cases

### 1. Simulate Encrypted SNMPv3 Traps & Syslog Alerts (`Checkmk`, `Zabbix`, `PRTG`)
Testing whether **Checkmk** Event Console, **Zabbix**, **PRTG**, **LibreNMS**, **SolarWinds**, or `snmptrapd` actually pages on an encrypted SNMPv3 `authPriv` trap usually means configuring a switch agent, loading vendor MIBs, matching EngineIDs, and pulling a fiber patch cord out of hardware. With FrameAssembly, you generate encrypted SNMPv3 traps (`SHA-256` + `AES-128`), SNMPv1/v2c notifications, `Syslog` events, and `NetFlow` / `IPFIX` / `sFlow` records in seconds:

```frameassembly
host core_sw { ip 10.10.1.2  mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:01 }
host checkmk { ip 10.10.1.50 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:50 }

flow link_down_alert(sw, nms) {
    sw -> nms vlan 100 snmp3 trap user "netops" engineid "80001f8801" engineboots 5 enginetime 3600 auth sha256 "AuthPass123!" priv aes "PrivPass123!" oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.1 int 2 wait 5ms
    sw -> nms vlan 100 syslog facility 16 severity 3 hostname "core-sw-01" app "link" msg "Gi0/1 changed state to down"
}

compile { link_down_alert(core_sw, checkmk) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly snmp_alert.fasm snmp_alert.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 snmp_alert.pcap
```

### 2. Validate Shadow IT, NDR & IDS Detection Rules (`Suricata`, `Zeek`, `Snort`)
Proving that your NDR sensor, DNS sinkhole, or SIEM catches Shadow IT SaaS/AI uploads (unauthorized TLS `sni` or HTTP/3 `quic`), rogue `dhcp` servers, or unauthorized `mdns` / `ssdp` discovery normally means hunting down noisy third-party `.pcap` captures. FrameAssembly builds exact detection-test captures in a few lines of `.fasm` code:

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 10.40.5.25 mac 00:50:56:40:05:25 }
host rogue_iot   { ip 10.40.5.99 mac 00:50:56:40:05:99 }
host sec_gateway { ip 10.40.5.1  mac 00:1c:73:40:05:01 }
host mdns_group  { ip 224.0.0.251 }

flow shadow_it_and_ndr_audit(ws, iot, gw, mcast) {
    ws  -> gw    dns query txid 0x4401 qname "shadow-ai-upload.example.net" qtype "a" wait 1ms
    ws  <- gw    dns response txid 0x4401 qname "shadow-ai-upload.example.net" qtype "a" rcode 5 wait 2ms
    ws  -> gw    tcp syn srcport 53443 dstport 443 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws  <- gw    tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws  -> gw    tcp ack wait 1ms
    ws  -> gw    tls clienthello sni "shadow-ai-upload.example.net" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    ws  <- gw    tls alert payload "BLOCKED_BY_SNI_POLICY" wait 2ms
    ws  -> gw    quic initial version 1 dcid "a1b2c3d4" scid "e5f60708" pktnum 1 payload "QUIC_SHADOW_SAAS" wait 2ms
    iot -> mcast mdns query qname "_airplay._tcp.local" qtype "ptr" wait 2ms
    iot -> gw    ssdp msearch st "ssdp:all"
}

compile { shadow_it_and_ndr_audit(workstation, rogue_iot, sec_gateway, mdns_group) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly ids_test.fasm ids_test.pcap && suricata -r ids_test.pcap -k none
```

### 3. Test Stateful Firewalls, VLAN Trunks & OT Rules Without Lab VMs
Sending a single spoofed packet at a stateful firewall (`nftables` / `iptables`, **Palo Alto**, **FortiGate**, **CheckPoint**) won't test your application rules because the firewall drops mid-stream data without a completed 3-way TCP handshake. FrameAssembly tracks TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` numbers and swaps reply ports on `<-` automatically, so you can verify DMZ rules, 802.1Q `vlan` tags, and industrial OT (`modbus`, `dnp3`, `s7comm`, `opcua`) policies before a maintenance window:

```frameassembly
host eng_ws  { ip 192.168.20.25  mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host dmz_srv { ip 203.0.113.10   mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }
host ot_plc  { ip 192.168.110.50 mac 00:0e:8c:aa:bb:01 }

flow acl_audit(c, srv, plc) {
    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 443 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- srv vlan 20 tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> srv vlan 20 tls clienthello sni "portal.example.com" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 2ms

    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp syn srcport 52001 dstport 22 win 64240 wait 1ms
    c <- srv vlan 20 tcp rst ack wait 1ms

    c -> plc vlan 110 tcp syn srcport 52002 dstport 502 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- plc vlan 110 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> plc vlan 110 tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> plc vlan 110 modbus readholdingregisters txid 1 unitid 1 addr 0 count 2
}

compile { acl_audit(eng_ws, dmz_srv, ot_plc) }
```

```console
# Replay into a SPAN/TAP sensor port (for inline firewalls, split client/server NICs via tcpprep + tcpreplay -i eth0 -I eth1)
$ frameassembly acl_test.fasm acl_test.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 acl_test.pcap
```

### 4. Anonymize & Edit Production `.pcap` Captures (`frameassembly reverse`)
When you need to attach a production capture to a vendor TAC ticket without leaking internal subnets or customer hostnames—or turn a live `tcpdump` capture into a Git-tracked regression test—run `frameassembly reverse`. Swap the `host` IPs, MACs, VLAN tags, or TLS `sni` names in `.fasm` code, delete background chatter, and recompile—FrameAssembly recalculates all L3/L4 checksums and TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` numbers automatically:

```console
$ frameassembly reverse customer_incident.pcap sanitized_ticket.fasm
```

```frameassembly
host host1 { ip 192.0.2.10 mac 00:11:22:33:44:01 }
host host2 { ip 198.51.100.20 mac 00:11:22:33:44:02 }

compile {
    host1 -> host2 vlan 100 tcp syn srcport 54321 dstport 443 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    host1 <- host2 vlan 100 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    host1 -> host2 vlan 100 tcp ack wait 1ms
    host1 -> host2 vlan 100 tls clienthello sni "sanitized-app.example.com" ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    host1 <- host2 vlan 100 tcp rst ack
}
```

```console
$ frameassembly sanitized_ticket.fasm sanitized_ticket.pcap
```

## How FrameAssembly Works

Every `.fasm` file uses up to three building blocks, with strictly lowercase keywords (`host`, `flow`, `compile`, `echorequest`, `clienthello`) and zero underscores or hyphens on built-in keywords:

1. **`host` — Declare Endpoints Once:** Bind names to `ip` (IPv4 or IPv6) and `mac` addresses—or declare MAC-only switches (`host sw1 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }`) for Layer 2 switching protocols (`lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `mpls`, `arp`).
2. **`flow` — Describe Exchanges Directionally:** Write packets top-to-bottom using `->` and `<-` arrows, optional `vlan` / `qinq` / `mpls` headers, Layer 2–7 protocol keywords, and `wait` deltas (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`).
3. **`compile` — Emit Standard Captures:** Call reusable flows across different host pairs, or write packet statements directly inside `compile { ... }` without a `flow` block.

```frameassembly
host sw1 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }
host sw2 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:02 }

compile {
    sw1 -> sw2 lldp chassisid "00:1c:73:00:00:01" portid "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "leaf-01" wait 2ms
    sw1 <- sw2 stp rstp rootid "4096/00:1c:73:00:00:02" bridgeid "4096/00:1c:73:00:00:02" portid 0x8001 cost 0 flags 0x3c
}
```

Under the hood, the compiler handles the packet plumbing automatically:

* **Stateful TCP Tracking:** Advances `SEQ` and `ACK` numbers from payload byte lengths and `SYN`/`FIN` flags, while flipping ports, IPs, and MAC addresses on `<-` replies.
* **Wire-Valid Framing & Checksums:** Computes Ethernet/802.1Q framing, IPv4/IPv6 lengths, and L3/L4/L7 checksums out of the box.
* **PCAP-to-`.fasm` Decompilation:** Turns existing `.pcap` and `.pcapng` captures into `.fasm` code so you can anonymize IPs or edit headers and recompile. Encrypted payloads (such as SNMPv3 `authPriv`, TLS application data, SSH, or IPsec `ESP`) stay intact as `tcp` or `udp` statements with `payload` / `hexpayload` so recompiled captures preserve exact wire bytes.
* **Git-Friendly:** Turns binary `.pcap` blobs into `.fasm` code files that you can review with `git diff` in CI/CD and regression suites.

## Why FrameAssembly Instead of Scapy or Lab VMs?

| Capability | FrameAssembly (`.fasm`) | Scapy (Python) | Full Lab VMs / GNS3 | Downloaded `.pcap` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Setup Overhead** | Single CLI binary or VS Code / Web Studio | Python + `venv` + packages | Hypervisor + OS images | None |
| **Admin Rights to Build PCAP** | Never required | Not for offline `wrpcap` | Admin / hypervisor access | Not required |
| **TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` Math** | Automatic on `->` / `<-` | Manual state in Python | Real OS TCP stack | Fixed static stream |
| **Anonymize & Edit `.pcap`s** | `frameassembly reverse` (`.pcap` <-> `.fasm`) | Custom Python parsing & checksum scripts | Cannot import `.pcap` into live state | Hex editor / `tcprewrite` only |
| **Version Control** | L2–L7 `.fasm` code | Imperative scripts | Multi-GB disk images | Binary blobs |
| **Capture Hygiene** | Zero background chatter | Isolated, high boilerplate | ARP / mDNS / OS noise | Foreign IPs & noise |

FrameAssembly is built to work **alongside** **`tcpreplay`**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, **Suricata**, and **Zeek**—not replace them. Instead of maintaining Python environments or booting multi-VM labs just to synthesize 10 packets—or struggling to sanitize a customer capture—you compile or reverse `.fasm` code in milliseconds and feed the resulting `.pcap` straight into your existing replay and analysis tools.

## Installation

### Try in Browser (No Install Required)
Open the official website and browser playground at [**frameassembly.ai.studio**](https://frameassembly.ai.studio/) to compile `.fasm` code <-> `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures and inspect packet ladders directly in your browser.

### VS Code Packet Studio Extension
Install the interactive VS Code Packet Studio (live diagnostics, 1-click Quick Fixes, protocol autocomplete, live Packet Ladder preview, `.fasm` -> `.pcap` compilation, and right-click `.pcap` -> `.fasm` decompilation):
```bash
code --install-extension SteveWinschel.frameassembly-vscode
```

### Cargo (Recommended CLI Install — Rust 1.85+)
```bash
cargo install frameassembly
```

### Linux & macOS Shell Installer (Includes Shell Tab Completion)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh
```

### Homebrew (macOS & Linux) & Scoop (Windows)
```bash
# Homebrew
brew install SteveWinschel/tap-FrameAssembly/frameassembly

# Scoop (Windows)
scoop bucket add frameassembly https://github.com/SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly && scoop install frameassembly
```

### Debian / Ubuntu (`.deb`) & Prebuilt Release Binaries
Download `.deb` packages, standalone archives for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and `SHA-256` checksums from [**GitHub Releases**](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/releases).

### WebAssembly Package (`npm`)
For browser tools, custom IDEs, and Node/bundler integrations:
```bash
npm install frameassembly-wasm
```

### Quick CLI Usage
```bash
# Inspect packet timing, flags, sequence numbers, and byte lengths in the terminal
frameassembly show demo.fasm

# Compile .fasm code to .pcap (writes demo.pcap by default, or pass an output path)
frameassembly demo.fasm
frameassembly demo.fasm custom.pcap

# Decompile an existing .pcap or .pcapng into .fasm code (writes trace.fasm by default, or pass an output path)
frameassembly reverse trace.pcap
frameassembly reverse trace.pcap sanitized.fasm

# Print CLI version and command help
frameassembly version
frameassembly help
```

## Supported Protocols and Documentation

FrameAssembly natively compiles and decompiles **81 protocols across Layers 2–7**. Start with the guides below or jump straight into the protocol reference for your layer:

* [**Getting Started (`docs/getting_started.md`)**](docs/getting_started.md) — Core `.fasm` syntax, `host` / `flow` / `compile` mechanics, AI copy-paste prompt, reverse PCAP conversion, and your first capture.
* [**Real-World Use Cases (`docs/use_cases.md`)**](docs/use_cases.md) — Copy-paste recipes for Checkmk/Zabbix SNMPv3 traps, Shadow IT & NDR detection, firewall/VLAN verification, and PCAP anonymization.
* [**Topologies & Dual-Stack (`docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`)**](docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md) — Multi-hop gateways, VLAN/QinQ trunks, and IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack flows.
* [**`.fasm` Media Type Specification (`docs/fasm-specification.md`)**](docs/fasm-specification.md) — Formal `text/vnd.frameassembly` format rules and `.fasm` extension disambiguation.
* [**Compiler Architecture (`docs/for_nerds.md`)**](docs/for_nerds.md) — Lexing, parsing, semantic validation, and binary emission internals for curious engineers.

### Layer 2–7 Protocol Reference

* [**Layer 2 — Switching & Data Link (`docs/l2_protocols.md`)**](docs/l2_protocols.md) — Ethernet II, IEEE 802.1Q `vlan`, 802.1ad `qinq`, `arp`, `stp` / `rstp`, `lldp`, `lacp`, `mpls`, and `eapol` (802.1X).
* [**Layer 3 — Network, Routing & Tunnels (`docs/l3_protocols.md`)**](docs/l3_protocols.md) — `IPv4`, `IPv6`, `icmp`, `ndp`, `igmp`, `mld`, `gre`, `ipsec` (`esp` / `ah`), `ikev2`, `vxlan`, `geneve`, `ospf`, `bgp`, `rip`, `pim`, `vrrp`, `hsrp`, `bfd`, `openflow`, and `wireguard`.
* [**Layer 4 — Transports (`docs/l4_transports.md`)**](docs/l4_transports.md) — Stateful `tcp` (flags, window, `mss`, options, automatic `SEQ`/`ACK`), `udp`, and `sctp`.
* [**Layer 7 — SNMPv1 / v2c / v3 (`docs/l7_snmp.md`)**](docs/l7_snmp.md) — `get`, `getnext`, `getbulk`, `set`, `response`, `trap`, `inform`, and encrypted `snmp3` USM (`SHA-256` auth + `AES-128` priv).
* [**Layer 7 — Infrastructure & Telemetry (`docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`)**](docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md) — `dns`, `mdns`, `dhcp` / `DHCPv6`, `ntp`, `ptp`, `radius`, `tacacs`, `syslog`, `netflow`, `ipfix`, and `sflow`.
* [**Layer 7 — Web, Cloud, Security & VoIP (`docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`)**](docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md) — `http`, `http2`, `grpc`, `websocket`, `tls` (`clienthello`, `sni`, `alpn`, `alert`), `quic`, `ssh`, `telnet`, `ftp`, `tftp`, `whois`, `sip`, `rtp`, `rtsp`, `stun`, and `ssdp`.
* [**Layer 7 — Mail, Auth, Storage, Databases & Brokers (`docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`)**](docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md) — `smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `kerberos`, `ldap`, `smb`, `nfs`, `postgres`, `mysql`, `redis`, `memcached`, `mqtt`, `coap`, and `amqp`.
* [**Layer 7 — Industrial OT & ICS (`docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`)**](docs/l7_industrial_ot.md) — `modbus`, `dnp3`, `s7comm`, `opcua`, `bacnet`, and `ethernetip`.

# Repository Agent Guide (`AGENTS.md`)

# AGENTS.md — FrameAssembly AI Agent & LLM Onboarding Guide

**FrameAssembly** (`frameassembly` v2.0.0, official website & interactive browser playground: [`https://frameassembly.ai.studio/`](https://frameassembly.ai.studio/), repository: [`https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly`](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly)) is a Rust 2024 Domain-Specific Language (DSL) and optimizing compiler that compiles declarative `.fasm` network traffic specifications into deterministic, nanosecond-precision `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet captures—and decompiles `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures back into canonical `.fasm` code—across **81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols** (`2,611` verified `.fasm` corpus scenarios).

---

## 1. Quick Build, Test & Verification Commands

```bash
# Cross-platform bootstrap install (prebuilt release binary fast-path or curl + C linker + rustup >= 1.85 + cargo install)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh

# Build compiler and CLI binary
cargo build --release

# Run all unit, integration, and corpus verification tests
cargo test

# Run the corpus verification suite (validates all 2,611 examples/**/*.fasm headers, AST parsing & PCAP output)
cargo test --test corpus_verification_tests

# Compile a single .fasm specification to a .pcap file (default root command; optional 2nd positional path defaults to <input_stem>.pcap)
cargo run -- demo.fasm output.pcap

# Show the terminal packet ladder for a .fasm file without writing a .pcap file
cargo run -- show demo.fasm

# Decompile a .pcap / .pcapng capture into canonical .fasm code (optional 2nd positional path defaults to <input_stem>.fasm)
cargo run -- reverse output.pcap reversed.fasm

# Display CLI usage or active compiler version (default root compile + 4 subcommands: show, reverse, help, version — no -o/--output flags)
cargo run -- help
cargo run -- version
```

---

## 2. Unified `<layer>/<protocol>` Repository Architecture

FrameAssembly enforces strict structural symmetry across `src/`, `examples/`, and `docs/`:

- **`src/lexer/mod.rs`**: Zero-copy `logos 0.14.4` strict-lowercase tokenizer defining `Token<'a>` for all 81 protocols, L2–L7 modifiers, SNMPv3 USM parameters, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), flexible user `Token::Ident` (`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*`), IPv4/IPv6, MAC, and OID literals (zero `_` or `-` in built-in keywords, no `ignore(ascii_case)`, no `Token::Loop`).
- **`src/ast/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Strongly-typed AST node and `*Spec` definitions (`RunStatement::{Invocation, Frame}`). Every AST type includes a strict-lowercase v2.0.0 `/// Syntax mapping: \`...\`` docstring binding the Rust type to its `.fasm` grammar.
- **`src/parser/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Two-phase `winnow 1.0.5` token-slice (`Stream<'i, 'a>`) combinator parsers (protocol-first `whois` disambiguation + 3-tier field dispatch), self-healing diagnostics (`replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'` and `loop` removal guidance), and semantic validator (`validate_semantics(&program, &source)` in `src/parser/validation.rs`).
- **`src/builders/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Zero-heap wire payload encoders and `src/builders/l7/snmp/` (`builder.rs`, `crypto.rs`) for RFC 1157 / 3416 / 3414 / 3826 / 7860 BER and USM encryption.
- **`src/backend/mod.rs` & `src/packet.rs` & `src/pcap.rs`**: 4-tuple TCP sequence/acknowledgment progression, bidirectional port inheritance across `->` and `<-`, multicast MAC derivation (RFC 2464 `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` and RFC 1112 `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`), and `pcap-file 2.0.0` PCAPNG serialization.
- **`src/reverse/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Five-stage PCAP/PCAPNG-to-`.fasm` decompiler (`reverse_pcap_reader`, `reverse_pcap_bytes`, `reverse_pcap_file`) with `container.rs`, `topology.rs`, `oracle.rs`, `shadow_emit.rs`, `src/reverse/l3/{ip,ipv6,icmpv6}.rs` alongside the 20 L3 protocol dissectors, and `src/reverse/l7/{snmp1,snmp2,snmp3}.rs` across all 50 L7 protocol dissectors (81 per-protocol dissectors total mirroring `src/ast/`, `src/parser/`, and `src/builders/` 1-to-1, emitting `host1`, `host2` without `_`, strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` keywords, and direct `compile` invocations with zero `loop` blocks).
- **`examples/{l2,l3,l4,l7,topologies}/`**: Verified v2.0.0 strict-lowercase `.fasm` corpus (`2,611` files) organized by `<layer>/<protocol>/<protocol>_<scenario>.fasm`.
- **`docs/*.md`**: 13 canonical Markdown guides (human-first getting started, use-case cookbook, 9 layer/topology references, `.fasm` media type specification, and `for_nerds.md` for compiler/LLM internals):
  - [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) — Step-by-step beginner guide: `.fasm` anatomy, defaults vs. overrides, automatic TCP `seq`/`acknum` and reply ports, cross-layer tags, compiler error messages, AI prompt helper, and pairing with Wireshark/`tshark` and `tcpreplay`.
  - [`docs/use_cases.md`](docs/use_cases.md) — Practical cookbook: SNMPv1/v2c/v3 traps & polls, Shadow IT detection QA, firewall ACL testing, VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/QoS verification, IDS/IPS & telemetry validation, OT/SCADA dissectors, and `.pcap` reversal.
  - [`docs/l2_protocols.md`](docs/l2_protocols.md) — Layer 2 switching & data-link protocols (`arp`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, `mpls`).
  - [`docs/l3_protocols.md`](docs/l3_protocols.md) — Layer 3 control, tunneling, VPN, and routing protocols (`icmp`, `ndp`, `igmp`, `mld`, `gre`, `vxlan`, `geneve`, `ipsec`, `esp`, `ah`, `ikev2`, `wireguard`, `ospf`, `bgp`, `rip`, `vrrp`, `hsrp`, `pim`, `bfd`, `openflow`).
  - [`docs/l4_transports.md`](docs/l4_transports.md) — Layer 4 transports (`tcp`, `udp`, `sctp`), 4-tuple state tracking, RFC 7323 TCP options, and SCTP multi-chunk signaling.
  - [`docs/l7_snmp.md`](docs/l7_snmp.md) — Layer 7 `snmp1`, `snmp2`, and `snmp3` USM authentication (`md5`/`sha`/`sha256`/`sha384`/`sha512`), encryption (`des`/`aes`), and all 9 ASN.1 SMI `varbind` types.
  - [`docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`](docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md) — Layer 7 infrastructure, time, AAA, and flow telemetry (`dns`, `mdns`, `dhcp`, `ntp`, `ptp`, `radius`, `tacacs`, `syslog`, `netflow`, `ipfix`, `sflow`).
  - [`docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`](docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md) — Layer 7 web, cloud-native, transport security, VoIP, and remote access (`http`, `http2`, `grpc`, `websocket`, `tls`, `quic`, `tftp`, `ftp`, `ssh`, `telnet`, `whois`, `sip`, `rtp`, `rtsp`, `stun`, `ssdp`).
  - [`docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`](docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md) — Layer 7 mail, directory, storage, databases, caches, and message brokers (`smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `kerberos`, `ldap`, `smb`, `nfs`, `redis`, `memcached`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `mqtt`, `coap`, `amqp`).
  - [`docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`](docs/l7_industrial_ot.md) — Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT (`modbus`, `bacnet`, `dnp3`, `s7comm`, `ethernetip`, `opcua`).
  - [`docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`](docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md) — Multi-host enterprise, data center EVPN-VXLAN, and campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC topologies.
  - [`docs/fasm-specification.md`](docs/fasm-specification.md) — Canonical RFC 6838 specification for the FrameAssembly `.fasm` file format (`text/vnd.frameassembly`), UTF-8 encoding, lexical magic rules, and `.fasm` extension disambiguation.
  - [`docs/for_nerds.md`](docs/for_nerds.md) — Six-stage zero-copy Rust compiler architecture, public Rust library API (`parse_program`, `compile_program`, `generate_pcap`, `reverse_pcap_bytes`), formal grammars (`EBNF`/`GBNF`/`Lark`), constrained decoding, and `examples/` SFT/RLVR corpus conventions.
- **Formal Grammars, Shell Completions, Packaging & `.fasm` Standards Registration (`contrib/`)**:
  - [`grammar.ebnf`](grammar.ebnf): Formal ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF grammar (strict-lowercase v2.0.0).
  - [`frameassembly.gbnf`](frameassembly.gbnf): `llama.cpp` & MLC `XGrammar` GBNF grammar for constrained decoding (`--grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf`).
  - [`frameassembly.lark`](frameassembly.lark): Earley/LALR Lark grammar for `vLLM`, `Outlines`, `Guidance`, `XGrammar`, and `llguidance`.
  - [`contrib/completions/`](contrib/completions/README.md): Shell Tab-completion scripts for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell.
  - [`contrib/packaging/`](contrib/packaging/README.md): Supported distribution manifests across Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`, Homebrew & Windows Scoop (`SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly`), NPM (`frameassembly-wasm`), and VS Code Marketplace (`frameassembly-vscode`).
  - [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md): IANA RFC 6838 Vendor Tree registration (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) & Wikidata property mappings (`P31`, `P1195`, `P1163`, `P973`).
  - [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml): Freedesktop.org `shared-mime-info` XML database definition (`*.fasm` glob + lexer-derived `<magic>` rules).
  - [`contrib/linguist/`](contrib/linguist/README.md): GitHub Linguist `languages.yml`, `heuristics.yml` regex disambiguation, and verified `.fasm` samples.
- **AI Routing Maps & Metadata**:
  - [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) & [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](.github/copilot-instructions.md): Agent & IDE instructions.
  - [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) & [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): Concise index map and single-fetch full context bundle.
  - [`context7.json`](context7.json), [`codemeta.json`](codemeta.json) & [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff): Structured AI/SEO and academic citation metadata.

---

## 3. Core FrameAssembly v2.0.0 DSL Rules & Invariants

1. **Program Structure, Strict-Lowercase Keywords & Flexible User Identifiers**:
   - Every `.fasm` file declares `host <id> { [ip <ip>] [mac <mac>] }` (at least one of `ip` or `mac` required; MAC-only endpoints valid for the 8 pure L2 protocols `arp`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, `mpls`), `flow <id>(<params>) { <statements> }`, and exactly one `compile { <invocations_or_frames> }` block (`loop` was removed in v2.0.0; `compile` supports flow invocations and inline frame statements).
   - **Strict-Lowercase Built-In Keywords (`[a-z0-9]+`)**: Every built-in keyword, protocol, modifier, and time unit (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) is **strictly lowercase alphanumeric with zero `_` and zero `-`** (no `ignore(ascii_case)`: `echorequest`, `innervlan`, `clienthello`, `hosthdr`, `transporthdr`, `sackperm`, `agentip`, `hellotime`, `whois`, `pkttype`, `read`, `write`, `nop`, `error`, `shutdownack`, `readholdingregisters`, etc.), backed by self-healing compiler diagnostics (`replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'`).
   - **Flexible User Identifiers**: User-defined `host`, `flow`, and parameter names match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*` (allowing uppercase, `_`, and internal `-` such as `fw-dmz-01` or `core_sw`, stopping cleanly before `->`). Reverse PCAP decompilation (`frameassembly reverse`) emits `host1`, `host2` without `_`, strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` tokens, and direct flow invocations in `compile` with zero `loop` blocks.
2. **Polymorphic Dual-Stack Flows**: A `flow` works identically over IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs. Mixing IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same statement is a semantic error.
3. **Zero-Keyword RFC Defaults**: Every one of the 81 protocols compiles with zero mandatory sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers and ports) and supports explicit field overrides.
4. **1 Statement = 1 Frame & Shared 4-Tuple State**: Each statement emits 1 frame. TCP-based L7 statements emit a `psh ack` frame on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple sequence/ack counters with raw `tcp` statements on the same connection.
5. **Branding, `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) Disambiguation, Supported Release Channels & Confidentiality**:
   - Always write the project name as one CamelCase word: `FrameAssembly` (or lowercase `frameassembly` strictly for the crate name, CLI binary, URLs, and code identifiers); never split the name into two words, which collides with CAD queries.
   - Maintain clear, factual disambiguation separating FrameAssembly `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) network packet specifications from unregistered x86 Flat Assembler and SymbiFlow/F4PGA FPGA FASM files.
   - Position FrameAssembly as the upstream "Packets as Code" companion compiler to `Wireshark`, `tshark`, `tcpreplay`, `Suricata`, and `Zeek` (comparing only against packet-crafting generators: `Scapy`, `text2pcap`, `Ostinato`), and describe its architecture accurately ("rootless", "offline", "deterministic", "no `libpcap` or raw sockets required") without claiming zero external crate dependencies.
   - **Supported Release Channels Only**: GitHub Releases + Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`, Crates.io (`frameassembly`), NPM (`frameassembly-wasm`), VS Code Marketplace (`frameassembly-vscode`), and `SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly` (`Homebrew` & `Scoop`)—do not reference or add workflows for any other third-party package or extension registries.
   - **Private User Context Confidentiality**: Never include private background context shared by the user in prompts (such as employer names or employment/apprenticeship status) anywhere in code, comments, examples, documentation, or metadata.
6. **Corpus, AI Discovery & Documentation Hygiene**:
   - **Audience Architecture, Natural Voice & Calling `.fasm` Code (Zero Developer Jargon, Zero AI Parroting & Zero Prompt Leaking)**: (1) `llms.txt` is optimized for search engines of AIs and `llms-full.txt` is optimized for pre-training and prompting of AIs; (2) `docs/*.md` are written for networking and cybersecurity professionals in a natural, direct human voice with practical tool examples (`Checkmk`, `Zabbix`, `Wireshark`, `Suricata`, `tcpreplay`); (3) READMEs (`README.md`, `frameassembly-vscode/README.md`, `frameassembly-wasm/README.md`) are tailored to their target audiences, with root `README.md` kept minimalistic—interesting and informative without being overwhelming—focused on the problems solved (preventing manual device/daemon configuration work, avoiding manual fault triggering on hardware, skipping lab VM setup, avoiding manual checksum/TCP sequence math), use cases (pentesting, testing firewalls, simulating SNMP traps, testing monitoring or cybersecurity solutions), and advantages over other solutions. Never spam filler AI adjectives (`"readable"`, `"clean"`, `"editable"`, `"canonical"`, `"repeatable"`), never parrot repetitive slogans across paragraphs (`"no root"`, `"without sudo, libpcap, or raw sockets"`, `"unprivileged user space"`, `"no programming experience required"`), never use compiler/PL jargon (`"DSL"`, `"Domain-Specific Language"`, `"declarative"`, `"polymorphic"`, `"deterministic"`) in `README.md` or `docs/*.md` (except `docs/for_nerds.md`), and never leak or quote informal prompt phrasing into documentation. Always call `.fasm` **code** (`Packets as Code`), never `"plain text"`.
   - Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` must start with `// PROMPT: ...` on line 1, `// TOKENS: ...` on line 2 (matching real strict-lowercase `src/lexer/mod.rs` tokens), and include `// INSTRUCTION: ...` before every `host`, `flow`, and `compile` block (`avg_line_length <= 85`, `max_line_length <= 200`, `words >= 50`). Human-facing docs (`README.md` and `docs/*.md` except `docs/for_nerds.md`) must never include `// PROMPT:`, `// TOKENS:`, or `// INSTRUCTION:` metadata comments.
   - **Canonical v2.0.0 Syntax Only (Anti-Hallucination Guardrail)**:
     - Never use uppercase built-in keywords (`HOST`, `TCP`, `WAIT`), underscores/hyphens in keywords (`echo_request`, `inner_vlan`, `host_hdr`, `sack_perm`), or `=`, colons, commas, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, or `mask` in `host` blocks (only `host <id> { [ip <ip>] [mac <mac>] }`).
     - Never declare parameterless `flow <id> { ... }` or use `from`, `to`, `reverse`, `send`, standalone `wait` lines, or `+5ms` / `[+delay]` prefixes (always `flow <id>(<params>) { <a> -> <b> <proto> ... [wait <int><ns|us|ms|s|m>] }`).
     - Never use `sport`, `dport`, `ack <n>`, `flags [...]`, `hop_limit`, `http ... host`, or `rtsp ... transport` (always `srcport`, `dstport`, `acknum <n>`, bare flag tokens `syn ack`, `ttl`, `hosthdr`, and `transporthdr`).
     - Never write `loop`, bare `compile`, argumentless flow calls inside `compile { <flow>(<hosts>) }`, a `compile` CLI subcommand, or legacy `-o` / `--output` CLI flags (compiling is the default root command `frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]`, alongside the 4 subcommands `show`, `reverse`, `help`, and `version`).
   - **Six-Way Grammar, Lexer, IDE, WASM & Docs Lockstep**: Every strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` keyword in `src/lexer/mod.rs`, `grammar.ebnf`, `frameassembly.gbnf`, `frameassembly.lark`, and `frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json` must be wired into `src/parser/` (with protocol-first `whois` disambiguation and 3-tier protocol-scoped field dispatch so `cut_err` or 0-arg flags never shadow other protocols) and included in `parse_spanned_ident`. Whenever lexer tokens or supported protocols change, synchronize `frameassembly-wasm`, `README.md`, `src/lib.rs`, `docs/fasm-specification.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`, and `contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`.
   - **100% Compilable Documentation & Examples**: Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` (`2,611` files) and `contrib/linguist/samples/` and every ````frameassembly` / ````fasm` code block in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `docs/*.md`, `contrib/**/*.md`, `src/**/*.rs`, and `.agents/skills/**/*.md` must compile with zero errors under v2.0.0 strict-lowercase syntax.
   - **Rustdoc & `docs.rs` SEO Hygiene**: Every `src/**/*.rs` file must start with `//!` (`< 50 KB` per file, `>= 50` words). Never place outer `///` comments on `pub mod` declarations that have inner `//!` docs. Keep internal parser submodules `pub(crate) mod` so `docs.rs` never generates empty module pages, use `#[doc(inline)]` on layer re-exports, and annotate all 81 AST `*Spec` structs with strict-lowercase `/// Syntax mapping:` and `#[doc(alias = "...")]`.
   - Never write literal NUL bytes (`0x00`) into any `.md` or `.txt` file.
   - Keep AI-critical Rust and corpus files (`src/**/*.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `examples/**/*.fasm`) strictly `< 50 KB` (`50,000` bytes) (human-facing `README.md` and `docs/*.md` have no `< 50 KB` cap), and maintain zero broken links or orphan `.md` files in `docs/`.
   - Never bump `version` in `Cargo.toml` or run `git commit`, `git push`, or `git tag` unless explicitly instructed by the user.

---

## 4. Antigravity & AI Agent Customization Routing Tables

### 4.1 Workspace Rules (`.agents/rules/*.md` — 15 Rules: `4` `always_on` + `11` `glob`-Scoped)

| Rule File | Trigger Mode | Scope / Globs & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`.agents/rules/frameassembly-dsl.md`](.agents/rules/frameassembly-dsl.md) | `always_on` | Canonical v2.0.0 strict-lowercase `.fasm` grammar, 6-stage forward compiler + reverse PCAP decompiler invariants, 81-protocol rules, confidentiality, and anti-hallucination guardrails |
| [`.agents/rules/versioning_and_git.md`](.agents/rules/versioning_and_git.md) | `always_on` | Enforces 4-way ecosystem version synchronization across supported release channels on explicit request and prohibits unrequested version bumps or `git commit`/`push`/`tag` |
| [`.agents/rules/temporary_files.md`](.agents/rules/temporary_files.md) | `always_on` | Workspace `temp/` directory and thread-safe RAII cleanup guards for scratch packet captures |
