# Layer 7 — Mail, Identity, Storage, Databases & Message Brokers

[**Use Cases**](#enterprise-and-secops-testing-use-cases) • [**Mail (`smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`)**](#mail-protocols-smtp-imap-pop3) • [**Identity (`kerberos`, `ldap`)**](#identity-and-directory-protocols-kerberos-ldap) • [**Storage (`smb`, `nfs`)**](#network-file-storage-smb-nfs) • [**Databases & Caches**](#databases-and-caches-postgres-mysql-redis-memcached) • [**Brokers (`mqtt`, `coap`, `amqp`)**](#message-brokers-and-iot-queues-mqtt-coap-amqp) • [**Docs Hub**](../README.md)

Testing enterprise firewall rules, DLP policies, or IDS signatures for Active Directory, file shares, databases, and mail gateways usually involves an absurd amount of collateral damage. Nobody wants to babysit a 24 GB Windows Server Domain Controller VM just to generate one Kerberos `TGS-REQ`, get their lab IP blacklisted on Spamhaus testing an `smtp` attachment rule, or hand-encode ASN.1 DER and UTF-16LE byte offsets in Python.

And if you just want to replay a fake `SELECT password_hash FROM users` or an `ADMIN$` share mount across a SPAN port with `tcpreplay` to see whether the SOC is actually looking at the dashboard -> FrameAssembly compiles all **14 enterprise Layer 7 protocols** into `.pcap` / `.pcapng` files in milliseconds without needing any server infrastructure (as usual, what you replay onto your coworker's segment is between you and HR) :)

## Enterprise and SecOps Testing Use Cases

### 1. Test Active Directory & Lateral Movement Detections Without a Domain Controller (`kerberos`, `ldap`, `smb`)
Validating **Suricata**, **Zeek**, or NDR rules for Kerberos pre-authentication failures, RC4-HMAC (`etype 23`) Kerberoasting, LDAP SPN enumeration, or SMB2 `ADMIN$` lateral movement normally requires spinning up an entire Windows lab forest. FrameAssembly encodes the ASN.1 DER/BER envelopes, NetBIOS framing, 64-byte `\xFESMB` headers, and UTF-16LE UNC paths directly from a few lines of `.fasm` code:

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 10.20.5.101 mac 00:50:56:20:05:65 }
host dc_01       { ip 10.20.1.10  mac 00:50:56:20:01:0a }
host file_srv    { ip 10.20.1.50  mac 00:50:56:20:01:32 }

flow ad_lateral_movement(ws, dc, fs) {
    // Kerberos pre-auth failure followed by an RC4-HMAC (etype 23) Kerberoast TGS request
    ws -> dc kerberos asreq realm "CORP.LOCAL" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.LOCAL" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc kerberos krberror realm "CORP.LOCAL" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.LOCAL" wait 2ms
    ws -> dc kerberos tgsreq realm "CORP.LOCAL" cname "jdoe" sname "mssqlsvc/sql01.corp.local" etype 23 wait 2ms
    ws <- dc kerberos tgsrep realm "CORP.LOCAL" cname "jdoe" sname "mssqlsvc/sql01.corp.local" etype 23 wait 2ms

    // Stateful LDAP directory SPN enumeration over TCP 389
    ws -> dc tcp syn srcport 51389 dstport 389 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc tcp ack wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap bindreq msgid 1 basedn "cn=jdoe,ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=local" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap bindres msgid 1 resultcode 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap searchreq msgid 2 basedn "dc=corp,dc=local" filter "(servicePrincipalName=*)" wait 2ms
    ws <- dc ldap searchdone msgid 2 resultcode 0 wait 1ms

    // SMB2 administrative share probe on TCP 445 (rejected with STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED)
    ws -> fs tcp syn srcport 51445 dstport 445 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws <- fs tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws -> fs tcp ack wait 1ms
    ws -> fs smb negotiate msgid 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> fs smb sessionsetup msgid 1 sessionid 0x0001000000000001 wait 1ms
    ws -> fs smb treeconnect msgid 2 sessionid 0x0001000000000001 share "\\\\10.20.1.50\\ADMIN$" wait 2ms
    ws <- fs smb treeconnect msgid 2 sessionid 0x0001000000000001 treeid 1 status 0xc0000022
}

compile { ad_lateral_movement(workstation, dc_01, file_srv) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly ad_audit.fasm ad_audit.pcap && suricata -r ad_audit.pcap -k none
```

### 2. Verify Mail Gateway Filters & Cleartext Auth Policies Without Fighting Postfix (`smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`)
Checking whether an inspection appliance catches spoofed `MAIL FROM` envelopes, blocked attachment extensions, or legacy cleartext `imap` / `pop3` logins shouldn't require `nc` typos or live mail relays. FrameAssembly tracks TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` state automatically across the full `smtp` conversation and formats CRLF-terminated mailbox sessions out of the box:

```frameassembly
host ext_mta  { ip 198.51.100.25 mac 00:11:22:33:44:25 }
host mail_gw  { ip 10.10.25.10   mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:10 }
host legacy_c { ip 10.10.50.88   mac 00:11:22:33:44:88 }

flow smtp_filter_check(mta, gw) {
    mta -> gw tcp syn srcport 52025 dstport 25 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    mta <- gw tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    mta -> gw tcp ack wait 1ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 220 reply "mx01.example.com ESMTP Postfix" wait 2ms
    mta -> gw smtp ehlo "mailer.suspicious-sender.test" wait 1ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 250 reply "mx01.example.com" wait 1ms
    mta -> gw smtp mailfrom "<ceo-urgent@suspicious-sender.test>" wait 1ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 250 reply "2.1.0 Ok" wait 1ms
    mta -> gw smtp rcptto "<finance@example.com>" wait 1ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 250 reply "2.1.5 Ok" wait 1ms
    mta -> gw smtp cmd "DATA" wait 1ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 354 reply "End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>" wait 1ms
    mta -> gw smtp cmd "Subject:" param "Urgent Wire Transfer" body "Please open invoice_q4.scr immediately." wait 3ms
    mta <- gw smtp code 550 reply "5.7.1 Message rejected by attachment policy" wait 2ms
    mta -> gw smtp quit
}

flow cleartext_mailbox_probe(c, gw) {
    c -> gw imap tag "A001" cmd "LOGIN" arg "finance@example.com Winter2026!" wait 2ms
    c <- gw imap tag "A001" status "NO" response "Cleartext authentication disabled" wait 2ms
    c -> gw pop3 cmd "USER" arg "finance@example.com" wait 2ms
    c <- gw pop3 err response "Plaintext POP3 prohibited; use port 995"
}

compile {
    smtp_filter_check(ext_mta, mail_gw)
    cleartext_mailbox_probe(legacy_c, mail_gw)
}
```

```console
$ frameassembly mail_test.fasm mail_test.pcap && tshark -r mail_test.pcap -Y "smtp || imap || pop"
```

### 3. Audit Database Activity Monitors, SQLi Rules & Exposed Caches (`postgres`, `mysql`, `redis`, `memcached`, `nfs`)
Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) sensors and internal segmentation firewalls are notoriously annoying to test because binary database protocols reject raw ASCII strings on TCP 5432 or 3306. FrameAssembly builds valid PostgreSQL v3.0 frontend/backend frames, little-endian MySQL v10 packets, RESP bulk-string arrays, Memcached UDP/binary requests, and ONC-RPC v2 `nfs` calls:

```frameassembly
host app_node { ip 10.30.1.15 mac 00:1a:2b:30:01:15 }
host data_srv { ip 10.30.2.40 mac 00:1a:2b:30:02:40 }

flow db_and_cache_audit(app, db) {
    // PostgreSQL v3.0 startup + suspicious SQL query inspection
    app -> db tcp syn srcport 55432 dstport 5432 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    app <- db tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    app -> db tcp ack wait 1ms
    app -> db postgres startup user "readonly_reporting" db "customers" wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres authok wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres readyforquery wait 1ms
    app -> db postgres query sql "SELECT email, password_hash FROM users WHERE '1'='1';" wait 2ms
    app <- db postgres errorresponse sql "permission denied for table users" wait 2ms

    // MySQL v10 server greeting + unauthorized root login rejection (Error 1045)
    app <- db mysql greeting serverversion "8.0.36" wait 1ms
    app -> db mysql login user "root" db "production" wait 1ms
    app <- db mysql err errcode 1045 wait 2ms

    // Unauthenticated Redis CONFIG probe, UDP Memcached stats & NFSv4 export check
    app -> db redis cmd "CONFIG" args "GET" args "dir" wait 1ms
    app <- db redis replytype "err" value "NOAUTH Authentication required" wait 1ms
    app -> db transport udp memcached cmd "stats" wait 1ms
    app -> db nfs vers 4 compound xid 0x99887766 tag "export_probe" path "/srv/backups"
}

compile { db_and_cache_audit(app_node, data_srv) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly show db_audit.fasm
$ frameassembly db_audit.fasm db_audit.pcap && zeek -C -r db_audit.pcap
```

### 4. Validate IoT & Microservice Broker ACLs (`mqtt`, `coap`, `amqp`)
Whether an edge gateway is publishing retained `mqtt` sensor readings, polling `coap` over UDP, or routing events across `amqp` 0-9-1 exchanges, you can verify DMZ broker rules without deploying Mosquitto or RabbitMQ:

```frameassembly
host edge_gw { ip 10.60.10.12 mac 00:1e:c0:60:10:12 }
host broker  { ip 10.60.1.5   mac 00:1e:c0:60:01:05 }

flow broker_pipeline(gw, brk) {
    // MQTT v3.1.1 connect + retained QoS 1 publish
    gw -> brk tcp syn srcport 51883 dstport 1883 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    gw <- brk tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    gw -> brk tcp ack wait 1ms
    gw -> brk mqtt connect clientid "turbine-gw-12" keepalive 60 wait 1ms
    gw <- brk mqtt connack returncode 0 wait 1ms
    gw -> brk mqtt publish topic "plant/line4/temp" qos 1 retain pktid 7 payload "{\"celsius\":84.2}" wait 2ms
    gw <- brk mqtt puback pktid 7 wait 1ms

    // CoAP confirmable GET + 2.05 Content ACK on UDP 5683
    gw -> brk coap con get msgid 0x2201 token 0x0a0b0c0d uripath "sensors/pressure" contentformat 50 wait 2ms
    gw <- brk coap ack code "2.05" msgid 0x2201 token 0x0a0b0c0d contentformat 50 payload "{\"bar\":6.4}" wait 2ms

    // AMQP 0-9-1 preface, channel open, and Basic.Publish on TCP 5672
    gw -> brk amqp protocolheader wait 1ms
    gw <- brk amqp connectionstart wait 1ms
    gw -> brk amqp channelopen channel 1 wait 1ms
    gw -> brk amqp basicpublish channel 1 exchange "telemetry.events" routingkey "alerts.high_temp" payload "{\"unit\":12}"
}

compile { broker_pipeline(edge_gw, broker) }
```

## Protocol Summary Matrix (14 Protocols)

| Protocol | Keyword | Default L4 & Port | Dual-Transport Override | Wire Framing Handled Automatically |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SMTP** | `smtp` | TCP `25` | `dstport 587` / `465` | CRLF command/status lines + `\r\n.\r\n` `DATA` terminator on `body` |
| **IMAP** | `imap` | TCP `143` | `dstport 993` | Tagged (`A01`), untagged (`*`), and completion (`OK`/`NO`/`BAD`) lines |
| **POP3** | `pop3` | TCP `110` | `dstport 995` | `+OK` / `-ERR` server indicators + CRLF client verbs |
| **Kerberos v5** | `kerberos` | UDP `88` | `transport tcp` | RFC 4120 ASN.1 DER `[APPLICATION 10..13, 30]` + SPN slash splitting |
| **LDAP v3** | `ldap` | TCP `389` | `dstport 636` / `3268` | RFC 4511 ASN.1 BER `LDAPMessage` (`0x30`) + search filter stripping |
| **SMB2 / SMB3** | `smb` | TCP `445` | `dstport 139` | 4B NetBIOS length + 64B `\xFESMB` header + UTF-16LE share/file paths |
| **NFS v2/v3/v4** | `nfs` | TCP `2049` | `transport udp` | 4B RPC Record Marking + 40B ONC-RPC v2 Call (`100003`) + XDR padding |
| **Redis (RESP)** | `redis` | TCP `6379` | `dstport 26379` | RESP `*<argc>\r\n$<len>\r\n` bulk-string arrays & typed server replies |
| **Memcached** | `memcached` | TCP `11211` | `transport udp` | ASCII text commands or 24-byte `0x80` Binary Protocol (`opcode`/`opaque`/`cas`) |
| **MySQL v10** | `mysql` | TCP `3306` | Custom `dstport` | 3B little-endian length + seq ID + `HandshakeV10` / `COM_QUERY` / `ERR` |
| **PostgreSQL v3** | `postgres` | TCP `5432` | Custom `dstport` | Unprefixed `0x00030000` `StartupMessage` + `'Q'`/`'R'`/`'C'`/`'Z'`/`'E'` tags |
| **MQTT v3.1.1** | `mqtt` | TCP `1883` | `dstport 8883` | Fixed header flags (`QoS`, `RETAIN`) + Remaining Length + packet IDs |
| **CoAP** | `coap` | UDP `5683` | `dstport 5684` | 4B RFC 7252 header + `c.dd` code packing + Option `11`/`12` delta encoding |
| **AMQP 0-9-1** | `amqp` | TCP `5672` | `dstport 5671` | `AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01` header + Method/Heartbeat frames + `0xCE` end byte |

## Detailed Syntax Reference

### Mail Protocols (`smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`)

* **`smtp` (RFC 5321 — Default TCP `25`)**
  * **Syntax:** `smtp [ehlo ["<domain>"] | helo ["<domain>"] | mailfrom ["<addr>"] | rcptto ["<addr>"] | quit | cmd "<verb>"] [param "<arg>"] [code <u16>] [reply "<text>"] [body "<mime_body>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Emits `"EHLO localhost\r\n"` when no fields are given. Because `data` is a cross-layer token, write `smtp cmd "DATA"` to send the `DATA` command line; supplying `body "..."` automatically appends the mandatory `\r\n.\r\n` end-of-data sequence. For message submission or implicit TLS port checks, add `dstport 587` or `dstport 465`.
* **`imap` (RFC 3501 / RFC 9051 — Default TCP `143`)**
  * **Syntax:** `imap [tag "<tag>"] [cmd "<verb>"] [arg "<str>"] [status "<OK|NO|BAD>"] [response "<text>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** `tag` defaults to `"A01"` (`cmd` defaults to `"NOOP"`). If `status` is specified, emits `<tag> <status> <response>\r\n`; if `response` is given without `cmd` or `status`, emits untagged `* OK <response>\r\n`.
* **`pop3` (RFC 1939 — Default TCP `110`)**
  * **Syntax:** `pop3 [cmd "<verb>"] [arg "<str>"] [ok | err] [response "<text>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Client commands default to `USER\r\n`. Use `ok` for `+OK <response>\r\n` and `err` for `-ERR <response>\r\n`.

### Identity and Directory Protocols (`kerberos`, `ldap`)

* **`kerberos` (RFC 4120 — Default UDP `88`, `transport tcp` for TCP `88`)**
  * **Syntax:** `kerberos [asreq | asrep | tgsreq | tgsrep | krberror] [realm "<REALM>"] [cname "<principal>"] [sname "<service/host>"] [etype <u32>] [transport tcp]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Defaults to `asreq`, `realm "CORP.LOCAL"`, `cname "user"`, `sname "krbtgt"`, and `etype 18` (`aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96`; use `etype 23` for `rc4-hmac` or `etype 17` for `aes128`). Service principals containing `/` (such as `"cifs/filesrv.corp.local"`) are automatically split into multi-component ASN.1 DER `PrincipalName` sequences. `krberror` emits error code `24` (`KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED`).
* **`ldap` (RFC 4511 — Default TCP `389`)**
  * **Syntax:** `ldap [bindreq | bindres | searchreq | searchentry | searchdone | unbindreq] [msgid <u32>] [basedn "<dn>"] [filter "<expr>"] [resultcode <u32>]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Defaults to `bindreq` (`msgid 1`, `basedn "dc=corp,dc=local"`). Providing `filter` automatically selects `searchreq` (`wholeSubtree`), and providing `resultcode` (e.g., `0` `success`, `49` `invalidCredentials`) selects `bindres` unless `searchdone` is set.

### Network File Storage (`smb`, `nfs`)

* **`smb` (MS-SMB2 — Default TCP `445`)**
  * **Syntax:** `smb [negotiate | sessionsetup | treeconnect | create | treedisconnect | command "<logoff|close|read|write>"] [status <u32>] [treeid <u32>] [sessionid <u64>] [msgid <u64>] [share "<unc_path>"] [filename "<file>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Automatically selects `treeconnect` when `share` is set, `create` when `filename` is set, or `negotiate` (`0x0202` dialect) otherwise. Always escape backslashes inside double-quoted UNC paths (`share "\\\\10.0.0.50\\IPC$"`).
* **`nfs` (RFC 1813 / RFC 7530 over ONC-RPC v2 — Default TCP `2049`, `transport udp` supported)**
  * **Syntax:** `nfs [compound | proc "<null|getattr|lookup|read|write|compound>"] [vers <2|3|4>] [xid <u32>] [tag "<str>"] [path "<export_path>"] [transport udp]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Defaults to `vers 4`, `proc "lookup"`, and `xid 0x12345678`. Use `xid` (not `txid`) to set the ONC-RPC transaction ID.

### Databases and Caches (`postgres`, `mysql`, `redis`, `memcached`)

* **`postgres` (Frontend/Backend v3.0 — Default TCP `5432`)**
  * **Syntax:** `postgres [startup | query | authok | commandcomplete | readyforquery | errorresponse] [user "<role>"] [db "<database>"] [sql "<statement_or_msg>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Emit **one** message type per statement line (`authok` on one `<-` frame, `readyforquery` on the next `<-` frame) so each wire message gets its own length header. On `commandcomplete`, `sql` sets the completion tag (default `"SELECT 1"`); on `errorresponse`, `sql` sets the SQLSTATE `28P01` error text.
* **`mysql` (Client/Server Wire Protocol v10 — Default TCP `3306`)**
  * **Syntax:** `mysql [greeting | login | query | ok | err | eof] [serverversion "<ver>"] [user "<user>"] [db "<schema>"] [sql "<statement>"] [errcode <u16>]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** `greeting` builds a server-to-client `HandshakeV10` (`serverversion` default `"8.0.35"`), `login` builds `HandshakeResponse41` (`user` default `"root"`), `query` sends `COM_QUERY` (`0x03`), and `err` emits `#28000Access denied` (`errcode` default `1045`).
* **`redis` (RESP2 / RESP3 — Default TCP `6379`)**
  * **Syntax:** `redis [get | set | cmd "<verb>"] [key "<key>"] [args "<arg>"...] [replytype "<simple|status|ok|error|err|integer|int|bulk>"] [value "<val>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** `args` can be repeated multiple times on the same statement to build multi-argument RESP arrays (`redis cmd "HSET" key "user:1" args "role" value "admin"`). Omitting all modifiers sends `*1\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n`.
* **`memcached` (ASCII & Binary Protocol — Default TCP `11211`, `transport udp` supported)**
  * **Syntax:** `memcached [get | set | cmd "<verb>"] [key "<key>"] [value "<val>"] [flags <u32>] [exptime <u32>] [opcode <u8>] [opaque <u32>] [cas <u64>] [transport udp]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Emits ASCII commands (`get`, `set`, `delete`, `stats`, `version`, `flush_all`) by default, and switches automatically to the 24-byte `0x80` Binary Protocol header whenever `opcode`, `opaque`, or `cas` is present.

### Message Brokers and IoT Queues (`mqtt`, `coap`, `amqp`)

* **`mqtt` (OASIS MQTT v3.1.1 — Default TCP `1883`)**
  * **Syntax:** `mqtt [connect | connack | publish | puback | subscribe | suback | pingreq | pingresp | disconnect | pkttype "<type>"] [clientid "<id>"] [topic "<topic>"] [qos <0..2>] [retain [0|1]] [pktid <u16>] [keepalive <u16>] [returncode <u8>]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Defaults to `connect` (`clientid "client-01"`, `keepalive 60`). Attach published message payloads with `payload "..."` or `hexpayload "..."`.
* **`coap` (RFC 7252 — Default UDP `5683`)**
  * **Syntax:** `coap [con | non | ack | rst | msgtype "<type>"] [get | post | put | delete | created | changed | notfound | code "<c.dd>"] [msgid <u16>] [token <u32|"<hex>">] [uripath "<path>"] [contentformat <u16>]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Inside a `coap` statement, `ack` and `rst` set the CoAP header message type rather than TCP flags. Use dotted `code "2.05"` (`Content`), `code "2.01"` (`Created`), or `code "4.04"` (`Not Found`) for RFC 7252 response codes, and `payload "..."` to append the `0xFF` payload marker.
* **`amqp` (AMQP 0-9-1 — Default TCP `5672`)**
  * **Syntax:** `amqp [protocolheader | connectionstart | channelopen | basicpublish | basicdeliver | heartbeat] [channel <u16>] [exchange "<name>"] [routingkey "<key>"]`
  * **Defaults & Gotchas:** Emits the 8-byte `AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01` preface when no frame flag is specified, or wraps `Connection.Start` (`10,10`), `Channel.Open` (`20,10`), `Basic.Publish` (`60,40`), `Basic.Deliver` (`60,60`), and `Heartbeat` frames with the mandatory `0xCE` frame-end byte.

## Reversing Existing Mail, Auth, Storage, Database & Broker Captures (`frameassembly reverse`)

```console
# Convert an existing LDAP, SMB, Postgres, MySQL, Redis, or MQTT .pcap / .pcapng capture into .fasm code
$ frameassembly reverse db_audit.pcap sanitized_db_audit.fasm
$ frameassembly sanitized_db_audit.fasm sanitized_db_audit.pcap
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`

# Layer 7 — Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT

[**Use Cases**](#ot-and-ics-security-testing-use-cases) • [**Protocol Matrix**](#ot-protocol-summary-matrix-6-protocols) • [**Modbus/TCP**](#modbustcp-modbus) • [**DNP3**](#ieee-1815-dnp3-dnp3) • [**Siemens S7comm**](#siemens-s7comm-s7comm) • [**BACnet/IP**](#bacnetip-bacnet) • [**EtherNet/IP**](#odva-ethernetip-ethernetip) • [**OPC UA**](#opc-ua-binary-opcua) • [**Docs Hub**](../README.md)

Testing IT firewall rules is forgiving: if you fat-finger a rule, someone complains that Jira is slow. Testing OT/ICS firewall policies and NDR sensors on a live plant floor is less fun—nobody lets you fire unauthorized Write Single Register or Siemens `plccontrol` stop commands at a running S7-1500 or substation RTU just to verify that your new conduit ACL works, and buying €20,000 worth of DIN-rail PLCs for your desk usually gets vetoed by finance.

FrameAssembly compiles **`modbus`**, **`dnp3`**, **`s7comm`**, **`bacnet`**, **`ethernetip`**, and **`opcua`** `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures -> complete with automatic TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` tracking, IEEE 1815 DNP3 per-chunk CRCs, and 802.1Q `vlan` / `pcp` priority tags. Feed the output straight into **Suricata**, **Zeek**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, **Claroty** / **Nozomi** / **Dragos** sensors, or **`tcpreplay`** without risking an unplanned factory shutdown :)

## OT and ICS Security Testing Use Cases

### 1. Verify Read-Only Polling vs. Unauthorized PLC Write Blocks (`modbus` & `s7comm`)
Most IEC 62443 zone conduits allow an HMI or historian to poll registers (`readholdingregisters` / S7 `readvar`) while blocking register writes (`writesingleregister` / `writevar`) and CPU run-state changes (`plccontrol`) from engineering or IT subnets. Because industrial DPI firewalls drop mid-stream packets that lack a valid 3-way handshake, FrameAssembly tracks the TCP sequence math automatically:

```frameassembly
host scada_hmi { ip 172.22.10.10 mac 00:1b:21:10:00:0a }
host rogue_eng { ip 172.22.99.66 mac 00:50:56:99:00:66 }
host line_plc  { ip 172.22.10.50 mac 00:0e:8c:10:00:32 }

flow modbus_and_s7_dpi_audit(hmi, rogue, plc) {
    // Allowed baseline: HMI polls 4 Modbus holding registers on VLAN 110 (802.1p PCP 6)
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 tcp syn srcport 50502 dstport 502 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    hmi <- plc vlan 110 pcp 6 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 tcp ack wait 1ms
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus readholdingregisters txid 1 unitid 1 addr 100 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus readholdingregisters txid 1 unitid 1 count 4 value 1500 isresponse wait 2ms

    // Policy violation 1: Rogue host attempts Modbus Write Single Register (Function 0x06)
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 modbus writesingleregister txid 99 unitid 1 addr 100 value 0xffff wait 2ms
    rogue <- plc vlan 110 tcp rst ack wait 1ms

    // Policy violation 2: Rogue host negotiates ISO-on-TCP S7comm (port 102) and sends writevar + plccontrol
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 tcp syn srcport 50102 dstport 102 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    rogue <- plc vlan 110 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 tcp ack wait 1ms
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 s7comm rosctr "job" setupcomm pduref 1 wait 1ms
    rogue <- plc vlan 110 s7comm rosctr "ackdata" setupcomm pduref 1 wait 1ms
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 s7comm rosctr "job" writevar pduref 2 area "db" dbnum 1 offset 0 count 4 hexpayload "deadbeef" wait 2ms
    rogue -> plc vlan 110 s7comm rosctr "job" plccontrol pduref 3 payload "P_PROGRAM"
}

compile { modbus_and_s7_dpi_audit(scada_hmi, rogue_eng, line_plc) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly plc_dpi.fasm plc_dpi.pcap && suricata -r plc_dpi.pcap -k none
```

### 2. Test Substation SCADA Rules Without Computing DNP3 CRCs by Hand (`dnp3`)
Crafting IEEE 1815 `dnp3` packets manually in hex editors or Python scripts is pure misery: DNP3 requires a reflected `0xA653` 16-bit CRC in little-endian byte order on the 10-byte Data Link header **and** after every 16-byte chunk of transport/application data—get one bit wrong and Wireshark or your substation firewall silently discards the frame. FrameAssembly calculates every DNP3 header and chunk CRC automatically (and still lets you pass `crc 0xdead` when you *want* to test malformed-frame drops):

```frameassembly
host scada_master { ip 10.210.1.10 mac 00:1b:21:d2:01:0a }
host substation   { ip 10.210.1.55 mac 00:a0:f4:d2:01:37 }

flow dnp3_substation_check(master, rtu) {
    master -> rtu tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 20000 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    master <- rtu tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    master -> rtu tcp ack wait 1ms

    // Class data integrity poll (Group 60, Variation 1) + Analog Input response (Group 30)
    master -> rtu dnp3 read src 1 dst 10 group 60 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "response" src 10 dst 1 group 30 variation 1 hexpayload "0100dc05" wait 3ms

    // Select-Before-Operate (SBO) breaker control sequence on CROB (Group 12, Variation 1)
    master -> rtu dnp3 select src 1 dst 10 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "response" src 10 dst 1 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master -> rtu dnp3 operate src 1 dst 10 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 confirm src 10 dst 1 wait 1ms

    // Intentional bad Data Link CRC for firewall frame-integrity drop testing
    master -> rtu dnp3 directoperate src 1 dst 10 group 12 variation 1 crc 0xdead
}

compile { dnp3_substation_check(scada_master, substation) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly substation.fasm substation.pcap && tshark -r substation.pcap -Y dnp3 -V
```

### 3. Audit Building Management, CIP Manufacturing Cells & IDMZ Historians (`bacnet`, `ethernetip`, `opcua`)
Modern facilities mix UDP broadcast building controls (`bacnet`), Rockwell/ODVA CIP explicit messaging (`ethernetip`), and cross-zone historian conduits (`opcua`). You can synthesize all three into a single regression `.pcap` to validate VLAN segmentation and IDMZ firewall conduits before a maintenance window:

```frameassembly
host bms_srv      { ip 192.168.40.10  mac 00:1b:21:40:00:0a }
host hvac_ctrl    { ip 192.168.40.85  mac 00:40:ae:40:00:55 }
host cell_scanner { ip 172.22.30.10   mac 00:00:bc:30:00:0a }
host cip_drive    { ip 172.22.30.25   mac 00:00:bc:30:00:19 }
host historian    { ip 172.22.200.100 mac 00:50:56:c8:00:64 }

flow bms_and_factory_conduit(bms, hvac, scanner, drive, hist) {
    // BACnet/IP Who-Is discovery + Present_Value (property 85) setpoint write on UDP 47808
    bms -> hvac bacnet whois wait 2ms
    bms <- hvac bacnet iam objecttype 8 objectinstance 4085 wait 2ms
    bms -> hvac bacnet readproperty invokeid 1 objecttype 0 objectinstance 1 propertyid 85 wait 2ms
    bms -> hvac bacnet writeproperty invokeid 2 objecttype 1 objectinstance 1 propertyid 85 value 72 wait 2ms

    // ODVA EtherNet/IP session registration + CIP Get_Attribute_Single on TCP 44818
    scanner -> drive tcp syn srcport 54818 dstport 44818 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    scanner <- drive tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    scanner -> drive tcp ack wait 1ms
    scanner -> drive ethernetip registersession context 0x0102030405060708 wait 1ms
    scanner <- drive ethernetip registersession sessionhandle 0x00001001 status 0 context 0x0102030405060708 wait 1ms
    scanner -> drive ethernetip sendrrdata sessionhandle 0x00001001 cipservice 0x0e cipclass 1 cipinstance 1 cipattr 7 wait 2ms

    // IEC 62443 IDMZ conduit: OPC UA Binary HEL/ACK/OPN handshake + NodeId poll on TCP 4840
    scanner -> hist vlan 200 pcp 4 tcp syn srcport 54840 dstport 4840 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    scanner <- hist vlan 200 pcp 4 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    scanner -> hist vlan 200 pcp 4 tcp ack wait 1ms
    scanner -> hist vlan 200 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "hel" chunktype "f" endpointurl "opc.tcp://172.22.200.100:4840" wait 1ms
    scanner <- hist vlan 200 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "ack" chunktype "f" wait 1ms
    scanner -> hist vlan 200 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "opn" chunktype "f" securechannelid 42 tokenid 1 seqnum 1 reqid 1 wait 1ms
    scanner -> hist vlan 200 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "msg" chunktype "f" securechannelid 42 tokenid 1 seqnum 2 reqid 2 nodeid "Drive01.OutputRPM" payload "1485"
}

compile { bms_and_factory_conduit(bms_srv, hvac_ctrl, cell_scanner, cip_drive, historian) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly show ot_conduit.fasm
$ frameassembly ot_conduit.fasm ot_conduit.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 ot_conduit.pcap
$ frameassembly reverse ot_conduit.pcap ot_conduit_reversed.fasm
```

## OT Protocol Summary Matrix (6 Protocols)

| Protocol | Keyword | Default L4 & Port | Dual-Transport Override | Wire Framing & Checksums Handled Automatically |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modbus/TCP** | `modbus` | TCP `502` | `transport udp` | 7-byte MBAP header + Function `0x01..0x06, 0x10` + byte-counted `isresponse` PDU |
| **DNP3** | `dnp3` | TCP `20000` | `transport udp` | 10B `0x0564` Data Link + `0xC0` Transport + App header + IEEE 1815 `0xA653` CRC-16 per 16B chunk |
| **Siemens S7comm** | `s7comm` | TCP `102` | TCP only (RFC 1006) | 4B TPKT v3 + 3B COTP DT Data (`0x02f080`) + 10/12B `0x32` S7 header + `S7ANY` bit-shifted pointers |
| **BACnet/IP** | `bacnet` | UDP `47808` | UDP (`0xBAC0`) | 4B BVLC (`0x81`, `0x0A` unicast / `0x0B` broadcast) + 2B NPDU + packed 32-bit ObjectIdentifier APDU |
| **EtherNet/IP** | `ethernetip` | TCP `44818` | `transport udp` (`dstport 2222`) | 24-byte little-endian Encapsulation Header + CPF items (`0x0000`, `0x00B2`) + CIP EPATH segments |
| **OPC UA Binary** | `opcua` | TCP `4840` | TCP (`UACP`) | 8-byte little-endian UACP header (`HEL`/`ACK`/`OPN`/`CLO`/`MSG`/`ERR`) + SecureChannel & String `NodeId` |

## Detailed Syntax Reference

### Modbus/TCP (`modbus`)
* **Default Transport:** TCP port `502` (add `transport udp` for Modbus over UDP `502`).
* **Syntax:**
  `modbus [readcoils | readdiscreteinputs | readholdingregisters | readinputregisters | writesinglecoil | writesingleregister | writemultipleregisters | func "<name>"] [txid <u16>] [protoid <u16>] [unitid <u8>] [addr <u16>] [count <u16>] [value <u16>] [isresponse] [transport udp]`
* **Defaults & Reply Mechanics:** Defaults to `readholdingregisters` (`0x03`), `txid 1`, `protoid 0`, `unitid 1`, `addr 0`, `count 1`, `value 0`. Add `isresponse` on `<-` PLC replies to switch from the 4-byte `[addr, count]` request layout to a byte-counted `[byte_count, register_values...]` response PDU.

### IEEE 1815 DNP3 (`dnp3`)
* **Default Transport:** TCP port `20000` (add `transport udp` for DNP3 over UDP `20000`).
* **Syntax:**
  `dnp3 [confirm | read | write | select | operate | directoperate | unsolicitedresponse | func "<response|...>"] [src <u16>] [dst <u16>] [group <u8>] [variation <u8>] [crc <u16>] [transport udp]`
* **Defaults & Reply Mechanics:** Defaults to `read` (Function `1`), little-endian Data Link `src 100` and `dst 1`, and Object `group 60` / `variation 1` (Qualifier `0x06`) when group or variation is specified. For outstation responses (Function `129`), write `func "response"`. Omit `crc` for valid IEEE 1815 frames, or set `crc <u16>` to deliberately corrupt the Data Link header CRC.

### Siemens S7comm (`s7comm`)
* **Default Transport:** TCP port `102` (ISO-on-TCP per RFC 1006).
* **Syntax:**
  `s7comm [setupcomm | readvar | writevar | plccontrol | func "<name>"] [rosctr "<job|ack|ackdata|userdata>"] [pduref <u16>] [area <u8|"<db|mk|pe|pa|ct|tm>">] [dbnum <u16>] [offset <u32>] [count <u16>]`
* **Defaults & Reply Mechanics:** Defaults to `rosctr "job"` (`0x01`), `setupcomm` (`0xF0`), and `pduref 1`. On `"ack"` (`0x02`) and `"ackdata"` (`0x03`) frames, FrameAssembly automatically expands the 10-byte S7 header to 12 bytes with `error_class` and `error_code`. On `readvar` / `writevar`, `area` accepts symbolic names (`"db"` / `0x84` Data Blocks, `"mk"` / `"m"` `0x83` Merkers, `"pe"` / `"i"` `0x81` Inputs, `"pa"` / `"q"` `0x82` Outputs, `"ct"` / `"c"` `0x1C` Counters, `"tm"` / `"t"` `0x1D` Timers) and bit-shifts `offset << 3` into the 10-byte `S7ANY` pointer automatically.

### BACnet/IP (`bacnet`)
* **Default Transport:** UDP port `47808` (`0xBAC0`).
* **Syntax:**
  `bacnet [whois | iam | readproperty | writeproperty] [invokeid <u8>] [objecttype <u16>] [objectinstance <u32>] [propertyid <u32>] [value <u32>]`
* **Defaults & Wire Behavior:** Defaults to `whois` using BVLC function `0x0B` (`Original-Broadcast-NPDU`); `iam`, `readproperty` (`0x0C`), and `writeproperty` (`0x0F`) automatically switch BVLC to `0x0A` (`Original-Unicast-NPDU`). `objecttype` defaults to `8` (`Device`; use `0` Analog Input, `1` Analog Output, `2` Analog Value), `objectinstance` defaults to `1234`, and `propertyid` defaults to `85` (`Present_Value`). Do not attach TCP flags to `bacnet` statements.

### ODVA EtherNet/IP (`ethernetip`)
* **Default Transport:** TCP port `44818` (for implicit I/O over UDP, combine `transport udp dstport 2222`).
* **Syntax:**
  `ethernetip [nop | listidentity | listservices | listinterfaces | registersession | unregistersession | sendrrdata | sendunitdata | cmd "<nop|...>"] [sessionhandle <u32>] [status <u32>] [context <u64>] [cipservice <u8>] [cipclass <u16>] [cipinstance <u16>] [cipattr <u16>] [transport udp]`
* **Defaults & Wire Behavior:** Defaults to `listidentity` (`0x0063`), or automatically upgrades to `sendrrdata` (`0x006F`) with Common Packet Format (`CPF`) Unconnected Data (`0x00B2`) whenever `cipservice` (default `0x0E` `Get_Attribute_Single`), `cipclass` (default `1` Identity Object), `cipinstance` (default `1`), or `cipattr` is present.

### OPC UA Binary (`opcua`)
* **Default Transport:** TCP port `4840`.
* **Syntax:**
  `opcua [msgtype "<hel|ack|opn|clo|msg|err>"] [chunktype "<f|c|a>"] [securechannelid <u32>] [tokenid <u32>] [seqnum <u32>] [reqid <u32>] [endpointurl "<url>"] [nodeid "<id>"]`
* **Defaults & Wire Behavior:** Defaults to `msgtype "hel"` (or `"msg"` if `nodeid` is supplied without `endpointurl`) and `chunktype "f"` (Final). `"hel"` and `"ack"` populate 64 KB receive/send buffer negotiation fields, while `"opn"`, `"clo"`, `"msg"`, and `"err"` encode little-endian `securechannelid`, `tokenid`, `seqnum`, `reqid`, and namespace-0 String `NodeId` headers.

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`

# Multi-Host Network Topologies & Dual-Stack Scenarios

Real production incidents rarely happen between just two hosts speaking a single protocol. A single user login, WAN failover, or microservice call typically crosses Layer 2 switching, Layer 3 routing or tunneling, Layer 4 transport handshakes, and three or four Layer 7 services across 4 to 8 devices.

Reproducing that kind of multi-hop sequence in a physical lab or a virtual network emulator (GNS3, EVE-NG, Containerlab) just to get a test capture takes hours: you have to boot half a dozen router and server images, wire up VLAN trunks and VRFs, configure routing protocols and AAA daemons, and then coordinate `tcpdump` across multiple interfaces while manually triggering the event.

FrameAssembly lets you express the entire multi-device conversation in a single `.fasm` file and run it with two CLI commands (`frameassembly topology.fasm` to build `topology.pcap` + `tcpreplay`, **Wireshark**, or **Suricata** to replay or inspect, or `frameassembly reverse trace.pcap` to convert an existing capture into `.fasm` code) using three core capabilities:

1. **Multi-Host Flows:** Pass 3, 4, or 8+ endpoints into a single `flow(client, switch, radius, firewall, server, siem)` to interleave north-south client traffic, east-west service calls, and out-of-band telemetry in exact chronological order.
2. **Reusable Dual-Stack IPv4 & IPv6 Flows:** Write a `flow` once and run it inside `compile` first with IPv4 `host` definitions and then with IPv6 `host` definitions—automatically switching between IPv4 (`EtherType 0x0800`) and IPv6 (`EtherType 0x86DD`), recomputing IPv4/IPv6 pseudo-header checksums, and deriving multicast MAC addresses per RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`) and RFC 2464 (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx`).
3. **Precise `wait` Timers & Multi-Call `compile` Sequences:** Combine nanosecond-to-minute inter-packet delays (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) with sequential flow calls and inline statements inside `compile` to generate realistic keepalive cadences, VXLAN/IPsec bursts, and RTP media streams.

> **104 Ready-to-Compile Topologies in `examples/topologies/`:**
> In addition to the 5 reference architectures below, you can browse **104 full-stack `.fasm` scenarios** in [`examples/topologies/`](../examples/topologies/).

---

## Core Architectural Building Blocks

### 1. Multi-Host Flows Across 3 to 8+ Devices

A `flow` header can accept any number of host endpoints. Inside the flow body, every statement specifies which two endpoints are communicating on that line (`ws -> sw`, `sw -> aaa`, `aaa -> siem`):

```text
flow branch_transaction(client, edge_fw, app_srv, siem) {
    client  -> app_srv tcp syn dstport 443 wait 1ms
    edge_fw -> siem    syslog facility 4 severity 6 msg "Permit TCP 443" wait 1ms
    client  <- app_srv tcp syn ack
}
```

When you run `branch_transaction(workstation, perimeter_fw, web_srv, splunk_siem)` inside `compile { ... }`, FrameAssembly plugs those four `host` definitions into `(client, edge_fw, app_srv, siem)` in matching left-to-right order.

### 2. Dual-Stack IPv4 / IPv6 Reuse & Multicast MAC Derivation

FrameAssembly enforces strict Layer 3 address-family consistency per statement (mixing an IPv4 host and an IPv6 host on the same arrow is rejected with a clear validation error), while allowing the exact same `flow` block to run unmodified over both IPv4 and IPv6:

| Feature | IPv4 Execution (`host { ip 10.x.x.x }`) | IPv6 Execution (`host { ip 2001:db8::x }`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ethernet EtherType** | `0x0800` (or `0x8100` / `0x88A8` / `0x8847` when tagged) | `0x86DD` (or `0x8100` / `0x88A8` / `0x8847` when tagged) |
| **L3 `ttl <0..255>` & `dscp <0..63>`** | Maps to IPv4 `TTL` and `TOS/DSCP` | Maps to IPv6 `Hop Limit` and `Traffic Class` |
| **L3 `flowlabel <0..1048575>`** | Silently ignored on IPv4 statements | Encoded into the 20-bit IPv6 `Flow Label` field |
| **Multicast Destination MAC** | Auto-derived as `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx` (RFC 1112) when `mac` is omitted on a `224.0.0.0/4` host | Auto-derived as `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` (RFC 2464) when `mac` is omitted on an `ff00::/8` host |
| **UDP Checksum `0x0000` Guard** | RFC 768 checksum | RFC 8200 §8.1 mandatory pseudo-header checksum (`0x0000` mapped to `0xFFFF`) |

### 3. Multi-Call Traffic Bursts & Inline Statements in `compile`

Inside `compile { ... }`, invoke reusable flows multiple times alongside direct one-off statements to build sustained traffic bursts while automatically advancing TCP sequence numbers and packet timestamps across every frame:

```text
compile {
    underlay_bringup(spine_01, leaf_01)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    leaf_01 -> collector ipfix seq 1 domainid 100 packets 3 octets 384
}
```

---

## 1. EVPN-VXLAN Leaf-Spine Data Center Fabric (`lldp` + `bfd` + `bgp` + `vxlan` + `ipfix`)

**Scenario:** Models a data center fabric link bring-up between a Spine switch (`spine_01`) and two ToR Leaf VTEPs (`leaf_01`, `leaf_02`), followed by an East-West VXLAN tenant burst and an IPFIX flow telemetry export to a fabric collector:
1. **Layer 2 Link Discovery (`lldp`):** Spine and Leaf exchange chassis/port capabilities and system names.
2. **Sub-Second Failure Detection (`bfd`):** 50ms (`50000` $\mu\text{s}$) BFD Control sessions reach State `3` (`Up`) with `ttl 255` GTSM protection.
3. **Underlay Routing (`bgp`):** eBGP `open` (`asn 65101` $\leftrightarrow$ `asn 65000`), `keepalive`, and `/32` VTEP loopback `update` advertisement.
4. **Overlay Data Plane (`vxlan`):** A 3-packet burst encapsulating tenant traffic in `vni 10100` with `dscp 26` (`AF31`) and the IPv4 Don't Fragment (`df`) bit set for Path MTU validation.
5. **Fabric Visibility (`ipfix`):** `leaf_01` exports a CFlow/IPFIX v10 accounting record summarizing the 3-packet VXLAN burst (`384` octets) to `collector` on UDP port `4739`.

```frameassembly
host spine_01  { ip 10.255.0.1    mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }
host leaf_01   { ip 10.255.0.11   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:01 }
host leaf_02   { ip 10.255.0.12   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:02 }
host collector { ip 10.255.100.50 mac 00:1c:73:00:99:50 }

flow underlay_bringup(spine, leaf) {
    // 1. IEEE 802.1AB LLDP neighbor discovery on point-to-point fabric link
    spine -> leaf lldp chassisid "spine-01.dc1" portid "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "spine-01" sysdesc "Arista EOS 4.32" wait 1ms
    spine <- leaf lldp chassisid "leaf-01.dc1" portid "Ethernet49/1" ttl 120 sysname "leaf-01" sysdesc "Arista EOS 4.32" wait 2ms

    // 2. RFC 5880 BFD 50ms timers (State 3 = Up, Multiplier = 3, TTL = 255)
    spine <- leaf bfd state 3 mydisc 101 yourdisc 1 mintx 50000 minrx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bfd state 3 mydisc 1 yourdisc 101 mintx 50000 minrx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms

    // 3. RFC 4271 eBGP peering and VTEP loopback /32 route advertisement
    spine <- leaf bgp open asn 65101 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bgp open asn 65000 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.1 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp keepalive ttl 255 wait 1ms
    spine -> leaf bgp keepalive ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp update asn 65101 prefix "10.254.1.11/32" nexthop 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 5ms
}

flow vxlan_east_west(vtep1, vtep2) {
    // RFC 7348 VXLAN UDP 4789 overlay frame (VNI 10100, DSCP AF31 = 26, Don't Fragment)
    vtep1 -> vtep2 vxlan vni 10100 dscp 26 df payload "EAST_WEST_TENANT_RPC_FRAME" wait 2ms
}

flow export_fabric_telemetry(leaf, col) {
    // RFC 7011 IPFIX v10 flow record reporting the 3 VXLAN packets (384 octets)
    leaf -> col ipfix seq 1 domainid 100 srcip 10.255.0.11 dstip 10.255.0.12 proto 17 srcport 49152 dstport 4789 packets 3 octets 384
}

compile {
    underlay_bringup(spine_01, leaf_01)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    export_fabric_telemetry(leaf_01, collector)
}
```

---

## 2. Campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC Port Onboarding (`eapol` + `radius` + `dhcp` + `arp` + `snmp3`)

**Scenario:** Captures the complete lifecycle of an employee workstation plugging into a Zero-Trust campus switch port across 4 network tiers (`workstation`, `access_sw`, `radius_srv`, and `nms_srv`):
1. **802.1X Supplicant Handshake (`eapol`):** The laptop sends `EAPOL-Start`, responds to the switch's `EAP-Request/Identity` (`eapcode 1, eapmethod 1`), and awaits port authorization.
2. **AAA Policy Verification (`radius`):** The switch relays the identity to the RADIUS server (`accessrequest` on UDP `1812`) and receives `accessaccept` with the assigned `framedip`, then sends `EAP-Success` (`eapcode 3`) to open the switch port.
3. **IPv4 Address Assignment (`dhcp`):** Full 4-packet `DORA` exchange (`discover` $\rightarrow$ `offer` $\rightarrow$ `request` $\rightarrow$ `ack`) assigning `10.10.50.100/24`.
4. **Duplicate Address Detection (`arp`):** The workstation broadcasts a Gratuitous ARP (`sha`, `spa`, and `tpa` announcing `10.10.50.100`).
5. **Encrypted NMS Audit (`snmp3`):** The switch sends an authenticated and AES-128-CFB encrypted SNMPv3 `inform` (`sha256` + `aes`) to the NMS reporting `ifOperStatus = up(1)` on port 12.

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 10.10.50.100 mac 00:22:44:66:88:aa }
host access_sw   { ip 10.10.50.1   mac 00:11:22:33:44:01 }
host radius_srv  { ip 10.10.1.10   mac 00:11:22:33:44:10 }
host nms_srv     { ip 10.10.1.20   mac 00:11:22:33:44:20 }

flow campus_dot1x_onboarding(ws, sw, aaa, nms) {
    // 1. IEEE 802.1X EAPOL Start and EAP-Identity exchange
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type start wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eappacket eapcode 1 eapid 1 eapmethod 1 wait 2ms
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type eappacket eapcode 2 eapid 1 eapmethod 1 identity "eng-laptop-42" wait 2ms

    // 2. RADIUS Access-Request / Access-Accept and EAP-Success (eapcode 3)
    sw -> aaa radius accessrequest id 42 user "eng-laptop-42" nasip 10.10.50.1 wait 5ms
    sw <- aaa radius accessaccept id 42 framedip 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eappacket eapcode 3 eapid 1 wait 5ms

    // 3. DHCPv4 DORA lease acquisition (Discover -> Offer -> Request -> Ack)
    ws -> sw dhcp discover xid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp offer xid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dnsserver 10.10.1.53 subnetmask 255.255.255.0 leasetime 43200 wait 5ms
    ws -> sw dhcp request xid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp ack xid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dnsserver 10.10.1.53 subnetmask 255.255.255.0 leasetime 43200 wait 5ms

    // 4. RFC 5227 Gratuitous ARP announcement
    ws -> sw arp gratuitous sha 00:22:44:66:88:aa spa 10.10.50.100 tpa 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms

    // 5. SNMPv3 USM authPriv (HMAC-SHA-256 + AES-128) Inform to NMS
    sw -> nms snmp3 inform user "nac_auditor" engineid "80001f88801122334455" engineboots 5 enginetime 3600 auth sha256 "AuditAuthKey2026!" priv aes "AuditPrivKey2026!" reqid 500 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "access-sw-floor2" varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.12 int 1
}

compile {
    campus_dot1x_onboarding(workstation, access_sw, radius_srv, nms_srv)
}
```

---

## 3. Dual-Stack IPv4 & IPv6 Cloud Service Mesh (`dns` + `tcp` + `tls` + `grpc` + `redis` + `postgres`)

**Scenario:** Demonstrates **reusable dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 flow generation**. A single 4-tier Kubernetes service-mesh flow (`service_mesh_checkout`) models:
1. CoreDNS service discovery (`dns`)
2. Explicit 3-way TCP handshake (`syn` $\rightarrow$ `syn ack` $\rightarrow$ `ack`) on port `50051`
3. mTLS 1.3 negotiation with `sni` and `alpn "h2"` (`tls`)
4. Unary gRPC `CreateOrder` call (`grpc`)
5. East-west Redis inventory cache lookup (`redis`) and PostgreSQL SQL order insert (`postgres`)

In `compile`, calling `service_mesh_checkout` first with the `_v4` hosts and then with the `_v6` hosts generates both the complete IPv4 cluster trace and the complete IPv6 cluster trace in one PCAPNG file.

```frameassembly
// IPv4 Kubernetes Pod & Service Endpoints
host ingress_v4 { ip 10.244.1.10 }
host coredns_v4 { ip 10.96.0.10 }
host orders_v4  { ip 10.244.2.20 }
host storage_v4 { ip 10.244.3.30 }

// IPv6 Kubernetes Pod & Service Endpoints
host ingress_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:1::10 }
host coredns_v6 { ip fd00:10:96::10 }
host orders_v6  { ip fd00:10:244:2::20 }
host storage_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:3::30 }

flow service_mesh_checkout(gw, dns_srv, svc, db) {
    // 1. Internal service discovery via CoreDNS
    gw -> dns_srv dns query txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "a" wait 1ms
    gw <- dns_srv dns response txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "a" rdata "10.244.2.20" wait 1ms

    // 2. TCP 3-way handshake + TLS 1.3 ALPN "h2" + gRPC request on port 50051
    gw -> svc tcp syn srcport 51051 dstport 50051 mss 1460 wscale 7 sackperm wait 1ms
    gw <- svc tcp syn ack mss 1460 wscale 7 sackperm wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tcp ack wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tls clienthello sni "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc tls serverhello ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    gw -> svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" payload "sku=NVME-4TB&qty=2" wait 2ms

    // 3. Server-side Redis cache check (TCP 6379) & PostgreSQL transaction (TCP 5432)
    svc -> db redis get key "inventory:NVME-4TB" wait 1ms
    svc <- db redis replytype "bulk" value "42" wait 1ms
    svc -> db postgres startup user "orders_app" db "commerce" wait 1ms
    svc <- db postgres authok wait 1ms
    svc <- db postgres readyforquery wait 1ms
    svc -> db postgres query sql "INSERT INTO orders (sku, qty) VALUES ('NVME-4TB', 2);" wait 2ms
    svc <- db postgres commandcomplete sql "INSERT 0 1" wait 1ms
    svc <- db postgres readyforquery wait 2ms

    // 4. gRPC OK response returned to the ingress gateway
    gw <- svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" grpcstatus 0 payload "order_id=90042" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    // Execute over IPv4 cluster network
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v4, coredns_v4, orders_v4, storage_v4)
    // Execute the exact same flow over IPv6 cluster network
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v6, coredns_v6, orders_v6, storage_v6)
}
```

---

## 4. WAN Branch Failover & IPsec/MPLS Backhaul (`bfd` + `ospf` + `vrrp` + `ikev2`/`esp` + `qinq`/`mpls`)

**Scenario:** Models an enterprise branch office with redundant WAN edge routers (`branch_r1`, `branch_r2`) failing over to an IPsec-over-Metro-Ethernet/MPLS backhaul connected to `hq_hub`:
1. **LAN First-Hop Redundancy (`vrrp`):** `branch_r1` advertises VRRPv3 Group `10` Master ownership (`priority 200`, `vip 10.250.10.1`).
2. **WAN Link Failure & IGP Convergence (`bfd` + `ospf`):** `branch_r1` signals a BFD `Down` state (`state 1, diag 1`), then floods an Area `0` OSPF Link State Update (`lsu`) to `branch_r2` and receives an `lsack`.
3. **Carrier QinQ IPsec Tunnel Bring-Up (`qinq` + `ikev2`):** `branch_r2` negotiates an IKEv2 Security Association (`sainit` and `auth`) with `hq_hub` across a Metro Ethernet IEEE 802.1ad QinQ trunk (`qinq 2100`, `innervlan 100`).
4. **MPLS Core Encrypted Data Plane (`mpls` + `esp`):** `branch_r2` and `hq_hub` exchange MPLS-labeled (`mpls 32100`, `exp 5`) IPsec `esp` tunnel packets with explicit Initialization Vectors (`iv`) and Integrity Check Values (`icv`).

```frameassembly
host branch_r1 { ip 10.250.10.2  mac 00:00:5e:00:01:0a }
host branch_r2 { ip 10.250.10.3  mac 00:1e:be:25:10:03 }
host hq_hub    { ip 172.31.250.1 mac 00:1e:be:31:fa:01 }

flow wan_failover_and_ipsec_mpls(r1, r2, hub) {
    // 1. VRRPv3 LAN gateway advertisement and preemptive priority takeover on VRID 10
    r1 -> r2 vrrp vrid 10 priority 200 advint 100 vip 10.250.10.1 version 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms

    // 2. BFD Down notification (state 1, diag 1) triggers OSPF Area 0 LSA flooding
    r1 -> r2 bfd state 1 diag 1 mydisc 501 yourdisc 502 mintx 100000 minrx 100000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    r2 -> r1 vrrp vrid 10 priority 220 advint 100 vip 10.250.10.1 version 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    r1 -> r2 ospf hello routerid 10.250.0.1 areaid 0 hellointerval 10 deadinterval 40 priority 100 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 -> r2 ospf lsu routerid 10.250.0.1 areaid 0 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 ospf lsack routerid 10.250.0.2 areaid 0 ttl 1 wait 3ms

    // 3. IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH negotiation over IEEE 802.1ad QinQ (S-VLAN 2100, C-VLAN 100)
    r2 -> hub qinq 2100 innervlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange sainit initiatorspi 0x1122334455667788 responderspi 0 msgid 0 flags 0x08 wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub qinq 2100 innervlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange sainit initiatorspi 0x1122334455667788 responderspi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 0 flags 0x20 wait 2ms
    r2 -> hub qinq 2100 innervlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange auth initiatorspi 0x1122334455667788 responderspi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 1 flags 0x08 wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub qinq 2100 innervlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange auth initiatorspi 0x1122334455667788 responderspi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 1 flags 0x20 wait 3ms

    // 4. Encrypted IPsec ESP tunnel traffic over MPLS Label 32100 (EXP 5 EF)
    r2 -> hub mpls 32100 exp 5 bos 1 mplsttl 60 dscp 46 esp spi 0x00102030 seq 1 iv "1122334455667788" icv "aabbccddeeff001122334455" nextheader 4 payload "ENCRYPTED_BRANCH_VOICE_FRAME_1" wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub mpls 32200 exp 5 bos 1 mplsttl 60 dscp 46 esp spi 0x00102031 seq 1 iv "8877665544332211" icv "554433221100ffeeddccbbaa" nextheader 4 payload "ENCRYPTED_HQ_VOICE_REPLY_1"
}

compile {
    wan_failover_and_ipsec_mpls(branch_r1, branch_r2, hq_hub)
}
```

---

## 5. IEC 62443 Industrial Substation & IDMZ Conduit (`modbus` + `dnp3` + `s7comm` + `opcua` + `syslog`)

**Scenario:** Validates a segmented **IEC 62443 / Purdue Model** industrial architecture spanning Level 2 Supervisory HMI (`substation_hmi`), Level 1 Field Controllers (`bay_rtu`, `s7_plc`), and a Level 3.5 Industrial DMZ Historian & SIEM (`idmz_historian`):
1. **Level 1–2 Process VLAN (`vlan 110, pcp 6`):** The supervisory HMI polls holding registers from `bay_rtu` via `modbus` (TCP `502`), executes an IEEE 1815 `dnp3` Class 0 integrity poll (TCP `20000`), and reads Data Block `DB1` from a Siemens PLC via `s7comm` (TCP `102`).
2. **Level 2–3.5 IDMZ Conduit (`vlan 120, pcp 4`):** The HMI forwards aggregated telemetry upstream to `idmz_historian` over an `opcua` binary session (TCP `4840`) and emits an RFC 5424 `syslog` compliance audit message (UDP `514`).

```frameassembly
host substation_hmi { ip 172.22.10.5   mac 00:1b:21:22:0a:05 }
host bay_rtu        { ip 172.22.10.50  mac 00:a0:c9:22:0a:32 }
host s7_plc         { ip 172.22.10.60  mac 00:0e:8c:22:0a:3c }
host idmz_historian { ip 172.22.20.100 mac 00:50:56:22:14:64 }

flow substation_conduit_telemetry(hmi, rtu, plc, idmz) {
    // 1. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110 (802.1p PCP 6): Modbus TCP register poll
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus readholdingregisters txid 1 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 8 wait 1ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus readholdingregisters txid 1 unitid 1 count 8 value 13800 isresponse wait 2ms

    // 2. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110: IEEE 1815 DNP3 Class 0 read & analog input response
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 read src 1 dst 10 group 60 variation 1 wait 2ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 func "response" src 10 dst 1 group 30 variation 1 wait 2ms

    // 3. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110: Siemens S7comm DB1 variable read
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "job" readvar pduref 10 area 0x84 dbnum 1 offset 0 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "ackdata" readvar pduref 10 count 4 payload "DB1_OK" wait 2ms

    // 4. Level 3.5 IDMZ VLAN 120 (802.1p PCP 4): OPC UA Historian push & Syslog SIEM audit
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "hel" chunktype "f" endpointurl "opc.tcp://172.22.20.100:4840/historian" wait 1ms
    hmi <- idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "ack" chunktype "f" wait 1ms
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msgtype "msg" chunktype "f" securechannelid 10 tokenid 1 seqnum 1 reqid 1 nodeid "ns=3;s=Feeder01.BusVoltageKV" payload "138.0" wait 2ms
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 syslog facility 4 severity 5 hostname "sub-hmi-01" app "scada-poller" msg "IEC62443-Conduit: Authorized Level 1 poll & IDMZ push completed"
}

compile {
    substation_conduit_telemetry(substation_hmi, bay_rtu, s7_plc, idmz_historian)
}
```
