# Documentation Bundle: `docs/fasm-specification.md`

# FrameAssembly (`.fasm`) File Format & Media Type Specification (`text/vnd.frameassembly`)

* **Canonical Media Type:** `text/vnd.frameassembly`
* **File Extension:** `.fasm`
* **Uniform Type Identifier (UTI):** `io.github.stevewinschel.frameassembly` (conforms to `public.source-code`, `public.text`)
* **Freedesktop Shared MIME Info:** [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) (`sub-class-of` `text/plain`, glob `*.fasm`) • [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md)
* **Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic` Rule:** [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic)
* **IANA Vendor Tree Registration Template:** [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](../contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md)
* **GitHub Linguist Grammar & Heuristics:** [`contrib/linguist/languages.yml`](../contrib/linguist/languages.yml), [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml) • [`contrib/linguist/README.md`](../contrib/linguist/README.md)
* **Formal Context-Free Grammars:** [`grammar.ebnf`](../grammar.ebnf) (ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF), [`frameassembly.gbnf`](../frameassembly.gbnf) (`llama.cpp` / `XGrammar` GBNF), [`frameassembly.lark`](../frameassembly.lark) (Earley/LALR Lark)
* **Shell Tab Completions & Supported Distribution:** [`contrib/completions/`](../contrib/completions/README.md) (`bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `PowerShell`) • [`contrib/packaging/`](../contrib/packaging/README.md) (GitHub Releases + `.deb`, Crates.io `frameassembly`, NPM `frameassembly-wasm`, VS Code Marketplace `frameassembly-vscode`, and `SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly` for Homebrew & Scoop)
* **Reference Compiler, Website & Repository:** `frameassembly` v2.0.0 • [frameassembly.ai.studio](https://frameassembly.ai.studio/) • [https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly) • [crates.io/crates/frameassembly](https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly) • [docs.rs/frameassembly](https://docs.rs/frameassembly)

---

## 1. Abstract & Scope

The **FrameAssembly** file format (`.fasm`, media type `text/vnd.frameassembly`) is a network packet specification code format ("Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code") for building network packet captures.

A `.fasm` document defines network endpoints (`host`), optional parameterized multi-packet traffic sequences (`flow`), and compilation targets (`compile`). Compiling `.fasm` code to `.pcap` is the default root command of the `frameassembly` reference CLI (`frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]`, defaulting to `<input_stem>.pcap`), paired with four subcommands:
* `frameassembly show <input.fasm>` — validates a `.fasm` file and prints a relative-timestamp packet ladder in the terminal without writing disk files.
* `frameassembly reverse <input.pcap> [output.fasm]` — decompiles `.pcap` or `.pcapng` captures into `.fasm` code (defaulting to `<input_stem>.fasm`), emitting `host1`, `host2`, ... declarations, strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` keywords, and chronological packet statements inside `compile { ... }`. Encrypted payloads (such as SNMPv3 `authPriv`, TLS application data, SSH, or IPsec `esp`) are not decrypted during decompilation and are preserved as `tcp` or `udp` statements with `payload` / `hexpayload`.
* `frameassembly help [subcommand]` and `frameassembly version` — display CLI command reference and active compiler version (with hidden `-h`/`--help` and `-V`/`--version` flags for script compatibility, and positional output paths rather than output flags).

Generated captures across all **81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 network protocols** feed directly into **Wireshark** and **`tshark`**, wire-speed packet injection via **`tcpreplay`**, and rule validation in intrusion detection systems (**Suricata**, **Zeek**, **Snort**), firewalls, network monitoring platforms (**Checkmk**, **Zabbix**), and CI/CD pipelines.

---

## 2. Media Type & File Identification (RFC 6838 & RFC 6657)

This section defines the formal media type registration parameters for `text/vnd.frameassembly` in accordance with [RFC 6838](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6838) (Media Type Specifications and Registration Procedures) and [RFC 6657](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6657) (Update to MIME regarding "charset" Parameter Handling in Textual Media Types).

| RFC 6838 §5.6 Field | Normative Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type name** | `text` |
| **Subtype name** | `vnd.frameassembly` |
| **Required parameters** | None. |
| **Optional parameters** | `charset`: Per RFC 6657 §3, the default charset is `UTF-8`. Implementations MUST support `UTF-8` without a Byte Order Mark (BOM). |
| **Encoding considerations** | `8bit` (UTF-8 source code). Documents containing only ASCII characters in comments and string literals are valid `7bit` US-ASCII. |
| **File extension(s)** | `.fasm` |
| **Macintosh file type code(s)** | `TEXT` |
| **Uniform Type Identifier (UTI)** | `io.github.stevewinschel.frameassembly` (`public.source-code`, `public.text`) |
| **Object Identifiers (OIDs)** | None. |
| **Fragment identifier considerations** | Supports [RFC 5147](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5147) `text/plain` character and line fragment identifiers (for example, `#line=10,25`). |
| **Published specification** | `https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/blob/main/docs/fasm-specification.md` |

---

## 3. Character Encoding, Line Endings & Binary Safety

1. **Character Encoding (`UTF-8`)**:
   - All `.fasm` files MUST be encoded in valid UTF-8 (RFC 3629).
   - All language keywords, protocol names, header modifiers, identifiers, numeric literals, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, MAC addresses, and ASN.1 Object Identifiers (OIDs) belong to the 7-bit US-ASCII character set (`0x20..0x7E`).
   - Non-ASCII UTF-8 code points MAY appear inside single-line comments (`// ...`) and double-quoted payload strings (`"..."`).
2. **Line Endings & Whitespace**:
   - The preferred line ending for `.fasm` files in version control is LF (`0x0A`, `\n`).
   - Compliant parsers MUST accept both LF (`\n`) and CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings, as well as horizontal tabs (`\t`), form feeds (`\f`), and spaces (`0x20`) as token delimiters (`[ \t\r\n\f]+`).
3. **Prohibition of Literal NUL Bytes (`0x00`)**:
   - A valid `.fasm` file MUST NOT contain literal NUL bytes (`0x00`).
   - Arbitrary binary wire payloads (including NUL bytes) are represented safely in `.fasm` code using hexadecimal escape sequences inside `payload "<string>"` (such as `\x00\x09\x01`) or hexadecimal byte strings inside `hexpayload "<hex>"` (such as `hexpayload "000102ff"`).

---

## 4. Document Structure & Lexical Grammar (v2.0.0)

### 4.1 Comments, Strict-Lowercase Keywords & Flexible User Identifiers

- **Single-Line Comments**: Comments begin with `//` and extend to the end of the line. Neither `#`, `;`, nor `/* ... */` are valid comment delimiters in `.fasm`.
- **Strict-Lowercase Built-In Keywords (`[a-z0-9]+`)**: In FrameAssembly v2.0.0, every structural keyword (`host`, `ip`, `mac`, `flow`, `compile`, `wait`), every one of the 81 protocol keywords, every Layer 2–Layer 7 modifier (`echorequest`, `innervlan`, `clienthello`, `hosthdr`, `transporthdr`, `sackperm`, `agentip`, `hellotime`, `whois`, `pkttype`, `read`, `write`, `nop`, `error`, `shutdownack`, `readholdingregisters`, etc.), and every time unit suffix (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) MUST be strictly lowercase alphanumeric (`[a-z0-9]+`) with **zero underscores (`_`)** and **zero hyphens (`-`)**. Case-insensitive keyword matching is not permitted; when an uppercase, underscored, or hyphenated typo is encountered, the reference compiler reports a self-healing diagnostic (`replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'`).
- **Flexible User-Defined Identifiers**: User-defined `host`, `flow`, and flow parameter identifiers match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*`, allowing uppercase characters, underscores (`core_sw`), and internal hyphens (`fw-dmz-01`) while stopping before `->`. Double-quoted string literals (`"..."`) preserve exact casing on the wire.

### 4.2 Three-Block Program Model

Every compilable `.fasm` file consists of up to three top-level block types:

1. **Endpoint Declarations (`host`)**:
   ```text
   host <identifier> {
       [ip <ipv4-or-ipv6-address>]
       [mac <mac-address>]
   }
   ```
   - At least one of `ip` or `mac` MUST be present (for example, `host sw1 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }` for a MAC-only Layer 2 switch).
   - `ip` *(required for Layer 3–7 protocols; optional for pure Layer 2 switching protocols `lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `mpls`, `arp`)*: Standard IPv4 dotted-quad (`10.0.0.1`) or IPv6 address (`2001:db8::1`, `fe80::1`, `ff02::fb`).
   - `mac` *(optional when `ip` is present)*: 48-bit Ethernet MAC address in IEEE colon notation (`00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`), hyphen notation (`00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`), or Cisco dotted-quad notation (`001a.2b3c.4d5e`). When omitted on an IP host, FrameAssembly derives a direction-aware unicast MAC or the standard multicast MAC per RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx` for IPv4 `224.0.0.0/4`) and RFC 2464 (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` for IPv6 `ff00::/8`).

2. **Parameterized Traffic Flows (`flow` — Optional When Using Inline `compile` Statements)**:
   ```text
   flow <identifier>(<param1>, <param2>, ...) {
       <endpoint_a> -> <endpoint_b> [modifiers...] <protocol> [protocol_fields...] [wait <duration>]
       <endpoint_a> <- <endpoint_b> [modifiers...] <protocol> [protocol_fields...] [wait <duration>]
   }
   ```
   - **1 Statement = 1 Frame**: Each statement inside a `flow` (or inline inside `compile`) emits one Ethernet frame.
   - **Directional Arrows**: `a -> b` transmits from `a` (source) to `b` (destination); `a <- b` transmits from `b` (source) back to `a` (destination), automatically reversing source and destination ports on reply packets.
   - **Shared 4-Tuple TCP State**: TCP-based Layer 7 statements automatically emit a `PSH ACK` segment on that protocol's standard port and share sequence (`seq`) and acknowledgment (`acknum`) counters with raw `tcp` statements on the same 4-tuple connection.
   - **Dual-Stack IPv4 and IPv6 Reuse**: A `flow` works across both IPv4 host pairs and IPv6 host pairs. Mixing an IPv4 endpoint and an IPv6 endpoint in the same statement is rejected during validation.

3. **Compilation & Inline Statements (`compile`)**:
   ```text
   compile {
       <flow_identifier>(<host1>, <host2>, ...)
       <host1> -> <host2> [modifiers...] <protocol> [protocol_fields...] [wait <duration>]
   }
   ```
   - Exactly one `compile` block defines the ordered sequence of flow invocations and inline packet statements written to the output capture (`loop` blocks were removed in FrameAssembly v2.0.0; repeat flow invocations or inline statements directly inside `compile { ... }`).

### 4.3 Lexical Token Classes

The reference lexer (`src/lexer/mod.rs`) partitions input code into the following token classes:

| Token Class | Lexical Pattern / Rule | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Structural Keywords** | `host`, `ip`, `mac`, `flow`, `compile`, `wait` (strict lowercase `[a-z0-9]+`, zero `_` or `-`) | `host`, `flow`, `compile`, `wait` |
| **Directional Operators** | `->` (forward frame), `<-` (reverse frame) | `client -> server`, `client <- server` |
| **Delimiters** | `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `,` | `flow web(c, s) { ... }` |
| **Time Unit Suffixes** | `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m` (strict lowercase, attached to or following `wait <int>`) | `wait 500ns`, `wait 10ms`, `wait 2s` |
| **MAC Address Literal** | `([0-9a-fA-F]{2}:){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}` \| `([0-9a-fA-F]{2}-){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}` \| `[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\.[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\.[0-9a-fA-F]{4}` | `00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`, `00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`, `001a.2b3c.4d5e` |
| **IPv4 / IPv6 Literal** | `[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` \| `::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*\|[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}(:[0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+` | `192.168.1.10`, `2001:db8::1`, `ff02::1:ff00:1` |
| **Numeric Literal** | `-?[0-9]+\|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+` | `443`, `0x88cc`, `65535` |
| **ASN.1 OID Literal** | `\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*` (3 or more arcs for OID context) | `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0`, `1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3` |
| **String Literal** | `"([^"\\]\|\\.)*"` (supports `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xHH`) | `"example.com"`, `"AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01"` |
| **User Identifier** | `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*` | `core_switch`, `fw-dmz-01`, `host1` |

### 4.4 Complete 81 Native Protocol Keywords

Every strict-lowercase protocol keyword below compiles with zero mandatory sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers and ports) and accepts protocol-specific field overrides:

| OSI Layer | Count | Strict-Lowercase `.fasm` Protocol Keywords |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Layer 2 (Switching & Data-Link)** | 8 | `arp`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, `mpls` |
| **Layer 3 (Control, Tunnel, VPN, Routing)** | 20 | `icmp`, `ndp`, `igmp`, `mld`, `gre`, `vxlan`, `geneve`, `ipsec`, `esp`, `ah`, `ikev2`, `wireguard`, `ospf`, `bgp`, `rip`, `vrrp`, `hsrp`, `pim`, `bfd`, `openflow` |
| **Layer 4 (Transport)** | 3 | `tcp`, `udp`, `sctp` |
| **Layer 7 (SNMP, Infra, Time, AAA, Telemetry)** | 14 | `snmp1`, `snmp2`, `snmp3`, `dns`, `mdns`, `dhcp`, `ntp`, `ptp`, `radius`, `tacacs`, `syslog`, `netflow`, `ipfix`, `sflow` |
| **Layer 7 (Web, Security, VoIP, Access)** | 16 | `http`, `http2`, `grpc`, `websocket`, `tls`, `quic`, `tftp`, `ftp`, `ssh`, `telnet`, `whois`, `sip`, `rtp`, `rtsp`, `stun`, `ssdp` |
| **Layer 7 (Mail, Auth, Storage, DB, Brokers)** | 14 | `smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `kerberos`, `ldap`, `smb`, `nfs`, `redis`, `memcached`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `mqtt`, `coap`, `amqp` |
| **Layer 7 (Industrial ICS / SCADA / OT)** | 6 | `modbus`, `bacnet`, `dnp3`, `s7comm`, `ethernetip`, `opcua` |

---

## 5. Lexical Magic, Content Sniffing & `.fasm` Extension Disambiguation

### 5.1 Authoritative Three-Way Format Disambiguation

The `.fasm` file extension is historically associated with three distinct formats across network engineering, systems assembly, and hardware synthesis. Because neither Flat Assembler nor FPGA FASM has registered a formal media type with IANA or Freedesktop.org, naive extension-only associations can cause misclassification.

The table below provides the technical disambiguation across eleven dimensions:

| Dimension | **FrameAssembly (`.fasm`)** | **Flat Assembler x86 (`.asm`, `.fasm`)** | **FPGA Bitstream Assembly (`FASM`, `.fasm`)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Domain** | Network packet capture specification code ("Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code") | Low-level x86 / x86-64 machine assembly language | FPGA hardware tile and interconnect feature configuration (SymbiFlow / F4PGA) |
| **Media Type** | `text/vnd.frameassembly` (RFC 6838 Vendor Tree candidate) | Unregistered (`text/x-asm`) | Unregistered (`text/plain`) |
| **Comment Delimiters** | `// single-line comment` (C/C++/Rust style) | `; single-line comment` (standard assembly style) | `# single-line comment` (Python/Tcl/sh style) |
| **Top-Level Block Syntax** | `host <id> { [ip ...] [mac ...] }`, `flow <id>(...) { ... }`, `compile { ... }` | Directives: `format PE/ELF`, `section '.text'`, `segment`, `org`, `use32`/`use64` | Hierarchical dot-separated hardware tile paths: `CLBLL_L_X10Y100.SLICEL_X0...` |
| **Statement Syntax & Operators** | Directional arrows `->` and `<-` paired with Layer 2–7 protocol keywords (`tcp`, `http`, `snmp3`) | x86 CPU mnemonics: `mov`, `eax`, `xor`, `call`, `int 80h`, `push`, `pop`, `db`, `dd` | Bit-slice assignments (`ALUT.INIT[63:0] = 64'h...`) or bare feature strings |
| **Target Output Artifact** | Standard `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture file | Native machine code binary (`.bin`, `.obj`, `.o`, `.exe`, `.elf`) | FPGA configuration bitstream (`.bit`, `.frames`) |
| **Reference Tool / Compiler** | `frameassembly` compiler & CLI (rootless, offline, no `libpcap` or raw sockets required) | Flat Assembler (`fasm`) assembler & linker | `fasm2frames` / `xc7frames2bit` (SymbiFlow / F4PGA architecture tooling) |
| **Downstream Consumers** | **Wireshark**, **`tshark`**, **`tcpreplay`**, **Suricata**, **Zeek**, Snort, test harnesses | Operating system loader, CPU execution, static linkers (`ld`, `link.exe`) | Xilinx 7-Series / Lattice iCE40 FPGA programming hardware |
| **Registry Authority** | Candidate IANA Vendor Tree (`text/vnd.frameassembly`), Freedesktop XML, Wikidata | Unregistered informal convention (`.asm` primary, `.fasm` secondary) | Unregistered informal convention (`.fasm` tile configuration) |
| **Text Encoding & Line Endings** | UTF-8 without BOM (RFC 6657), LF / CRLF accepted, literal NUL (`0x00`) prohibited | ASCII or regional 8-bit code pages, CR+LF or LF | US-ASCII, LF or CRLF |
| **Syntax Highlighting Scopes** | `source.frameassembly` (TextMate), `FrameAssembly` (Linguist) | `source.assembly` or `source.x86` | Generic text or hardware configuration |

### 5.2 Explicit Syntactic Distinguishing Marks & Zero False-Positive Proof

Because each format operates in a separate domain, their lexical token sets and grammars do not overlap:

1. **Comment Syntax Discrimination**:
   - FrameAssembly exclusively accepts single-line comments introduced by `//`. Semicolons (`;`) and hash marks (`#`) are lexical errors outside quoted strings.
   - Flat Assembler exclusively uses semicolons (`;`) for comments.
   - FPGA FASM exclusively uses hash characters (`#`) for comments.
2. **Top-Level Structural Blocks**:
   - Every compilable FrameAssembly file contains strict-lowercase structural blocks: `host`, optional `flow`, and `compile`.
   - Flat Assembler source files never declare `host`, `flow`, or `compile` blocks; they declare `format`, `section`, `segment`, `org`, or raw assembly labels.
   - FPGA FASM files never declare blocks or braces; they consist of newline-separated feature lines with dot-separated tile identifiers.
3. **Directional Flow Statements vs Machine Mnemonics vs Tile Paths**:
   - FrameAssembly packet statements always use directional operators (`client -> server` or `client <- server`) followed by OSI layer protocol tokens (`tcp`, `udp`, `vlan`, `http`, `snmp3`).
   - Flat Assembler statements consist of x86 opcodes and registers (`mov eax, 1`).
   - FPGA FASM statements consist of tile coordinates and bit-slices (`HCLK_L_X0Y130.ENABLE_BUFFER`).

### 5.3 Content-Sniffing & Linguist Heuristics

GitHub Linguist, `bat`, `Chroma`, and Pygments identify FrameAssembly `.fasm` documents with zero false positives using the strict-lowercase v2.0.0 regular expression heuristics published in [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml):

- **Positive FrameAssembly Anchors**:
  - `^\s*host\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*\{\s*(?:ip|mac)\b`
  - `^\s*flow\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*\([A-Za-z0-9_,\s-]*\)\s*\{`
  - `^\s*compile\s*\{\s*(?:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*\(|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*(?:->|<-))`
  - Directional packet statement: `\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*(?:->|<-)\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s+(?:...strict-lowercase protocol & modifier tokens...)\b`
- **Negative / Competing Format Anchors**:
  - Flat Assembler: `(?i)^\s*format\s+(?:PE|PE64|ELF|ELF64|MZ|COFF|binary)\b`, `(?i)^\s*(?:section|segment|use16|use32|use64|org)\b`, or lines beginning with `^\s*;`.
  - FPGA FASM: Lines beginning with `#` or matching tile patterns `^[A-Z0-9_]+(?:\.[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}`.

### 5.4 Freedesktop `shared-mime-info` Magic Signatures & Desktop Integration

The Freedesktop MIME package in [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) (documented in [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md)) registers `text/vnd.frameassembly` as a subclass of `text/plain` with glob `*.fasm` (`weight="60"`) and `<magic priority="60">` rules matching strict-lowercase v2.0.0 keywords:
- `host ` or `host\t` within bytes `0..1024` AND (`ip ` or `mac `) within bytes `0..1536` AND `compile` within bytes `0..8192`, or
- `flow ` or `flow\t` within bytes `0..2048` AND `compile` within bytes `0..8192`.

Priority `60` ensures that FrameAssembly specifications take precedence over generic text handlers on Linux and BSD desktops while avoiding collisions with Flat Assembler and FPGA FASM.

### 5.5 Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic` Content Sniffing

Unix systems and command-line utilities using `libmagic` identify FrameAssembly `.fasm` files via [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic):

```magic
0	search/2048	host\ 
>0	search/1536	ip\ 
>>0	search/8192	compile	FrameAssembly network packet specification
!:mime	text/vnd.frameassembly
!:ext	fasm

0	search/2048	host\ 
>0	search/1536	mac\ 
>>0	search/8192	compile	FrameAssembly network packet specification
!:mime	text/vnd.frameassembly
!:ext	fasm

0	search/2048	flow\ 
>0	search/8192	compile	FrameAssembly network packet specification
!:mime	text/vnd.frameassembly
!:ext	fasm
```

Running `file -i <file.fasm>` returns `text/vnd.frameassembly; charset=us-ascii` or `utf-8`.

### 5.6 FAQ: What is a `.fasm` File? (FrameAssembly vs. Flat Assembler vs. FPGA FASM)

#### Q1: What is a `.fasm` file in FrameAssembly?
A `.fasm` file is a network traffic specification written in FrameAssembly `.fasm` code ("Packets as Code"). It defines network endpoints (`host`), optional directional packet exchanges across OSI Layers 2 through 7 (`flow`), and capture targets (`compile`). Running `frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]` compiles `.fasm` code offline into `.pcap` or `.pcapng` captures for Wireshark, `tshark`, `tcpreplay`, Suricata, and Zeek; `frameassembly show <input.fasm>` previews the packet ladder in the terminal; and `frameassembly reverse <input.pcap> [output.fasm]` decompiles captures back into `.fasm` code.

#### Q2: How does a FrameAssembly `.fasm` file differ from an x86 Flat Assembler file?
Flat Assembler (traditionally abbreviated FASM) is a machine-code assembler that translates low-level x86/x86-64 assembly instructions into binary executables (`.exe`, `.elf`, `.bin`). Flat Assembler files use semicolon (`;`) comments, format directives (`format PE`, `section '.text'`), and CPU mnemonics (`mov`, `jmp`, `xor`). In contrast, FrameAssembly files use slash (`//`) comments, strict-lowercase blocks (`host`, `flow`, `compile`), and networking statements (`client -> server tcp syn`).

#### Q3: How does a FrameAssembly `.fasm` file differ from an FPGA FASM file?
In open-source FPGA toolchains (SymbiFlow / F4PGA), FASM stands for FPGA Assembly. It describes low-level FPGA configuration bitstreams using hash (`#`) comments and dot-separated hardware tile feature paths (such as `CLBLL_L_X10Y100.SLICEL_X0.ALUT.INIT[63:0]`). It has no network endpoints, protocols, or flow logic.

#### Q4: How do tools, operating systems, and code editors disambiguate `.fasm` files?
Multi-tier content sniffing eliminates false-positive collisions:
1. **GitHub**: `.gitattributes` (`linguist-language=FrameAssembly`) and Linguist `heuristics.yml` detect strict-lowercase `host`, `flow`, `compile`, and directional arrows (`->` and `<-`).
2. **Linux & BSD Desktops**: Freedesktop `shared-mime-info` (`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`) and `libmagic` (`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`) inspect file bytes for `host ... ip|mac ... compile` or `flow ... compile` magic tokens, reporting `text/vnd.frameassembly`.
3. **VS Code & Web Packet Studio**: The VS Code Marketplace extension (`SteveWinschel.frameassembly-vscode`) and browser studio ([`frameassembly.ai.studio`](https://frameassembly.ai.studio/)) register the `source.frameassembly` TextMate scope and `text/vnd.frameassembly` MIME type.

#### Q5: Can I compile an x86 Flat Assembler or FPGA FASM file with the `frameassembly` compiler?
No. FrameAssembly is a network packet capture compiler. If you pass an x86 Flat Assembler or FPGA FASM file to `frameassembly`, the parser detects foreign syntax (such as `;` or `#` comments, `format PE`, or tile paths) and displays a plain-English error explaining that FrameAssembly `.fasm` files use `host`, `flow`, and `compile` blocks.

### 5.7 Registry Status Across Standards Bodies & Public Databases

The `.fasm` file extension and `text/vnd.frameassembly` media type maintain registration entries and packaging assets across major registries and supported channels:

1. **IANA Media Type Registry**: RFC 6838 Vendor Tree registration application in [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](../contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md).
2. **Freedesktop `shared-mime-info`**: XML package definition in [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) and upstream merge request guide in [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md).
3. **Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic`**: Magic rule definition in [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic).
4. **GitHub Linguist**: Language definition in [`contrib/linguist/languages.yml`](../contrib/linguist/languages.yml), disambiguation heuristics in [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml), TextMate grammar in [`frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json`](../frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json), and upstream PR guide in [`contrib/linguist/README.md`](../contrib/linguist/README.md).
5. **Wikidata Knowledge Graph**: Entity specification and QuickStatements batch script mapping properties `P31`, `P1195`, `P1163`, `P973`, `P856`, `P1324`, `P275`, `P306`, and `P277`.
6. **Supported Software Channels**: GitHub Releases + Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`, Crates.io (`frameassembly`), NPM (`frameassembly-wasm`), VS Code Marketplace (`frameassembly-vscode`), and `SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly` (`Homebrew` & `Scoop`), documented in [`contrib/packaging/README.md`](../contrib/packaging/README.md).

---

## 6. Security Considerations (RFC 6838 §4.6 & RFC 3552)

1. **Passive, Non-Executable Format**:
   - A `.fasm` file is a passive network packet specification describing network endpoints and packet header fields. It contains no general-purpose executable code, macros, shell invocations, or system calls.
2. **Bounded, Side-Effect-Free Compilation**:
   - The `frameassembly` language is intentionally non-Turing-complete: there are no loops (`loop` was removed in FrameAssembly v2.0.0), no unbounded recursion, no dynamic memory allocation expressions, and no conditional branching.
   - The language includes no file-inclusion directives (`include` or `import`) and performs no network I/O or DNS resolution during compilation, eliminating Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and local file inclusion vectors when compiling untrusted `.fasm` inputs.
   - The compiler runs offline without `CAP_NET_RAW`, raw sockets, or `libpcap`.
3. **Downstream Packet Capture Considerations**:
   - Compiling `.fasm` code (`frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]`) produces a passive `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture file.
   - Because FrameAssembly is built for firewall, IDS/IPS (**Suricata**, **Zeek**, **Snort**), and protocol dissector (**Wireshark** / `tshark`) testing, generated `.pcap` files may intentionally contain custom header combinations, fragmentation overlaps (`mf` + `fragoffset`), out-of-window TCP sequence numbers, or intrusion-detection test signatures.
   - Replaying a generated `.pcap` file onto a live network interface requires explicit invocation of an external replay tool (such as `tcpreplay`) by an authorized administrator.

---

## 8. Validated `.fasm` v2.0.0 Specification Examples

Every example below is a complete `text/vnd.frameassembly` document verified by the `frameassembly` v2.0.0 compiler (`frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]`).

### Example 1: Stateful TCP Handshake, HTTP/1.1 Transaction & Encrypted SNMPv3 USM Trap

```frameassembly
// Define IPv4 network endpoints (user identifiers allow _ and -)
host web_client    { ip 10.10.1.10  mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:10 }
host app-srv-01    { ip 10.10.1.80  mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:80 }
host nms_collector { ip 10.10.1.250 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:fa }

// Stateful HTTP health check followed by an RFC 7860 SNMPv3 SHA-256 + AES-128 trap
flow service_check_and_alert(client, srv, nms) {
    client -> srv tcp syn srcport 51400 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    client <- srv tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    client -> srv tcp ack wait 1ms
    client -> srv http get uri "/healthz" hosthdr "app.internal" wait 4ms
    client <- srv http status 200 reason "OK" body "{\"status\":\"healthy\"}" wait 2ms
    srv -> nms vlan 100 snmp3 trap user "secops" engineid "80001f888001020304" engineboots 3 enginetime 1200 auth sha256 "AuthSecret2026!" priv aes "PrivSecret2026!" oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "app-srv-01" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    service_check_and_alert(web_client, app-srv-01, nms_collector)
}
```

### Example 2: Dual-Stack IPv4/IPv6 Flow Reuse with Carrier 802.1ad QinQ & MPLS Tagging

```frameassembly
// IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint pairs
host edge_v4 { ip 172.16.10.1   mac 00-50-56-C0-00-01 }
host core_v4 { ip 172.16.10.2   mac 00-50-56-C0-00-02 }
host edge_v6 { ip 2001:db8:10::1 mac 0050.56c0.0011 }
host core_v6 { ip 2001:db8:10::2 mac 0050.56c0.0012 }

// Reusable TLS 1.3 handshake over 802.1ad QinQ (S-VLAN 2000 / C-VLAN 100) and MPLS label 32000
flow carrier_tls_probe(pe_a, pe_b) {
    pe_a -> pe_b qinq 2000 innervlan 100 pcp 5 mpls 32000 exp 5 bos 1 mplsttl 64 dscp 46 ttl 64 tls clienthello sni "api.carrier.example" ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    pe_a <- pe_b qinq 2000 innervlan 100 pcp 5 mpls 32000 exp 5 bos 1 mplsttl 63 dscp 46 ttl 63 tls serverhello ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
}

compile {
    carrier_tls_probe(edge_v4, core_v4)
    carrier_tls_probe(edge_v6, core_v6)
}
```

### Example 3: Industrial OT / SCADA Modbus TCP & IEEE 1815 DNP3 Conduit Verification

```frameassembly
host scada_master   { ip 192.168.50.10 mac 00:1b:21:50:00:10 }
host substation_rtu { ip 192.168.50.20 mac 00:0e:8c:50:00:20 }

flow substation_poll(master, rtu) {
    master -> rtu vlan 50 modbus readholdingregisters txid 10 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 4 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu vlan 50 modbus readholdingregisters txid 10 unitid 1 count 4 value 1200 isresponse wait 2ms
    master -> rtu vlan 50 dnp3 read src 1 dst 10 seq 1 group 60 variation 1 wait 5ms
}

compile {
    substation_poll(scada_master, substation_rtu)
}
```

### Example 4: Pure Layer 2 MAC-Only Switches & Inline `compile` Packet Statements

```frameassembly
host sw1 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }
host sw2 { mac 00:1c:73:00:00:02 }

compile {
    sw1 -> sw2 lldp chassisid "00:1c:73:00:00:01" portid "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "spine-01" wait 2ms
    sw1 <- sw2 stp rstp rootid "4096/00:1c:73:00:00:02" bridgeid "4096/00:1c:73:00:00:02" portid 0x8001 cost 0 flags 0x3c
}
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/for_nerds.md`

# For Nerds: Six-Stage Compiler Architecture, Rust Library API & Formal Grammars

While FrameAssembly is designed so network engineers, firewall administrators, and NOC/SOC operators can generate deterministic `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures with a few lines of declarative `.fasm` code ("Packets as Code"), under the hood `frameassembly` (v2.0.0, Rust Edition 2024) is a six-stage, zero-copy optimizing compiler, a five-stage PCAP/PCAPNG-to-`.fasm` decompiler, a reusable Rust library crate, and a formally specified language (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) backed by six-way synchronized context-free grammars, IDE/WASM bindings ([`frameassembly.ai.studio`](https://frameassembly.ai.studio/)), and a `2,611`-scenario compiler-verified training corpus.

This guide is the dedicated home for **systems engineers**, **Rust developers**, and **AI/ML practitioners**. For the formal RFC 6838 media type specification, UTF-8 encoding rules, lexical magic numbers, and `.fasm` extension disambiguation (IANA, Freedesktop `shared-mime-info`, Wikidata, and GitHub Linguist), see **[`docs/fasm-specification.md`](fasm-specification.md)** and **[`contrib/`](../contrib/)**.

---

## 1. Six-Stage Zero-Copy Rust Compiler Pipeline

FrameAssembly compiles `.fasm` source buffers into nanosecond-precision `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures through a deterministic six-stage pipeline in pure userspace—rootless, offline, and requiring **no `libpcap` or raw sockets** (`CAP_NET_RAW` is never required at build time or runtime).

```text
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                           .fasm Source Text (&'a str)                         │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 1: Zero-Copy Lexical Analysis (src/lexer/mod.rs — logos 0.14.4)         │
 │  • DFA scanner emitting SpannedToken<'a> = (Token<'a>, Range<usize>) slices   │
 │  • 646 strict-lowercase [a-z0-9]+ keywords/units (zero '_'/'-'), 81 protocols │
 │  • Flexible user Token::Ident ([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*)       │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 2: Two-Phase Token-Slice Parsing (src/parser/ — winnow 1.0.5)           │
 │  • Operates on Stream<'i, 'a> = &'i [(Token<'a>, Range<usize>, &'a str)]      │
 │  • Protocol-first whois guard + 3-tier scoped dispatch (universal -> protocol │
 │    -> fallback) + self-healing diagnostics ("replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'")    │
 │  • Contextual identifier recovery (parse_spanned_ident) for host/flow/params  │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 3: Semantic Validation (src/parser/validation.rs — miette 7.6)          │
 │  • Symbol uniqueness & duplicate host/flow/param detection                    │
 │  • Flow arity, protocol_requires_ip (L2 MAC-only vs L3+ IP), & dual-stack     │
 │  • IEEE/RFC bounds (vlan, dscp, ecn, ttl, flowlabel, gentrap, hsrp hellotime) │
 │  • Cross-protocol modifier exclusivity with byte-accurate miette SourceSpans  │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 4: Zero-Heap Wire Builders, Checksums & Crypto (src/builders/, packet.rs)│
 │  • Inner-outward encapsulation: L7 -> L4 -> L3 -> MPLS/QinQ/VLAN/Ethernet II  │
 │  • Disjoint-slice RFC 1071 checksums, RFC 8200 UDP 0x0000->0xFFFF rule,       │
 │    RFC 4443/5798 IPv6 pseudo-headers, SCTP CRC32c (LE), DNP3 CRC-16 (LE)      │
 │  • ASN.1 BER/DER (rasn 0.28) + SNMPv3 USM (RFC 3414/3826/7860) Ku -> Kul      │
 │    key localization, DES-CBC / AES-128-CFB, and HMAC-MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2          │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 5: Stateful 4-Tuple & Bidirectional Port Engine (src/backend/)          │
 │  • Evaluates RunStatement::{Invocation, Frame} inside compile { ... }         │
 │  • Stage 5a (EndpointPairPorts): Two-stage port inheritance across -> and <-  │
 │  • Stage 5b (Canonical4Tuple): Shared TCP seq/acknum state across tcp & L7,   │
 │    syn/fin +1 ghost-byte accounting, and automatic psh ack framing            │
 │  • Dynamic L7DispatchResult tuple preservation (dhcp, mdns, ptp, radius)      │
 └───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ STAGE 6: Nanosecond PCAPNG Serialization (src/pcap.rs) & Reverse (src/reverse)│
 │  • Transactional in-memory synthesis -> SHB -> IDB (IfTsResol(9)) -> EPBs     │
 │  • 5-stage PCAP/PCAPNG-to-.fasm decompiler (host1, host2, oracle verified)    │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Stage 1: Zero-Copy Strict-Lowercase Lexical Analysis (`src/lexer/mod.rs`)

The front-end tokenizer is built on [`logos 0.14.4`](https://docs.rs/logos) and compiles the `Token<'a>` enum into a jump-table Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA):

* **Zero-Copy Lifetimes (`Token<'a>`)**: Variable-length tokens—including `Token::Ident(&'a str)`, `Token::StringLit(&'a str)`, `Token::IpAddress(&'a str)`, `Token::MacAddress(&'a str)`, `Token::OidStr(&'a str)`, and `Token::Number(&'a str)`—borrow slices directly from the input `&'a str` source buffer without heap allocation.
* **Strict-Lowercase Built-In Keywords (`[a-z0-9]+`, Zero `_`, Zero `-`, No `ignore(ascii_case)`)**: In FrameAssembly v2.0.0, all `646` built-in keyword and time-unit tokens (`host`, `ip`, `mac`, `flow`, `compile`, `wait`, all 81 protocol names, L2–L7 modifiers such as `echorequest`, `innervlan`, `clienthello`, `hosthdr`, `transporthdr`, `sackperm`, `agentip`, `hellotime`, `whois`, `pkttype`, `read`, `write`, `nop`, `error`, `shutdownack`, `readholdingregisters`, and time suffixes `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) use exact lowercase `#[token("...")]` attributes without `ignore(ascii_case)`.
* **v2.0.0 Token Consolidation & Removal of `loop`**: `Token::Loop` is completely removed (`loop` blocks were retired in v2.0.0 in favor of direct flow invocations and inline frame statements inside `compile { ... }`); `sackperm`, `agentip`, `hellotime` (unified across STP `u16` and HSRP `<= 255` `u8`), and `whois` (unified across `Protocol::Whois` and BACnet `whois`) are deduplicated; and `pkttype`, `read`, `write`, `nop`, `error`, and `shutdownack` are first-class `Token` variants.
* **Flexible User Identifiers**: `Token::Ident` uses `#[regex(r"[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*", priority = 1)]` so user-defined `host`, `flow`, and parameter names permit uppercase letters, underscores (`core_sw`), and internal hyphens (`fw-dmz-01`) while stopping cleanly before `->`.
* **Six-Tier DFA Priority Disambiguation**: Overlapping lexical classes are resolved deterministically at compile time via `logos` priority weights:
  1. `priority = 6`: IEEE 802.3 MAC addresses across colon-separated (`00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`), Windows hyphen-separated (`00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`), and Cisco dotted-quad (`001a.2b3c.4d5e`) formats—outranks IPv6 hextets and dotted OIDs.
  2. `priority = 5`: Dotted-quad IPv4 literals (`[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`)—outranks dotted ASN.1 OIDs.
  3. `priority = 4`: Signed decimal and hexadecimal integer literals (`-?[0-9]+|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+`).
  4. `priority = 3`: ASN.1 Object Identifiers (`\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*`).
  5. `priority = 2`: IPv6 addresses (`::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*|...`) and strict-lowercase time suffixes (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`).
  6. `priority = 1`: Flexible user-defined identifiers (`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*`).
* **Spanned Token Output (`SpannedToken<'a>`)**: `lexer::lex(input)` returns `Result<Vec<(Token<'a>, Range<usize>)>, CompilerError>`, pairing every token with its exact byte offset range in `O(N)` time while skipping whitespace (`[ \t\r\n\f]+`) and single-line comments (`//[^\r\n]*`).

### Stage 2: Two-Phase Token-Slice Combinator Parsing (`src/parser/`)

Rather than parsing raw characters with backtracking regexes, FrameAssembly uses a two-phase [`winnow 1.0.5`](https://docs.rs/winnow) combinator architecture operating over a contiguous 3-tuple token slice (`Stream<'i, 'a>` in `src/parser/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub type Stream<'i, 'a> = &'i [(Token<'a>, core::ops::Range<usize>, &'a str)];
```

* **Protocol-First `whois` Disambiguation & Three-Tier Scoped Field Dispatch (`src/parser/statement.rs` & `src/parser/fields.rs`)**: Across 81 network protocols, many domain keywords naturally overlap (`whois`, `hellotime`, `cookie`, `data`, `value`, `version`, `status`, `token`, `msgid`, `group`, `get`, `set`, `response`, `reqid`, `echoreply`, `query`, `report`, `request`, `reply`, `read`, `write`, `nop`, `error`, and `keepalive`). FrameAssembly prevents cross-protocol keyword shadowing in `parse_frame_statement`:
  1. **Protocol-First Guard**: When `current_protocol.is_none()`, an explicit protocol-keyword matcher runs *before* fallback field parsing so `a -> b whois domain "example.com"` always sets `Protocol::Whois` instead of being intercepted by BACnet's `whois` modifier.
  2. **Three-Tier Modifier Loop**:
     * `parse_universal_field`: Cross-layer L2 (`vlan`, `qinq`, `mpls`, `srcmac`, `dstmac`, `ethertype`), L3 (`ttl`, `dscp`, `ecn`, `flowlabel`, `ipid`, `df`, `mf`, `fragoffset`), L4 (`srcport`, `dstport`, `seq`, `acknum`, `win`, `mss`, `wscale`, `sackperm`, `tsval`, `tsecr`, TCP flags—bypassing `ack` and `rst` when the active protocol is `coap`, `dhcp`, `tftp`, or `sip`), payload (`payload`, `hexpayload`), and timing (`wait`) modifiers.
     * `dispatch_protocol_field(active_proto, input)`: Routes directly to the active protocol's dedicated combinator module (`src/parser/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`, kept `pub(crate) mod` for clean `docs.rs` output).
     * `parse_fallback_field`: Invoked only when diagnosing cross-protocol modifier mistakes so Stage 3 can report a rich semantic error rather than a generic syntax failure.
* **Contextual Keyword Recovery (`parse_spanned_ident` in `src/parser/ident.rs`)**: Every keyword token in `Token<'a>` is mapped in `parse_spanned_ident`, allowing users to name hosts, flows, or flow parameters `http`, `dns`, `client`, `server`, `token`, or `status` without reserved-word collisions.
* **Self-Healing Diagnostics (`src/parser/mod.rs` & `src/error.rs`)**: When parsing fails on `Token::Ident(raw)`:
  * If `raw.to_ascii_lowercase().replace(['_', '-'], "")` matches a valid v2.0.0 built-in keyword `<kw>`, the compiler emits `"Keywords in FrameAssembly 2.0 are strictly lowercase without '_' or '-': replace '<raw>' with '<kw>'."` (powering 1-click Quick Fix actions in `frameassembly-vscode`).
  * If `raw.eq_ignore_ascii_case("loop")`, the compiler emits `"The 'loop' block was removed in FrameAssembly 2.0; invoke flows or frame statements directly inside 'compile { ... }'."`

### Stage 3: Semantic Validation (`src/parser/validation.rs`)

Once `parse_all` constructs the `Program<'a>` AST, `validate_semantics(&program, &source)` enforces domain invariants before any wire buffers are allocated, returning structured [`miette 7.6`](https://docs.rs/miette) diagnostics on failure:

1. **Symbol Uniqueness**: Rejects duplicate `host` declarations, duplicate `flow` declarations, and duplicate parameter names within a `flow` signature, reporting the exact source span of the duplicate.
2. **Statement Modifier Uniqueness & Exclusivity**: Rejects duplicate modifiers on the same statement, duplicate TCP flags (e.g., `syn syn`), and simultaneous `payload` + `hexpayload` declarations.
3. **IEEE & RFC Numeric Field Bounds**:
   * `vlan`: `1..=4094` (IEEE 802.1Q 12-bit VID; `0` and `4095` are reserved).
   * `dscp`: `0..=63` (RFC 2474 6-bit Differentiated Services Code Point).
   * `ecn`: `0..=3` (RFC 3168 2-bit Explicit Congestion Notification).
   * `ttl`: `0..=255` (8-bit IPv4 Time-to-Live / IPv6 Hop Limit).
   * `flowlabel`: `0..=0xFFFFF` (`0..=1,048,575`, RFC 8200 20-bit IPv6 Flow Label).
   * `gentrap`: `0..=6` (RFC 1157 SNMPv1 generic trap code).
   * `hellotime` on `hsrp`: `0..=255` (RFC 2281 8-bit HSRP hello timer, unified with 16-bit STP `hellotime`).
4. **Cross-Protocol Modifier Gates**: Rejects TCP flags or `seq`/`acknum`/`win` on `udp`, rejects SNMP modifiers on raw `tcp`/`udp`, rejects SNMPv3 USM fields (`user`, `engineid`, `auth`, `priv`) on `snmp1`/`snmp2`, rejects `getbulk`/`inform` on `snmp1`, and rejects `community` on `snmp3`.
5. **Flow Arity, Inline `compile` Statements (`RunStatement::{Invocation, Frame}`) & Dual-Stack Endpoint Homogeneity**: Verifies that every flow call (`RunStatement::Invocation`) and inline directional packet statement (`RunStatement::Frame`) inside `compile { ... }` resolves every endpoint to a declared `host` (with at least one of `ip` or `mac` declared), enforces `protocol_requires_ip` (allowing MAC-only `host` blocks across all 8 pure Layer 2 protocols: `arp`, `vlan`, `qinq`, `mpls`, `lldp`, `stp`, `lacp`, `eapol`, while requiring `ip` for Layer 3–7 protocols), and verifies `caller_host.ip.is_ipv4() == callee_host.ip.is_ipv4()` whenever both endpoints carry an IP. Mixing an IPv4 host and an IPv6 host in the same packet statement is caught at compile time with the exact statement span.

### Stage 4: Zero-Heap Protocol Wire Builders & Checksum/Crypto Engines (`src/builders/` & `src/packet.rs`)

FrameAssembly constructs frames **inner-outward** (`Application Layer 7 -> Transport Layer 4 -> Network Layer 3 -> Data-Link Layer 2`) so every outer header knows the exact byte length and checksum of its encapsulated payload before serialization:

```text
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Ethernet II (14B) + Optional QinQ (8B) / VLAN (4B) + Optional MPLS (4B) │
 │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
 │  │ IPv4 Header (20B, RFC 791 cksum) OR IPv6 Header (40B, RFC 8200)   │  │
 │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
 │  │  │ TCP (20B + RFC 7323 opts) / UDP (8B) / SCTP (12B + chunks)  │  │  │
 │  │  │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │  │
 │  │  │  │ Layer 7 Wire Builder Payload + Optional payload Bytes │  │  │  │
 │  │  │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │  │
 │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
 │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

* **Disjoint-Slice RFC 1071 One's-Complement Checksum (`packet::internet_checksum`)**:
  Implemented over `&[&[u8]]` using Rust's `slice.as_chunks::<2>()` so pseudo-headers, transport headers, and payloads are summed in place without concatenating temporary heap vectors:
  * **IPv4 Header Checksum (RFC 791)**: Computed over the 20-byte IPv4 header (`bytes 10..12`).
  * **TCP & UDP Pseudo-Header Checksums (RFC 9293 / RFC 768 / RFC 8200)**: Computed over `[&pseudo_header, &l4_header, payload]` for both IPv4 (12-byte pseudo-header) and IPv6 (40-byte pseudo-header).
  * **Mandatory UDP `0x0000 -> 0xFFFF` Folding (RFC 768 / RFC 8200 §8.1)**: In UDP, a checksum field of `0x0000` indicates "no checksum computed" (illegal over IPv6 and dropped by strict stacks). Whenever the one's-complement sum evaluates to `0x0000`, `build_udp_datagram` maps it to `0xFFFF`.
  * **L3 Control & Routing Checksums**: Native RFC 1071 and IPv6 pseudo-header checksums (RFC 4443 / RFC 5798) are computed automatically for `icmp` (IPv4 Type 8/0 & ICMPv6 Type 128/129), `ndp` (Types 133–137), `igmp`, `mld` (Types 130–132), `gre` (RFC 2784 optional checksum when `C=1`), `ospf` (RFC 2328 header checksum excluding the 64-bit authentication field), and `vrrp` (RFC 3768 v2 and RFC 5798 dual-stack v3 pseudo-header checksum).
* **SCTP Castagnoli CRC32c (`builders::l4::sctp::crc32c`, RFC 9260 §3.3.10)**:
  Uses a `const` 256-entry lookup table for the reflected Castagnoli polynomial `0x82F63B78` (normal `0x1EDC6F41`). The 32-bit CRC is computed with bytes `8..12` zeroed and written into the SCTP Common Header in **little-endian** byte order (`cksum.to_le_bytes()`) while all other SCTP fields remain big-endian.
* **DNP3 IEEE 1815-2012 Reflected CRC-16 (`builders::l7::dnp3::calculate_dnp3_crc`)**:
  Computes the reflected polynomial `0xA653` (normal `0x3D65`) with inverted remainder (`!crc`) written in **little-endian** order after the 8-byte Data Link header (`0x0564` sync) and after every 16-byte chunk of Transport + Application user data.
* **ASN.1 BER/DER & SNMPv3 USM Cryptography (`src/builders/l7/snmp/`)**:
  * Uses [`rasn 0.28.15`](https://docs.rs/rasn), `rasn-smi`, and `rasn-snmp` to encode SMIv1/SMIv2 `VarBind` lists across all 9 ASN.1 application/universal types (`int`, `string`, `oid`, `ipaddr`, `counter32`, `gauge32`, `timeticks`, `opaque`, `counter64`) and SNMPv1/v2c/v3 PDUs. Over IPv6, `snmp1` `TrapV1` automatically falls back to `0.0.0.0` for the 4-byte `agent-addr` field per RFC 3584 §3.1.
  * **RFC 3414 & RFC 7860 Key Localization (`Ku -> Kul`)**: `password_to_key_generic<D>` stretches the passphrase to `1,048,576` bytes (1 MB) in 64-byte blocks through `Md5`, `Sha1`, `Sha256`, `Sha384`, or `Sha512` to derive the master key $K_u$, then hashes $K_u \parallel \text{snmpEngineID} \parallel K_u$ to produce the localized key $K_{ul}$.
  * **Privacy Encryption (`DES-CBC` & `AES-128-CFB`)**:
    * `priv des` (RFC 3414 §8.1.1): Splits the 16-byte localized key into an 8-byte DES key and 8-byte pre-IV, XORs the pre-IV with the 8-byte salt to form the CBC IV, zero-pads the BER `ScopedPDU` to an 8-byte multiple, and encrypts via `cbc::Encryptor<Des>`.
    * `priv aes` (RFC 3826 §3.1.2.1): Forms the 128-bit CFB IV by concatenating `snmpEngineBoots (4B BE) || snmpEngineTime (4B BE) || 64-bit salt (8B)` and encrypts the `ScopedPDU` stream in-place via `cfb_mode::Encryptor<Aes128>`.
  * **Two-Pass Whole-Message HMAC Signing**: Inserts a zeroed placeholder of the exact RFC truncation length—12 bytes for `md5`/`sha` (RFC 3414 96-bit) or 24/32/48 bytes for `sha256`/`sha384`/`sha512` (RFC 7860 192/256/384-bit)—into `msgAuthenticationParameters`, BER-encodes the outer `SnmpV3Message`, computes the truncated HMAC over the serialized message, and splices the digest into `msgAuthenticationParameters` before re-encoding.

### Stage 5: Stateful 4-Tuple & Bidirectional Port Engine (`src/backend/`)

`backend::compile_program` evaluates `RunStatement::{Invocation, Frame}` entries in the `compile` block and maintains two complementary state machines across statements:

* **Stage 5a — Two-Stage Bidirectional Port Inheritance (`EndpointPairPorts`)**:
  For every `(caller, callee)` endpoint pair in a `flow` or inline `compile` sequence:
  * On a forward arrow (`c -> s`), `src_port` defaults to the remembered `caller_port` (or `12345` on first use) unless overridden by `srcport`, and `dst_port` defaults to the protocol's RFC well-known destination port (or an explicitly set `callee_port`).
  * On a reverse arrow (`c <- s`), the source and destination ports automatically flip: `src_port` inherits the server's port and `dst_port` inherits `caller_port` (`12345` or the custom `srcport` from the request).
* **Dynamic L7 Builder Return-Tuple Preservation (`src/backend/l7_dispatch.rs`)**:
  Several protocols dynamically select ports or multicast destination IPs based on address family or message type. `build_l7_packet_payload` returns an `L7DispatchResult` struct `{ payload, is_tcp, src_port, dst_port, target_ip }` that preserves:
  * `dhcp`: `(payload, 68, 67)` for DHCPv4 vs. `(payload, 546, 547)` for DHCPv6.
  * `mdns`: `(payload, 224.0.0.251, 5353)` over IPv4 vs. `(payload, ff02::fb, 5353)` over IPv6.
  * `ptp`: `(payload, 319)` for IEEE 1588 Event messages (`sync`, `delayreq`, `pdelayreq`, `pdelayresp`) vs. `(payload, 320)` for General messages (`followup`, `delayresp`, `announce`, `signaling`, `management`).
  * `radius`: `(payload, 1812)` for Authentication (`accessrequest`, `accessaccept`, `accessreject`, `accesschallenge`) vs. `(payload, 1813)` for Accounting (`accountingrequest`, `accountingresponse`), automatically assigning the server source port on `<-` replies.
* **Stage 5b — Canonical 4-Tuple TCP State Machine (`Canonical4Tuple` & `TcpStreamState`)**:
  All TCP-based protocols (`tcp`, `bgp`, `openflow`, `tacacs`, `ftp`, `ssh`, `telnet`, `http`, `http2`, `grpc`, `websocket`, `tls`, `rtsp`, `smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `ldap`, `smb`, `redis`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `mqtt`, `amqp`, `whois`, `s7comm`, `opcua`, default-TCP `modbus`/`nfs`/`memcached`/`dnp3`/`ethernetip`, and `transport tcp` overrides on `dns`/`sip`/`syslog`/`kerberos`) share a canonical 4-tuple table keyed by sorted endpoints `((IpAddr, u16), (IpAddr, u16))`:
  * Each new stream initializes `seq1 = 1000` and `seq2 = 1000`.
  * Every frame uses the sender's current sequence counter (unless overridden by `seq <u32>`, which resynchronizes the counter) and sets `acknum` to the peer's current sequence counter.
  * After each frame, the sender's sequence counter advances by `payload_len + (1 if syn) + (1 if fin)` using wrapping 32-bit arithmetic.
  * TCP-based L7 statements without explicit TCP flags automatically emit `psh ack` (`0x18`) frames on that connection, seamlessly continuing the sequence numbers established by a preceding raw `tcp` 3-way handshake.
* **Automatic Multicast & Unicast MAC Derivation (`derive_mac`)**:
  When a `host` omits `mac` (and the statement omits `srcmac`/`dstmac`) or when a protocol targets a multicast group (`ndp`, `igmp`, `mld`, `ospf`, `rip`, `vrrp`, `hsrp`, `pim`, `mdns`), FrameAssembly derives the IEEE 802.3 MAC automatically:
  * **IPv6 Multicast (`ff00::/8`, RFC 2464 §7)**: Maps the low 32 bits of the IPv6 address to `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx`.
  * **IPv4 Multicast (`224.0.0.0/4`, RFC 1112 §6.4)**: Maps the low 23 bits of the IPv4 address to `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx` (`octets[1] & 0x7F`).
  * **Unicast Fallback**: Uses `00:00:00:00:00:01` for the forward caller and `00:00:00:00:00:02` for the callee.
  * **RFC Hop Limit Defaults**: Automatically sets IPv6 Hop Limit / IPv4 TTL to `255` for `ndp` (RFC 4861) and `vrrp` (RFC 5798) when `ttl` is not explicitly specified.

### Stage 6: Nanosecond PCAPNG Serialization (`src/pcap.rs`) & 5-Stage PCAP Decompiler (`src/reverse/`)

`pcap::PcapWriter` wraps [`pcap-file 2.0.0`](https://docs.rs/pcap-file) to emit standards-compliant PCAP Next Generation (`PCAPNG`) captures:

1. **Transactional Synthesis**: `backend::generate_pcap` executes `compile_program(program)` in memory first, creating the output file on disk only after all frames have been synthesized without error.
2. **Block Ordering (`SHB -> IDB -> EPB`)**:
   * **Section Header Block (`SHB`)**: Emitted automatically by `PcapNgWriter::new(file)` with magic bytes `0x0A0D0D0A`.
   * **Interface Description Block (`IDB`)**: Configured with `DataLink::ETHERNET` (`LINKTYPE_ETHERNET = 1`), `snaplen = 65535`, and `InterfaceDescriptionOption::IfTsResol(9)` (`10^-9` nanosecond resolution). Including `IfTsResol(9)` prevents the $1000\times$ timestamp skew that occurs when nanosecond timestamps are interpreted as default microseconds (`10^-6`).
   * **Enhanced Packet Blocks (`EPB`)**: Starts at deterministic epoch `1_700_000_000_000_000_000` ns (`2023-11-14T22:13:20Z`) and advances by each statement's `wait` duration (default `10ms` = `10_000_000` ns), writing `Duration::from_nanos(ts_nanos_total)` and `Cow::Borrowed(packet_data)`.

In the reverse direction (`frameassembly reverse <input.pcap> [output.fasm]`, defaulting to `<input_stem>.fasm`), `src/reverse/` decompiles binary `.pcap` and `.pcapng` captures back into canonical strict-lowercase v2.0.0 `.fasm` code through a 5-stage pipeline:
1. **Container Normalization (`src/reverse/container.rs`)**: Detects PCAPNG (`0x0A0D0D0A`) vs. microsecond/nanosecond legacy PCAP magic numbers, normalizes 8 linktypes (`ETHERNET`, `RAW`, `IPV4`, `IPV6`, `LINUX_SLL`, `LINUX_SLL2`, `NULL`, `LOOP`) into 14-byte Ethernet II frames, and strips 60/64-byte Ethernet zero-padding and 4-byte FCS trailers.
2. **Modular `<layer>/<protocol>` Dissection (`src/reverse/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`)**: Uses `etherparse 0.21.0` (`SlicedPacket` / `LaxSlicedPacket` and `link_exts`) for zero-copy L2–L4 slicing (`src/reverse/l3/{ip,ipv6,icmpv6}.rs` alongside the 20 L3 protocol dissectors) and dispatches across 81 per-protocol decompiler modules (including `src/reverse/l7/{snmp1,snmp2,snmp3}.rs` across all 50 L7 protocol dissectors) matching `src/ast/`, `src/parser/`, and `src/builders/` 1-to-1.
3. **Deterministic Topology Discovery (`src/reverse/topology.rs`)**: Infers sequential `host1`, `host2`, ... declarations (zero underscores), tracks dominant unicast MACs, pairs broadcast/multicast frames, and locks directional arrows (`->` vs. `<-`) per endpoint pair.
4. **Per-Packet Self-Check Compiler Oracle (`src/reverse/oracle.rs`)**: Compiles each candidate `.fasm` statement in memory via `parse_program` -> `compile_program` (`verify_with_oracle`), automatically attaching residual `payload`/`hexpayload` or stepping down cleanly to raw L4 (`tcp`/`udp`) or L2 (`vlan`/`qinq`/`mpls`) statements with zero `//` warning or fallback comments.
5. **Shadow-State Elision & Emission (`src/reverse/shadow_emit.rs`)**: Mirrors the forward compiler's `EndpointPairPorts` and `Canonical4Tuple` TCP sequence/acknowledgment state machine to elide redundant defaults and emits `host<N>` declarations (`host1`, `host2`, ...) and a single `compile { ... }` block containing strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` tokens and zero `loop` blocks.

---

## 2. CLI Contract, Supported Packaging & `<layer>/<protocol>` Symmetry

### CLI Command Contract (`src/main.rs` & `contrib/completions/`)

In FrameAssembly v2.0.0, compiling `.fasm` to `.pcap` is the **default root command** (using positional arguments with no `compile` CLI subcommand and no output flags), paired with four subcommands:
* `frameassembly <input.fasm> [output.pcap]` — compiles `.fasm` to `.pcap` / `.pcapng` (defaults to `<input_stem>.pcap`).
* `frameassembly show <input.fasm>` — validates and prints a relative-timestamp packet ladder in the terminal without writing disk files.
* `frameassembly reverse <input.pcap> [output.fasm]` — decompiles `.pcap` / `.pcapng` into canonical v2.0.0 `.fasm` code (defaults to `<input_stem>.fasm`).
* `frameassembly help [subcommand]` & `frameassembly version` — display CLI documentation and version (`-h`/`--help` and `-V`/`--version` remain supported as hidden flags for script compatibility).
* Static Tab-completion scripts for **Bash**, **Zsh**, **Fish**, and **PowerShell** live in [`contrib/completions/`](../contrib/completions/README.md), and supported release channels in [`contrib/packaging/`](../contrib/packaging/README.md) cover GitHub Releases + Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`, Crates.io (`frameassembly`), NPM (`frameassembly-wasm`), VS Code Marketplace (`frameassembly-vscode`), and `SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly` (`Homebrew` & `Scoop`).

### Repository `<layer>/<protocol>` Symmetry

FrameAssembly enforces a 1-to-1 structural symmetry across `src/`, `examples/`, and `docs/`:

```text
frameassembly/
├── Cargo.toml                         # Crate manifest (v2.0.0, Rust 1.85+, Edition 2024, centralized [lints])
├── grammar.ebnf                       # Formal ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF grammar (strict-lowercase v2.0.0)
├── frameassembly.gbnf                 # GGML BNF grammar for llama.cpp / XGrammar constrained decoding
├── frameassembly.lark                 # Earley/LALR Lark grammar for Outlines / vLLM / Guidance / llguidance
├── llms.txt / llms-full.txt           # AI agent discovery index & single-fetch RAG context bundle
├── contrib/
│   ├── completions/                   # Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell Tab-completion scripts
│   ├── packaging/                     # .deb, Homebrew & Scoop tap, NPM WASM, and VS Code packaging
│   └── {iana,linguist,magic,mime}/    # text/vnd.frameassembly MIME, libmagic, IANA & Linguist rules
├── frameassembly-wasm/                # WebAssembly (wasm-bindgen) compiler, decompiler & UTF-16 IDE diagnostics
├── frameassembly-vscode/              # VS Code Packet Studio & TextMate grammar (source.frameassembly)
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                         # Crate root & public library re-exports
│   ├── main.rs                        # Clap 4.6 CLI (<input.fasm> [output.pcap], show, reverse, help, version)
│   ├── error.rs                       # CompilerError enum with self-healing miette::Diagnostic spans
│   ├── packet.rs                      # Ethernet/VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/IPv4/IPv6/TCP/UDP framing & RFC 1071 checksums
│   ├── pcap.rs                        # PcapWriter PCAPNG serializer with IfTsResol(9) nanosecond timestamps
│   ├── lexer/
│   │   └── mod.rs                     # Logos 0.14.4 strict-lowercase Token<'a> DFA & lex() entrypoint
│   ├── ast/
│   │   ├── mod.rs                     # Program, HostDef, FlowDef, RunStatement, FrameStatement, Protocol
│   │   └── {l2,l3,l4,l7}/             # 81 *Spec structs with strict-lowercase /// Syntax mapping: docs
│   ├── parser/
│   │   ├── mod.rs                     # Stream<'i, 'a>, parse_program(), self-healing error helpers
│   │   ├── fields.rs                  # ParsedField, parse_universal_field, dispatch_protocol_field
│   │   ├── statement.rs               # Protocol-first whois guard & 3-tier modifier loop
│   │   ├── validation.rs              # validate_semantics() semantic invariant pass
│   │   └── {l2,l3,l4,l7}/             # 81 pub(crate) per-protocol winnow field combinators
│   ├── builders/
│   │   ├── mod.rs                     # WireContext<'a> & layer builder exports
│   │   ├── {l2,l3,l4}/                # L2, L3, and L4 wire encoders (including SCTP CRC32c)
│   │   └── l7/                        # snmp/{builder,crypto}.rs + 47 L7 wire builders
│   ├── backend/
│   │   ├── mod.rs                     # compile_program(), generate_pcap(), 4-tuple & port inheritance state
│   │   └── l7_dispatch.rs             # L7DispatchResult dynamic port & multicast IP preservation
│   └── reverse/
│       ├── mod.rs                     # reverse_pcap_reader(), reverse_pcap_bytes(), reverse_pcap_file()
│       ├── container.rs               # PCAP/PCAPNG magic detection, 8-linktype normalization & FCS strip
│       ├── topology.rs                # Deterministic host1, host2 discovery, dominant MACs & arrow locking
│       ├── oracle.rs                  # Per-packet self-checking forward-compiler oracle verification
│       ├── shadow_emit.rs             # 4-tuple shadow-state default elision & compile block emission
│       └── {l2,l3,l4,l7}/             # 81 protocol dissectors (l3/{ip,ipv6,icmpv6}.rs, l7/{snmp1,snmp2,snmp3}.rs)
├── docs/                              # 13 canonical Markdown guides
├── examples/                          # 2,611 verified strict-lowercase .fasm scenarios across 82 directories
└── tests/                             # 12 integration test suites including corpus_verification_tests.rs
```

### Core Architectural & DSL Design Invariants

1. **Strict `<layer>/<protocol>` Symmetry**: Every one of the 81 protocols maps 1-to-1 across `src/ast/<layer>/<protocol>.rs` (`*Spec` struct with strict-lowercase `/// Syntax mapping:` docstring), `src/parser/<layer>/<protocol>.rs` (`winnow` field combinator), `src/builders/<layer>/<protocol>.rs` (wire payload encoder), `src/reverse/<layer>/<protocol>.rs` (PCAP-to-`.fasm` decompiler), and `examples/<layer>/<protocol>/<protocol>_<scenario>.fasm` (`>= 30` verified scenarios per protocol).
2. **Zero Mandatory Sub-Keywords**: Every protocol compiles with zero sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers, EtherTypes, IP protocol numbers, and well-known ports) while exposing every AST `*Spec` field as an optional override (enforced by Gate 6 of `corpus_verification_tests`).
3. **1 Statement = 1 Frame & Shared 4-Tuple TCP State**: Each statement in a `flow` or inline in `compile` emits one Ethernet frame. TCP-based Layer 7 statements automatically emit `psh ack` (`0x18`) frames on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple sequence and acknowledgment counters with raw `tcp` statements on the same connection.
4. **Polymorphic Dual-Stack Flow Reuse**: A single `flow` executes identically over IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs without duplicating flow logic, while mixing IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same packet statement is rejected at compile time by `validate_semantics`.
5. **Six-Way Strict-Lowercase Grammar, Parser, IDE & WASM Lockstep**: Every strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` keyword token in `src/lexer/mod.rs` (zero `_`, zero `-`, zero `loop`) is synchronized across `src/parser/`, `grammar.ebnf`, `frameassembly.gbnf`, `frameassembly.lark`, `frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json`, and `frameassembly-wasm` (enforced by Gate 4 of `corpus_verification_tests`).

---

## 3. Using `frameassembly` as a Rust Library

In addition to the `frameassembly` CLI binary, the crate exposes its full compiler and decompiler pipelines as a library so Rust projects can synthesize deterministic network frames in memory for protocol parser unit tests, IDS/IPS engine benchmarks, or automated `.pcap` fixture generation.

### Public API Reference

| Function / Type | Signature & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`lexer::lex`](../src/lexer/mod.rs) | `pub fn lex<'a>(input: &'a str) -> Result<Vec<(Token<'a>, Range<usize>)>, CompilerError>` — Tokenizes `.fasm` source text into zero-copy strict-lowercase `Token<'a>` items paired with byte-offset ranges. |
| [`parser::parse_program`](../src/parser/mod.rs) | `pub fn parse_program<'a>(input_str: &'a str) -> Result<Program<'a>, CompilerError>` — Runs `lexer::lex`, parses the token stream into a `Program<'a>` AST, and automatically runs `validate_semantics`. |
| [`parser::validate_semantics`](../src/parser/validation.rs) | `pub fn validate_semantics(program: &Program, src: &str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>` — Validates symbol uniqueness, flow arity, `protocol_requires_ip`, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 homogeneity, numeric ranges, and modifier rules. |
| [`backend::compile_program`](../src/backend/mod.rs) | `pub fn compile_program(program: &Program) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` — Evaluates `compile` in memory, returning `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_nanos)` for each emitted frame. |
| [`backend::generate_pcap`](../src/backend/mod.rs) | `pub fn generate_pcap(program: &Program, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>` — Compiles `program` and writes a nanosecond-resolution PCAPNG capture file to `output_path`. |
| [`packet::build_wire_packet`](../src/packet.rs) | `pub fn build_wire_packet(...) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CompilerError>` — Low-level builder constructing a complete Ethernet/VLAN/QinQ/MPLS + IPv4/IPv6 + TCP/UDP frame with RFC 1071 checksums. |
| [`pcap::PcapWriter`](../src/pcap.rs) | `PcapWriter::create(path: &str)` & `writer.write_packet(packet_data: &[u8], ts_nanos_total: u64)` — Streaming PCAPNG writer initialized with `LINKTYPE_ETHERNET` and `IfTsResol(9)`. |
| [`reverse::reverse_pcap_reader`](../src/reverse/mod.rs) | `pub fn reverse_pcap_reader<R: std::io::Read>(reader: R) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>` — Decompiles a `.pcap` or `.pcapng` stream into canonical v2.0.0 `.fasm` code (`ReverseOutput { fasm, packet_count, host_count }`). |
| [`reverse::reverse_pcap_bytes`](../src/reverse/mod.rs) | `pub fn reverse_pcap_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>` — Decompiles an in-memory `.pcap` or `.pcapng` byte slice into canonical v2.0.0 `.fasm` code. |
| [`reverse::reverse_pcap_file`](../src/reverse/mod.rs) | `pub fn reverse_pcap_file(path: impl AsRef<std::path::Path>) -> Result<ReverseOutput, CompilerError>` — Decompiles a `.pcap` or `.pcapng` file on disk into canonical v2.0.0 `.fasm` code. |
| [`error::CompilerError`](../src/error.rs) | Structured diagnostic enum implementing `std::error::Error` and `miette::Diagnostic` with variants `LexError { src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::lex_error`), `ParseError { message: String, src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::parse_error`), `SemanticError { message: String, src: String, span: (usize, usize) }` (`frameassembly::semantic_error`), and `BackendError(String)` (`frameassembly::backend_error`). |

### Example 1: In-Memory Frame Synthesis & Byte-Offset Assertions

Use `parse_program` and `compile_program` in Rust integration tests to synthesize multi-frame conversations directly into `Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>` without touching the filesystem:

```rust
use frameassembly::backend::compile_program;
use frameassembly::parser::parse_program;

fn main() {
    let fasm = r#"
        host hmi { ip 192.168.10.5  mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e }
        host plc { ip 192.168.10.20 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5f }

        flow modbus_poll(c, s) {
            c -> s tcp syn srcport 50100 dstport 502 seq 1000 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
            c <- s tcp syn ack seq 2000 acknum 1001 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
            c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms
            c -> s modbus txid 1 unitid 1 readholdingregisters addr 100 count 4 wait 5ms
            c <- s modbus txid 1 unitid 1 readholdingregisters isresponse value 42 wait 5ms
        }

        compile {
            modbus_poll(hmi, plc)
        }
    "#;

    let program = parse_program(fasm).expect("valid v2.0.0 .fasm specification");
    let frames = compile_program(&program).expect("in-memory wire synthesis succeeds");

    // 5 statements -> 5 Ethernet frames
    assert_eq!(frames.len(), 5);

    // Verify Ethernet II EtherType is IPv4 (0x0800 at bytes 12..14)
    let (req_frame, req_ts_ns) = &frames[3];
    assert_eq!(&req_frame[12..14], &[0x08, 0x00]);

    // Verify TCP destination port is 502 (0x01F6 at bytes 36..38) and PSH|ACK (0x18 at byte 47)
    assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([req_frame[36], req_frame[37]]), 502);
    assert_eq!(req_frame[47], 0x18);

    // Verify nanosecond timestamp delta between frame 3 and frame 4 is 5ms (5,000,000 ns)
    let (resp_frame, resp_ts_ns) = &frames[4];
    assert_eq!(*resp_ts_ns - *req_ts_ns, 5_000_000);

    // Verify bidirectional port inheritance flipped ports on `c <- s` (src_port = 502, dst_port = 50100)
    assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([resp_frame[34], resp_frame[35]]), 502);
    assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([resp_frame[36], resp_frame[37]]), 50100);
}
```

### Example 2: Writing Deterministic `.pcap` Fixtures to Disk

```rust
use frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap;
use frameassembly::parser::parse_program;

fn write_dns_fixture(output_path: &str) {
    let fasm = r#"
        host stub_v6     { ip 2001:db8:10::5 }
        host resolver_v6 { ip 2001:4860:4860::8888 }

        flow dns_lookup(c, s) {
            c -> s dns query txid 0x1a2b qname "api.example.com" qtype "aaaa" wait 2ms
            c <- s dns response txid 0x1a2b qname "api.example.com" qtype "aaaa" rdata "2001:db8:99::80" ansttl 300 wait 5ms
        }

        compile {
            dns_lookup(stub_v6, resolver_v6)
        }
    "#;

    let program = parse_program(fasm).expect("valid dual-stack DNS specification");
    generate_pcap(&program, output_path).expect("PCAPNG written with IfTsResol(9)");
}
```

### Example 3: Inspecting Structured `miette` Diagnostics Programmatically

All front-end error variants carry the source string (`src`) and byte-offset tuple `span: (start_byte, byte_len)`, allowing callers to pattern-match on errors or render graphical terminal reports via `miette::GraphicalReportHandler`:

```rust
use frameassembly::error::CompilerError;
use frameassembly::parser::parse_program;

fn verify_mixed_ip_family_rejection() {
    let invalid_fasm = r#"
        host v4_node { ip 10.0.0.1 }
        host v6_node { ip 2001:db8::1 }
        flow mismatch(a, b) {
            a -> b icmp echorequest
        }
        compile {
            mismatch(v4_node, v6_node)
        }
    "#;

    let err = parse_program(invalid_fasm).expect_err("mixed IPv4/IPv6 endpoints must fail");
    match err {
        CompilerError::SemanticError { message, span, .. } => {
            assert!(message.contains("Mixed IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints"));
            assert!(span.1 > 0);
        }
        other => panic!("Expected SemanticError, got: {:?}", other),
    }
}
```

## 4. Formal Grammars, Constrained LLM Decoding & RLVR Architecture

Because `.fasm` v2.0.0 is a compact, non-Turing-complete specification language with strict-lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` built-in keywords and zero mandatory protocol sub-keywords, it is directly suited for **constrained LLM decoding** (guaranteed 100% syntactically valid generation) and **Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)**.

### Six-Way Grammar, Lexer, IDE & WASM Lockstep

FrameAssembly maintains six grammar, IDE, and WASM artifacts in strict automated lockstep verified by Gate 4 of `tests/corpus_verification_tests.rs` (which checks that all `646` strict-lowercase `#[token("...")]` literals in `src/lexer/mod.rs` exist in every grammar with zero `_`, zero `-`, and zero `loop`, and that every RHS non-terminal resolves to a defined LHS rule):

| Artifact | Format | Target Inference Engines & Tooling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`src/lexer/mod.rs`](../src/lexer/mod.rs) | Rust `logos 0.14.4` DFA | Authoritative strict-lowercase compiler token vocabulary (`Token<'a>`) |
| [`grammar.ebnf`](../grammar.ebnf) | ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF | Canonical human and compiler context-free grammar specification |
| [`frameassembly.gbnf`](../frameassembly.gbnf) | GGML BNF (`GBNF`) | `llama.cpp` (`--grammar-file`), `MLC-LLM`, `XGrammar`, `KoboldCpp`, `TabbyAPI` |
| [`frameassembly.lark`](../frameassembly.lark) | Lark Earley / LALR | `Outlines`, `vLLM` (`guided_grammar`), `SGLang`, `Guidance`, `llguidance` |
| [`frameassembly.tmLanguage.json`](../frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json) | TextMate JSON (`source.frameassembly`) | VS Code (`frameassembly-vscode`), VSCodium, Cursor, Windsurf, and GitHub/Shiki |
| [`frameassembly-wasm/src/lib.rs`](../frameassembly-wasm/src/lib.rs) | WebAssembly (`wasm-bindgen`) | In-browser compiler (`compile_fasm_to_pcapng`), decompiler (`reverse_pcap`), packet inspector (`inspect_fasm`), and UTF-16 IDE diagnostics (`validate_fasm`) |

### Core v2.0.0 Grammar Productions (`EBNF` / `GBNF` / `Lark`)

All three context-free grammars enforce strict-lowercase `host`, `flow`, and `compile` blocks, flexible user identifiers, and `run_statement = flow_invocation | frame_statement` (`loop` removed):

```ebnf
(* ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF excerpt — grammar.ebnf *)
program          = { top_level_decl } , compile_block , { top_level_decl } ;
top_level_decl   = host_declaration | flow_declaration ;
host_declaration = "host" , identifier , "{" , host_property , { host_property } , "}" ;
host_property    = ( "ip" , ip_address ) | ( "mac" , mac_address ) ;
flow_declaration = "flow" , identifier , "(" , [ param_list ] , ")" , "{" , { frame_statement } , "}" ;
frame_statement  = endpoint , ( "->" | "<-" ) , endpoint , { frame_field } ;
compile_block    = "compile" , "{" , { run_statement } , "}" ;
run_statement    = flow_invocation | frame_statement ;
```

```bnf
# GGML BNF excerpt — frameassembly.gbnf
root ::= ws (host-decl | flow-decl)* compile-block (host-decl | flow-decl)* ws
host-decl ::= "host" ws1 ident ws "{" ws host-prop+ "}" ws
host-prop ::= ("ip" ws1 ip-addr | "mac" ws1 mac-addr) ws
flow-decl ::= "flow" ws1 ident ws "(" ws param-list? ")" ws "{" ws frame-stmt* "}" ws
compile-block ::= "compile" ws "{" ws run-stmt* "}" ws
run-stmt ::= flow-call | frame-stmt
```

```lark
// Earley / LALR Lark excerpt — frameassembly.lark
start: top_level_decl* compile_block top_level_decl*
top_level_decl: host_decl | flow_decl
host_decl: "host" ident "{" host_prop+ "}"
host_prop: "ip" ip_addr | "mac" MAC_ADDR
flow_decl: "flow" ident "(" param_list? ")" "{" frame_stmt* "}"
compile_block: "compile" "{" run_stmt* "}"
run_stmt: flow_call | frame_stmt
```

### Constrained Decoding with `llama.cpp` (`frameassembly.gbnf`)

Pass `--grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf` to `llama-cli` or `llama-server` to mask out invalid token logits at every decoding step, then compile the generated `.fasm` directly with the default `frameassembly` command:

```bash
llama-cli \
  -m qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct-q8_0.gguf \
  --grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf \
  -p "Write a FrameAssembly v2.0.0 (.fasm) program that performs a TCP 3-way handshake between 10.0.0.1 and 10.0.0.2 on port 443 and sends a TLS clienthello with sni 'secure.example.com'." \
  > generated.fasm && frameassembly generated.fasm synthesized.pcap
```

### Constrained Decoding with Python `Outlines` / `vLLM` (`frameassembly.lark`)

Use `frameassembly.lark` with `outlines` or `vLLM` structured outputs to guarantee valid v2.0.0 `.fasm` generation from Python inference pipelines:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import outlines

lark_grammar = Path("frameassembly.lark").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
model = outlines.models.transformers("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct")
generator = outlines.generate.cfg(model, lark_grammar)

fasm_code = generator(
    "Generate a FrameAssembly v2.0.0 (.fasm) specification for a bgp open and keepalive "
    "session between peer_a (10.0.0.1, asn 65001) and peer_b (10.0.0.2, asn 65002)."
)
```

### Four-Stage Hierarchical Verifiable Compiler Reward (RLVR / GRPO)

Because `frameassembly` compiles in microseconds in pure memory without `libpcap` or network interfaces, the Rust library serves directly as a dense, deterministic reward oracle $R(x, y) \in [0.0, 1.0]$ for GRPO / PPO post-training:

1. **Stage 1 — Lexical Validity ($R = 0.15$, $+0.15$)**: `frameassembly::lexer::lex(candidate)` succeeds with zero `LexError` tokens.
2. **Stage 2 — Syntactic AST Validity ($R = 0.40$, $+0.25$)**: `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(candidate)` constructs a syntactically valid `Program<'a>` AST (`host` + optional `flow` + `compile`).
3. **Stage 3 — Semantic Validity ($R = 0.70$, $+0.30$)**: `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics(&program, candidate)` passes symbol resolution, flow arity, field range, `protocol_requires_ip`, and dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 homogeneity checks.
4. **Stage 4 — Wire, PCAPNG & Reverse Decompiler Oracle ($R = 1.00$, $+0.30$)**: `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(&program)` emits deterministic Ethernet frames with valid RFC checksums (IPv4 header, TCP/UDP pseudo-header, ICMP/ICMPv6, SCTP CRC-32c, DNP3 CRC-16) and round-trips through `frameassembly::reverse::reverse_pcap_bytes`.

```rust
use frameassembly::backend::compile_program;
use frameassembly::error::CompilerError;
use frameassembly::lexer::lex;
use frameassembly::parser::parse_program;

/// Computes a dense 4-stage verifiable reward in [0.0, 1.0] for an LLM-generated `.fasm` candidate.
pub fn compute_rlvr_reward(candidate_fasm: &str) -> f64 {
    if lex(candidate_fasm).is_err() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let mut reward = 0.15; // Stage 1 passed (R = 0.15): 100% valid strict-lowercase lexical tokens

    // parse_program runs both syntactic parsing (Stage 2) and validate_semantics (Stage 3)
    match parse_program(candidate_fasm) {
        Ok(program) => {
            reward += 0.55; // Stage 2 (+0.25 -> R = 0.40) + Stage 3 (+0.30 -> R = 0.70) passed
            if let Ok(frames) = compile_program(&program)
                && !frames.is_empty()
                && frames.iter().all(|(bytes, _)| bytes.len() >= 14)
            {
                reward += 0.30; // Stage 4 passed (R = 1.00): valid wire frames synthesized
            }
        }
        Err(CompilerError::SemanticError { .. }) => {
            reward += 0.25; // Stage 2 passed (R = 0.40, syntactically valid AST), failed Stage 3 semantics
        }
        Err(_) => {}
    }
    reward
}
```
