## `src/ast/l3/ndp.rs`

```rust
//! IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP, RFC 4861) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines link-local IPv6 address resolution, Neighbor Unreachability Detection (NUD), Duplicate
//! Address Detection (DAD), and Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC) router discovery messages
//! specified in RFC 4861 over ICMPv6 (Next Header `58`, Hop Limit `255`). Supports `routersolicit`
//! (Type `133`), `routeradvert` (Type `134`, carrying `routerlifetime`), `neighborsolicit` (Type
//! `135`, automatically computing the Solicited-Node Multicast destination `ff02::1:ffXX:XXXX` and
//! attaching Option 1 Source Link-Layer Address `slla`), `neighboradvert` (Type `136`, setting
//! Solicited + Override flags `0x60` and Option 2 Target Link-Layer Address `tlla`), and `redirect` (`137`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b ndp [routersolicit | routeradvert | neighborsolicit | neighboradvert | redirect] [target <ipv6>] [slla <mac>] [tlla <mac>] [routerlifetime <u16>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// RFC 4861 IPv6 Neighbor Discovery ICMPv6 message type code.
#[doc(alias = "NdpMessageType")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NdpType {
    /// Router Solicitation (`routersolicit`, ICMPv6 Type `133`, sent to all-routers `ff02::2`).
    RouterSolicit,
    /// Router Advertisement (`routeradvert`, ICMPv6 Type `134`, periodic or solicited SLAAC beacon).
    RouterAdvert,
    /// Neighbor Solicitation (`neighborsolicit`, ICMPv6 Type `135`, resolves link-layer address or performs DAD).
    NeighborSolicit,
    /// Neighbor Advertisement (`neighboradvert`, ICMPv6 Type `136`, supplies Target Link-Layer Address).
    NeighborAdvert,
    /// Redirect (`redirect`, ICMPv6 Type `137`, informs host of a better first-hop router).
    Redirect,
}

/// IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (RFC 4861) specification over ICMPv6 (`58`).
///
/// Syntax mapping: `ndp [routersolicit | routeradvert | neighborsolicit | neighboradvert | redirect] [target <ipv6>] [slla <mac>] [tlla <mac>] [routerlifetime <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "ndp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 4861")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC4861")]
#[doc(alias = "SLAAC")]
#[doc(alias = "ICMPv6")]
#[doc(alias = "routersolicit")]
#[doc(alias = "routeradvert")]
#[doc(alias = "neighborsolicit")]
#[doc(alias = "neighboradvert")]
#[doc(alias = "redirect")]
#[doc(alias = "target")]
#[doc(alias = "slla")]
#[doc(alias = "tlla")]
#[doc(alias = "routerlifetime")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct NdpSpec<'a> {
    /// NDP message type (`neighborsolicit`, `neighboradvert`, `routersolicit`, `routeradvert`, `redirect`; default `neighborsolicit`).
    pub ndp_type: Option<NdpType>,
    /// 128-bit Target IPv6 address for Neighbor Solicitation, Neighbor Advertisement, or Redirect (`target <ipv6>`).
    pub target: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 48-bit Source Link-Layer Address NDP Option 1 override (`slla <mac>`).
    pub slla: Option<[u8; 6]>,
    /// 48-bit Target Link-Layer Address NDP Option 2 override (`tlla <mac>`).
    pub tlla: Option<[u8; 6]>,
    /// 16-bit Router Lifetime in seconds for Router Advertisements (`routerlifetime <u16>`, default `1800`).
    pub router_lifetime: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l3/openflow.rs`

```rust
//! OpenFlow Switch Protocol (ONF OpenFlow v1.0–v1.5) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines Software-Defined Networking (SDN) Southbound control channel messages exchanged between an
//! OpenFlow controller and an OpenFlow-enabled switch over TCP port `6653` (IANA standard) or `6633`.
//! Every OpenFlow message starts with an 8-byte `ofp_header` comprising an 8-bit `version` (`version`,
//! default `4` for OpenFlow 1.3), an 8-bit `type` code (`hello` `0`, `echoreq` `2`, `echoreply` `3`,
//! `featuresreq` `5`, `featuresreply` `6`, `packetin` `10`, `packetout` `13`, `flowmod` `14`), a
//! 16-bit total message `length`, and a 32-bit transaction identifier `xid` (`xid`), optionally
//! accompanied by Datapath ID (`dpid`), flow `tableid`, and flow rule `priority` attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b openflow [hello | echoreq | echoreply | featuresreq | featuresreply | packetin | packetout | flowmod] [version <u8>] [xid <u32>] [dpid <u64>] [tableid <u8>] [priority <u16>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// ONF OpenFlow Switch Protocol `ofp_type` message classification.
#[doc(alias = "OfpType")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OpenflowType {
    /// `OFPT_HELLO` (`0`): Symmetric connection startup version negotiation message.
    Hello,
    /// `OFPT_ECHO_REQUEST` (`2`): Symmetric control channel liveness probe request.
    EchoReq,
    /// `OFPT_ECHO_REPLY` (`3`): Symmetric control channel liveness probe response.
    EchoReply,
    /// `OFPT_FEATURES_REQUEST` (`5`): Controller request querying switch datapath capabilities (`dpid`).
    FeaturesReq,
    /// `OFPT_FEATURES_REPLY` (`6`): Switch response advertising `datapath_id` and supported tables/ports.
    FeaturesReply,
    /// `OFPT_PACKET_IN` (`10`): Asynchronous switch-to-controller punt of a table-miss or controller-action packet.
    PacketIn,
    /// `OFPT_FLOW_MOD` (`14`): Controller-to-switch command installing, modifying, or deleting a flow table entry.
    FlowMod,
    /// `OFPT_PACKET_OUT` (`13`): Controller-to-switch command injecting a raw frame out a switch port.
    PacketOut,
}

/// OpenFlow Switch Protocol (ONF v1.3+) specification over TCP port `6653`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `openflow [hello | echoreq | echoreply | featuresreq | featuresreply | packetin | packetout | flowmod] [version <u8>] [xid <u32>] [dpid <u64>] [tableid <u8>] [priority <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "openflow")]
#[doc(alias = "OpenFlow")]
#[doc(alias = "SDN")]
#[doc(alias = "6653")]
#[doc(alias = "ofp_header")]
#[doc(alias = "hello")]
#[doc(alias = "echoreq")]
#[doc(alias = "echoreply")]
#[doc(alias = "featuresreq")]
#[doc(alias = "featuresreply")]
#[doc(alias = "packetin")]
#[doc(alias = "packetout")]
#[doc(alias = "flowmod")]
#[doc(alias = "version")]
#[doc(alias = "xid")]
#[doc(alias = "dpid")]
#[doc(alias = "tableid")]
#[doc(alias = "priority")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct OpenflowSpec<'a> {
    /// OpenFlow wire protocol version (`version <u8>`, e.g. `1` = OF 1.0, `4` = OF 1.3, `5` = OF 1.4; default `4`).
    pub version: Option<u8>,
    /// OpenFlow message type (`hello`, `echoreq`, `echoreply`, `featuresreq`, `featuresreply`, `packetin`, `flowmod`, `packetout`; default `hello`).
    pub of_type: Option<OpenflowType>,
    /// 32-bit Transaction ID correlating requests and replies (`xid <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub xid: Option<u32>,
    /// 64-bit switch Datapath Identifier (`dpid <u64>`).
    pub dpid: Option<u64>,
    /// 8-bit pipeline Flow Table Identifier (`tableid <u8>`).

    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.

}

## `src/ast/l3/ospf.rs`

```rust
//! Open Shortest Path First (OSPFv2 RFC 2328 / OSPFv3 RFC 5340) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines link-state Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) control packets transmitted directly over IP
//! protocol `89` (`0x59`) to multicast AllSPFRouters (`224.0.0.5` for IPv4, `ff02::5` for IPv6).
//! The 24-byte OSPF header encodes `Version` (`2`), `Type` (`1` `hello`, `2` `dbd`, `3` `lsr`, `4`
//! `lsu`, `5` `lsack`), 16-bit `Packet Length`, 32-bit `Router ID` (`routerid`), 32-bit `Area ID`
//! (`areaid`, default `0` backbone `0.0.0.0`), 16-bit Checksum, `AuType`, and 64-bit Authentication,
//! followed by a 20-byte Hello body specifying `Network Mask`, `HelloInterval` (`hellointerval`,
//! default `10`s), `Options`, `Rtr Pri` (`priority`, default `1`), and `RouterDeadInterval` (`deadinterval`, default `40`s).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b ospf [hello | dbd | lsr | lsu | lsack] [routerid <ipv4>] [areaid <u32>] [hellointerval <u16>] [deadinterval <u32>] [priority <u8>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// RFC 2328 / RFC 5340 OSPF packet type code.
#[doc(alias = "OspfPacketType")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OspfType {
    /// Type `1` (`hello`): Discovers and maintains neighbor adjacencies and elects DR/BDR on broadcast links.
    Hello,
    /// Type `2` (`dbd`): Database Description packet exchanging link-state database summary headers.
    Dbd,
    /// Type `3` (`lsr`): Link State Request querying specific LSA records from a neighbor.
    Lsr,
    /// Type `4` (`lsu`): Link State Update flooding full LSA instances across the OSPF area.
    Lsu,
    /// Type `5` (`lsack`): Link State Acknowledgment confirming reliable receipt of flooded LSAs.
    LsAck,
}

/// Open Shortest Path First (RFC 2328 OSPFv2 / RFC 5340 OSPFv3) specification over IP protocol `89`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `ospf [hello | dbd | lsr | lsu | lsack] [routerid <ipv4>] [areaid <u32>] [hellointerval <u16>] [deadinterval <u32>] [priority <u8>]`
#[doc(alias = "ospf")]
#[doc(alias = "OSPFv2")]
#[doc(alias = "OSPFv3")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 2328")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC2328")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 5340")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC5340")]
#[doc(alias = "hello")]
#[doc(alias = "dbd")]
#[doc(alias = "lsr")]
#[doc(alias = "lsu")]
#[doc(alias = "lsack")]
#[doc(alias = "routerid")]
#[doc(alias = "areaid")]
#[doc(alias = "hellointerval")]
#[doc(alias = "deadinterval")]
#[doc(alias = "priority")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct OspfSpec<'a> {
    /// OSPF packet type (`hello`, `dbd`, `lsr`, `lsu`, or `lsack`; default `hello`).
    pub ospf_type: Option<OspfType>,
    /// 32-bit OSPF Router ID formatted as an IPv4 address (`routerid <ipv4>`).
    pub router_id: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 32-bit OSPF Area ID (`areaid <u32>`, default `0` for Area `0.0.0.0`).
    pub area_id: Option<u32>,
    /// 16-bit Hello Interval in seconds (`hellointerval <u16>`, default `10`).
    pub hello_interval: Option<u16>,
    /// 32-bit Router Dead Interval in seconds (`deadinterval <u32>`, default `40`).
    pub dead_interval: Option<u32>,
    /// 8-bit Designated Router election Priority (`priority <u8>`, default `1`; `0` = ineligible).
    pub priority: Option<u8>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l3/pim.rs`

```rust
//! Protocol Independent Multicast - Sparse Mode (PIM-SM, RFC 7761) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines multicast distribution tree control messages specified in RFC 7761 (obsoleting RFC 4601)
//! and transmitted directly over IP protocol `103` (`0x67`) to the All-PIM-Routers link-local
//! multicast address (`224.0.0.13` for IPv4, `ff02::d` for IPv6) or unicast to a Rendezvous Point
//! (`rp`). The 4-byte PIMv2 header encodes a 4-bit `PIM Ver` (`2`), a 4-bit `Type` (`0` `hello`,
//! `1` `register`, `3` `joinprune`), an 8-bit `Reserved` byte, and a 16-bit ones'-complement
//! `Checksum`, followed by TLV options (`Option 1` `holdtime` default `105`s, `Option 19` `drpriority`
//! default `1`) and multicast tree `(S, G)` or `(*, G)` state (`source`, `group`, `rp`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b pim [hello | joinprune | register] [holdtime <u16>] [drpriority <u32>] [group <ip>] [source <ip>] [rp <ip>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// Protocol Independent Multicast Sparse Mode (RFC 7761) specification over IP protocol `103`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `pim [hello | joinprune | register] [holdtime <u16>] [drpriority <u32>] [group <ip>] [source <ip>] [rp <ip>]`
#[doc(alias = "pim")]
#[doc(alias = "PIM-SM")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 7761")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC7761")]
#[doc(alias = "103")]
#[doc(alias = "hello")]
#[doc(alias = "joinprune")]
#[doc(alias = "register")]
#[doc(alias = "holdtime")]
#[doc(alias = "drpriority")]
#[doc(alias = "group")]
#[doc(alias = "source")]
#[doc(alias = "rp")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct PimSpec<'a> {
    /// Indicates a PIMv2 `hello` neighbor discovery and DR election message (`hello`).
    pub is_hello: bool,
    /// Indicates a PIMv2 `joinprune` shared-tree `(*,G)` or shortest-path-tree `(S,G)` control message (`joinprune`).
    pub is_join_prune: bool,
    /// Indicates a PIMv2 `register` unicast first-hop DR-to-RP multicast data encapsulation message (`register`).
    pub is_register: bool,
    /// Multicast Group IPv4 or IPv6 address (`group <ip>`).
    pub group: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Multicast Source IPv4 or IPv6 address for `(S,G)` SPT state (`source <ip>`).
    pub source: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Rendezvous Point IPv4 or IPv6 address for `(*,G)` shared tree state (`rp <ip>`).
    pub rp: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 16-bit PIM Hello Option 1 Holdtime in seconds (`holdtime <u16>`, default `105`).
    pub holdtime: Option<u16>,
    /// 32-bit PIM Hello Option 19 Designated Router Priority (`drpriority <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub dr_priority: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l3/rip.rs`

```rust
//! Routing Information Protocol (RIPv2 RFC 2453 / RIPng RFC 2080) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines distance-vector Interior Gateway Protocol route table request and advertisement messages
//! specified in RFC 2453 (RIPv2 over UDP port `520` to multicast `224.0.0.9`) and RFC 2080 (RIPng
//! for IPv6 over UDP port `521` to multicast `ff02::9`). A 24-byte RIPv2 packet consists of a 4-byte
//! header (`Command`: `1` `request` or `2` `response`, `Version`: `2`, 16-bit `Must Be Zero`) followed
//! by one or more 20-byte Route Table Entries (RTEs) encoding `Address Family Identifier` (`2`), 16-bit
//! `Route Tag` (`tag`), 32-bit `IP Address` (`prefix`), 32-bit `Subnet Mask` (`255.255.255.0`), 32-bit
//! `Next Hop` (`nexthop`), and 32-bit hop-count `Metric` (`metric`, `1..=16` where `16` = infinity).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b rip [request | response] [prefix <ip>] [metric <1..16>] [nexthop <ip>] [tag <u16>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// RFC 2453 / RFC 2080 RIP message command code.
#[doc(alias = "RipCommandType")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RipCommand {
    /// Command `1` (`request`): Queries a neighboring router for all or part of its RIP routing table.
    Request,
    /// Command `2` (`response`): Periodic, solicited, or triggered advertisement containing Route Table Entries.
    Response,
}

/// Routing Information Protocol (RFC 2453 RIPv2 / RFC 2080 RIPng) specification over UDP `520` / `521`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `rip [request | response] [prefix <ip>] [metric <1..16>] [nexthop <ip>] [tag <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "rip")]
#[doc(alias = "RIPv2")]
#[doc(alias = "RIPng")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 2453")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC2453")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 2080")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC2080")]
#[doc(alias = "request")]
#[doc(alias = "response")]
#[doc(alias = "prefix")]
#[doc(alias = "metric")]
#[doc(alias = "nexthop")]
#[doc(alias = "tag")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct RipSpec<'a> {
    /// RIP Command code (`request` `1` or `response` `2`; default `response`).
    pub command: Option<RipCommand>,
    /// Advertised destination network prefix IP address (`prefix <ip>`, default `10.0.0.0`).
    pub prefix: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 32-bit Bellmann-Ford hop count metric (`metric <1..=16>`, default `1`; `16` indicates unreachable / poison reverse).
    pub metric: Option<u32>,
    /// Immediate Next-Hop router IP address (`nexthop <ip>`, default `0.0.0.0` meaning the advertising router).
    pub nexthop: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 16-bit external route redistribution Tag (`tag <u16>`, default `0`, often carrying an external BGP/OSPF ASN).
    pub tag: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l3/vrrp.rs`

```rust
//! Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRPv3 RFC 5798 / VRRPv2 RFC 3768) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines the standards-based First Hop Redundancy Protocol (FHRP) advertisement packet specified
//! in RFC 5798 (VRRPv3 for IPv4 and IPv6) and RFC 3768 (VRRPv2) transmitted directly over IP protocol
//! `112` (`0x70`) with `TTL = 255` to multicast `224.0.0.18` (IPv4) or `ff02::12` (IPv6). The VRRPv3
//! wire header packs a 4-bit `Version` (`3`), a 4-bit `Type` (`1` Advertisement), an 8-bit Virtual
//! Router Identifier (`vrid`, `1..=255`), an 8-bit election `Priority` (`priority`, `1..=254`, `255`
//! for IP address owner), an 8-bit `Count IPvX Addr` (`1`), a 12-bit `Max Adver Int` in centiseconds
//! (`advint`, default `100` = 1.0s), a 16-bit Checksum, and the Virtual IP address (`vip`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b vrrp [vrid <1..255>] [priority <0..255>] [advint <u16>] [vip <ip>] [version <2|3>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (RFC 5798 VRRPv3 / RFC 3768 VRRPv2) specification over IP protocol `112`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `vrrp [vrid <1..255>] [priority <0..255>] [advint <u16>] [vip <ip>] [version <2|3>]`
#[doc(alias = "vrrp")]
#[doc(alias = "VRRPv3")]
#[doc(alias = "VRRPv2")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 5798")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC5798")]
#[doc(alias = "112")]
#[doc(alias = "vrid")]
#[doc(alias = "priority")]
#[doc(alias = "advint")]
#[doc(alias = "vip")]
#[doc(alias = "version")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct VrrpSpec<'a> {
    /// 8-bit Virtual Router Identifier (`vrid <1..=255>`, default `1`).
    pub vrid: Option<u8>,
    /// 8-bit Master election Priority (`priority <0..=255>`, default `100`; `255` = VIP owner, `0` = Master release).
    pub priority: Option<u8>,
    /// 12-bit Maximum Advertisement Interval in centiseconds for VRRPv3 (`advint <u16>`, default `100` = 1.00s).
    pub adv_int: Option<u16>,
    /// Virtual IPv4 or IPv6 gateway address protected by the VRRP group (`vip <ip>`).
    pub vip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// VRRP protocol version (`version <2|3>`, default `3`).
    pub version: Option<u8>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

//! Virtual eXtensible Local Area Network (VXLAN, RFC 7348) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines the Layer 2-over-UDP network virtualization overlay encapsulation specified in RFC 7348
//! for multi-tenant cloud data centers and BGP EVPN (RFC 7432 / RFC 8365) Spine-Leaf fabrics. VXLAN
//! Tunnel Endpoints (VTEPs) encapsulate inner IEEE 802.3 Ethernet frames inside an 8-byte VXLAN header
//! carried over UDP destination port `4789` (with ECMP entropy hashed into the outer UDP source port).
//! The 8-byte VXLAN wire header consists of an 8-bit `Flags` byte (`0x08`, where bit 4 is the mandatory
//! `I` flag indicating a valid VNI), 24 bits of `Reserved` zeros, a 24-bit VXLAN Network Identifier
//! (`vni`, `0..=16_777_215`, default `4096`), and a trailing 8-bit `Reserved` zero field.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b vxlan [vni <u24>] [srcport <u16>] [payload "<str>" | hexpayload "<hex>"]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// Syntax mapping: `vxlan [vni <0..16777215>]`
#[doc(alias = "vxlan")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 7348")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC7348")]
#[doc(alias = "VTEP")]
#[doc(alias = "EVPN")]
#[doc(alias = "4789")]
#[doc(alias = "vni")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct VxlanSpec<'a> {
    /// 24-bit VXLAN Network Identifier (`vni <0..=16_777_215>` or `vnid`, default `4096`).
    pub vni: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l3/wireguard.rs`

```rust
//! WireGuard Next-Generation Secure Network Tunnel (`Noise_IKpsk2`) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines the modern cryptographic VPN protocol designed by Jason A. Donenfeld and carried over
//! UDP port `51820`. WireGuard combines the `Noise_IKpsk2` handshake framework (Curve25519 ECDH,
//! BLAKE2s hashing, HKDF, and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD) with four fixed-layout little-endian message
//! types: Type `1` Handshake `initiation` (`148` bytes, carrying `sender_index`, 32B ephemeral key,
//! 48B encrypted static key, 28B encrypted TAI64N timestamp, and two 16B BLAKE2s MACs), Type `2`
//! Handshake `response` (`92` bytes, carrying `sender_index` and `receiver_index`), Type `3` `cookie`
//! Reply (`64` bytes, carrying `receiver_index`, 24B XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce, and 32B encrypted cookie
//! for DoS mitigation), and Type `4` Transport `data` (`16`B header with `receiver_index` and 64-bit `counter`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b wireguard [type <initiation|response|cookie|data> | initiation | cookie | data] [sender <u32>] [receiver <u32>] [counter <u64>] [payload "<str>" | hexpayload "<hex>"]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// WireGuard protocol message type (`1..=4`).
#[doc(alias = "WgMessageType")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WireguardType {
    /// Type `1` (`initiation`): 148-byte `Noise_IKpsk2` Handshake Initiation message.
    Initiation,
    /// Type `2` (`response`): 92-byte `Noise_IKpsk2` Handshake Response message.
    Response,
    /// Type `3` (`cookie`): 64-byte Cookie Reply message mitigating stateless CPU-exhaustion DoS attacks.
    Cookie,
    /// Type `4` (`data`): ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated transport data frame with a 64-bit anti-replay counter.
    Data,
}

/// WireGuard cryptographic VPN tunnel specification over UDP port `51820`.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `wireguard [type <initiation|response|cookie|data> | initiation | cookie | data] [sender <u32>] [receiver <u32>] [counter <u64>]`
#[doc(alias = "wireguard")]
#[doc(alias = "WireGuard")]
#[doc(alias = "Noise_IK")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 8439")]
#[doc(alias = "51820")]
#[doc(alias = "ChaCha20Poly1305")]
#[doc(alias = "initiation")]
#[doc(alias = "response")]
#[doc(alias = "cookie")]
#[doc(alias = "data")]
#[doc(alias = "sender")]
#[doc(alias = "receiver")]
#[doc(alias = "counter")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct WireguardSpec<'a> {
    /// WireGuard packet type (`initiation` `1`, `response` `2`, `cookie` `3`, or `data` `4`; default `initiation`).
    pub msg_type: Option<WireguardType>,
    /// 32-bit little-endian Sender session index (`sender <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub sender: Option<u32>,
    /// 32-bit little-endian Receiver session index (`receiver <u32>`, default `1` or `2`).
    pub receiver: Option<u32>,
    /// 64-bit little-endian ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce / anti-replay packet counter for `data` frames (`counter <u64>`, default `0`).
    pub counter: Option<u64>,
    /// Optional lifetime phantom marker for AST uniformity.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l4/sctp.rs`

```rust
//! Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP, RFC 9260 / RFC 4960) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines the abstract syntax tree parameters for RFC 9260 Stream Control Transmission Protocol
//! packets encapsulated directly over IPv4 or IPv6 using IP Protocol number `132` (`0x84`).
//! Every SCTP packet begins with a 12-byte Common Header containing the 16-bit Source Port,
//! 16-bit Destination Port, 32-bit Verification Tag (`vtag`), and 32-bit little-endian
//! Castagnoli CRC32c checksum, followed by one or more 32-bit aligned Chunks (`data`, `init`,
//! `initack`, `sack`, `heartbeat`, `heartbeatack`, `abort`, `shutdown`, `shutdownack`, `cookieecho`, `cookieack`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b sctp [chunk <type>] [vtag <u32>] [stream <u16>] [ssn <u16>] [ppid <u32>] [srcport <u16>] [dstport <u16>]`

use alloc::string::String;

/// Stream Control Transmission Protocol (RFC 9260) association and chunk parameters specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `sctp [chunk <data|init|initack|sack|heartbeat|heartbeatack|abort|shutdown|shutdownack|cookieecho|cookieack>] [vtag <u32>] [stream <u16>] [ssn <u16>] [ppid <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "sctp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9260")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9260")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 4960")]
#[doc(alias = "proto 132")]
#[doc(alias = "SctpSpec")]
#[doc(alias = "chunk")]
#[doc(alias = "vtag")]
#[doc(alias = "stream")]
#[doc(alias = "ssn")]
#[doc(alias = "ppid")]
#[doc(alias = "init")]
#[doc(alias = "initack")]
#[doc(alias = "sack")]
#[doc(alias = "heartbeat")]
#[doc(alias = "shutdownack")]
#[doc(alias = "cookieecho")]
#[doc(alias = "cookieack")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct SctpParams {
    /// 32-bit Verification Tag (`vtag <u32>`) authenticating the SCTP association in the Common Header.
    pub vtag: Option<u32>,
    /// 16-bit Stream Identifier (`stream <u16>`) inside an SCTP `data` chunk header.
    pub stream: Option<u16>,
    /// 16-bit Stream Sequence Number (`ssn <u16>`) for ordered delivery within a stream.
    pub ssn: Option<u16>,
    /// 32-bit Payload Protocol Identifier (`ppid <u32>`, e.g., `60` for 5G NGAP, `18` for LTE S1AP, `3` for M3UA).
    pub ppid: Option<u32>,
    /// SCTP Chunk Type name (`chunk <name>`, e.g., `"INIT"`, `"INIT_ACK"`, `"COOKIE_ECHO"`, `"COOKIE_ACK"`, `"DATA"`, `"SACK"`, `"SHUTDOWN_ACK"`).
    pub chunk: Option<String>,
}

/// Type alias for Stream Control Transmission Protocol (RFC 9260) specification ([`SctpParams`]).
///
/// Syntax mapping: `sctp [chunk <data|init|initack|sack|heartbeat|heartbeatack|abort|shutdown|shutdownack|cookieecho|cookieack>] [vtag <u32>] [stream <u16>] [ssn <u16>] [ppid <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "sctp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9260")]
#[doc(alias = "chunk")]
#[doc(alias = "vtag")]
#[doc(alias = "stream")]
#[doc(alias = "ssn")]
#[doc(alias = "ppid")]
pub type SctpSpec = SctpParams;
```

## `src/ast/l4/tcp.rs`

```rust
//! Transmission Control Protocol (TCP, RFC 9293 / RFC 7323) AST definitions.
//!
//! Defines the control flags and header options for RFC 9293 Transmission Control Protocol
//! segments encapsulated over IPv4 or IPv6 using IP Protocol number `6`. The 20-byte base TCP
//! header contains 16-bit Source and Destination Ports, 32-bit Sequence Number (`seq`), 32-bit
//! Acknowledgment Number (`acknum`), 4-bit Data Offset, 8-bit Control Flags (`cwr`, `ece`,
//! `urg`, `ack`, `psh`, `rst`, `syn`, `fin`), 16-bit Window Size (`win`), 16-bit Checksum,
//! and 16-bit Urgent Pointer (`urgent`), followed by 32-bit padded TLV options (`mss`, `wscale`,
//! `sackperm`, `tsval`, `tsecr`).
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b tcp [syn] [ack] [fin] [rst] [psh] [urg] [ece] [cwr] [srcport <u16>] [dstport <u16>] [seq <u32>] [acknum <u32>] [win <u16>] [mss <u16>] [wscale <u8>] [sackperm] [tsval <u32>] [tsecr <u32>]`

/// TCP 8-bit control flags in byte 13 of the RFC 9293 TCP header (`cwr`, `ece`, `urg`, `ack`, `psh`, `rst`, `syn`, `fin`).
///
/// Syntax mapping: `tcp [syn] [ack] [fin] [rst] [psh] [urg] [ece] [cwr]`
///
/// # Examples
/// ```rust
/// use frameassembly::ast::TcpFlag;
/// let flag = TcpFlag::Syn;
/// ```
#[doc(alias = "tcp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9293")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 3168")]
#[doc(alias = "syn")]
#[doc(alias = "ack")]
#[doc(alias = "fin")]
#[doc(alias = "rst")]
#[doc(alias = "psh")]
#[doc(alias = "urg")]
#[doc(alias = "ece")]
#[doc(alias = "cwr")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum TcpFlag {
    /// Synchronize sequence numbers (`syn`, bit mask `0x02`).
    Syn,
    /// Acknowledgment field significant (`ack`, bit mask `0x10`).
    Ack,
    /// No more data from sender (`fin`, bit mask `0x01`).
    Fin,
    /// Reset the connection (`rst`, bit mask `0x04`).
    Rst,
    /// Push Function (`psh`, bit mask `0x08`).
    Psh,
    /// Urgent Pointer field significant (`urg`, bit mask `0x20`).
    Urg,
    /// ECN-Echo (`ece`, bit mask `0x40`, RFC 3168).
    Ece,
    /// Congestion Window Reduced (`cwr`, bit mask `0x80`, RFC 3168).
    Cwr,
}

/// RFC 9293 / RFC 7323 / RFC 2018 TCP header options specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `tcp [syn] [ack] [fin] [rst] [psh] [urg] [ece] [cwr] [srcport <u16>] [dstport <u16>] [seq <u32>] [acknum <u32>] [win <u16>] [urgent <u16>] [mss <u16>] [wscale <u8>] [sackperm] [tsval <u32>] [tsecr <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "tcp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9293")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9293")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 7323")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC7323")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 2018")]
#[doc(alias = "proto 6")]
#[doc(alias = "TcpSpec")]
#[doc(alias = "mss")]
#[doc(alias = "wscale")]
#[doc(alias = "sackperm")]
#[doc(alias = "tsval")]
#[doc(alias = "tsecr")]
#[doc(alias = "seq")]
#[doc(alias = "acknum")]
#[doc(alias = "win")]
#[doc(alias = "urgent")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct TcpOptions {
    /// Maximum Segment Size option (`mss <u16>`, Kind `2`, Length `4`).
    pub mss: Option<u16>,
    /// Window Scale shift count option (`wscale <u8>`, Kind `3`, Length `3`, RFC 7323).
    pub wscale: Option<u8>,
    /// Selective Acknowledgment Permitted option (`sackperm`, Kind `4`, Length `2`, RFC 2018).
    pub sack_perm: bool,
    /// TCP Timestamps Value (`tsval <u32>`, Kind `8`, Length `10`, RFC 7323).
    pub tsval: Option<u32>,
    /// TCP Timestamps Echo Reply (`tsecr <u32>`, Kind `8`, Length `10`, RFC 7323).
    pub tsecr: Option<u32>,
}

/// Type alias for Transmission Control Protocol (RFC 9293 / RFC 7323) specification ([`TcpOptions`]).
///
/// Syntax mapping: `tcp [syn] [ack] [fin] [rst] [psh] [urg] [ece] [cwr] [srcport <u16>] [dstport <u16>] [seq <u32>] [acknum <u32>] [win <u16>] [urgent <u16>] [mss <u16>] [wscale <u8>] [sackperm] [tsval <u32>] [tsecr <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "tcp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9293")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 7323")]
#[doc(alias = "mss")]
#[doc(alias = "wscale")]
#[doc(alias = "sackperm")]
#[doc(alias = "tsval")]
#[doc(alias = "tsecr")]
pub type TcpSpec = TcpOptions;
```

## `src/ast/l7/amqp.rs`

```rust
//! Advanced Message Queuing Protocol v0-9-1 (AMQP 0-9-1) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`AmqpSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an AMQP 0-9-1 wire frame
//! over TCP port 5672 (or 5671 for AMQPS). On the wire, a session begins with the 8-byte protocol
//! header `amqp\x00\x00\x09\x01`, followed by general frames consisting of a 1-byte Frame Type
//! (`1` Method, `2` Content Header, `3` Content Body, `8` Heartbeat), a 16-bit Channel number, a
//! 32-bit Payload Size, the class/method arguments, and a trailing `0xCE` frame-end octet.
//! Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax models AMQP frames via
//! `amqp [protocolheader | connectionstart | channelopen | basicpublish | basicdeliver | heartbeat] [channel <u16>] [exchange <str>] [routingkey <str>]`.

/// Advanced Message Queuing Protocol v0-9-1 (AMQP 0-9-1) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `amqp [protocolheader | connectionstart | channelopen | basicpublish | basicdeliver | heartbeat] [channel <u16>] [exchange <str>] [routingkey <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "amqp")]
#[doc(alias = "AMQP 0-9-1")]
#[doc(alias = "ISO/IEC 19464")]
#[doc(alias = "5672")]
#[doc(alias = "protocolheader")]
#[doc(alias = "connectionstart")]
#[doc(alias = "channelopen")]
#[doc(alias = "basicpublish")]
#[doc(alias = "basicdeliver")]
#[doc(alias = "heartbeat")]
#[doc(alias = "channel")]
#[doc(alias = "exchange")]
#[doc(alias = "routingkey")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct AmqpSpec<'a> {
    /// 8-byte `amqp\x00\x00\x09\x01` protocol header handshake flag (`protocolheader`).
    pub is_protocol_header: bool,
    /// `Connection.Start` (Class 10, Method 10) frame flag (`connectionstart`).
    pub is_connection_start: bool,
    /// `Channel.Open` (Class 20, Method 10) frame flag (`channelopen`).
    pub is_channel_open: bool,
    /// `Basic.Publish` (Class 60, Method 40) frame flag (`basicpublish`).
    pub is_basic_publish: bool,
    /// `Basic.Deliver` (Class 60, Method 60) frame flag (`basicdeliver`).
    pub is_basic_deliver: bool,
    /// AMQP Heartbeat (Frame Type 8) flag (`heartbeat`).
    pub is_heartbeat: bool,
    /// 16-bit virtual channel number (`channel <u16>`, default `1` or `0` for connection/heartbeat).
    pub channel: Option<u16>,
    /// Target exchange name for `Basic.Publish` / `Basic.Deliver` (`exchange <str>`).
    pub exchange: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Message routing key string (`routingkey <str>`).
    pub routing_key: Option<&'a str>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l7/bacnet.rs`

```rust
//! Building Automation and Control Networks (BACnet/IP, ANSI/ASHRAE 135) AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`BacnetSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an ANSI/ASHRAE 135
//! BACnet/IP frame over UDP port 47808 (`0xBAC0`). On the wire, a BACnet/IP packet consists of a
//! 4-byte BACnet Virtual Link Control (BVLC) header (`0x81` type, function `0x0A` Original-Unicast
//! or `0x0B` Original-Broadcast, and 16-bit length), a 2-byte NPDU header (Version `0x01` and
//! control byte), and an APDU encoding unconfirmed services (`Who-Is`, `I-Am`) or confirmed
//! services (`ReadProperty` `0x0C`, `WriteProperty` `0x0F`). Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `bacnet [whois | iam | readproperty | writeproperty] [invokeid <u8>] [objecttype <u16>] [objectinstance <u32>] [propertyid <u32>] [value <u32>]`.

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// ANSI/ASHRAE 135 BACnet/IP Building Automation protocol specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `bacnet [whois | iam | readproperty | writeproperty] [invokeid <u8>] [objecttype <u16>] [objectinstance <u32>] [propertyid <u32>] [value <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "bacnet")]
#[doc(alias = "ASHRAE 135")]
#[doc(alias = "ISO 16484-5")]
#[doc(alias = "BVLC")]
#[doc(alias = "47808")]
#[doc(alias = "whois")]
#[doc(alias = "iam")]
#[doc(alias = "readproperty")]
#[doc(alias = "writeproperty")]
#[doc(alias = "invokeid")]
#[doc(alias = "objecttype")]
#[doc(alias = "objectinstance")]
#[doc(alias = "propertyid")]
#[doc(alias = "value")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct BacnetSpec<'a> {
    /// Unconfirmed `Who-Is` (service choice 8) broadcast discovery flag (`whois`).
    pub is_who_is: bool,
    /// Unconfirmed `I-Am` (service choice 0) device announcement flag (`iam`).
    pub is_i_am: bool,
    /// Confirmed `ReadProperty` (service choice 12) flag (`readproperty`).
    pub is_read_property: bool,
    /// Confirmed `WriteProperty` (service choice 15) flag (`writeproperty`).
    pub is_write_property: bool,
    /// 8-bit confirmed service Invoke ID (`invokeid <u8>`, default `1`).
    pub invoke_id: Option<u8>,
    /// 10-bit BACnet Object Type code (`objecttype <u16>`, e.g., `0` Analog Input, `8` Device).
    pub object_type: Option<u16>,
    /// 22-bit BACnet Object Instance number (`objectinstance <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub object_instance: Option<u32>,
    /// BACnet Property Identifier (`propertyid <u32>`, default `85` for `Present_Value`).
    pub property_id: Option<u32>,
    /// Property unsigned integer value for `WriteProperty` (`value <u32>`).
    pub value: Option<u32>,
    /// Lifetime marker preserving uniform `'a` parameterization across L7 specs.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l7/coap.rs`

```rust
//! Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP, RFC 7252) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`CoapSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an RFC 7252 Constrained
//! Application Protocol (CoAP) message over UDP port 5683 (or 5684 for DTLS-secured CoAPS). On the
//! wire, a CoAP frame starts with a 4-byte binary header (2-bit Version `1`, 2-bit Type `con`/`non`
//! /`ack`/`rst`, 4-bit Token Length, 8-bit `c.dd` Code byte, and 16-bit big-endian Message ID),
//! followed by the variable-length Token, delta-encoded CoAP Options (`Uri-Path` option 11,
//! `Content-Format` option 12), and an optional `0xFF` payload marker. Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `coap [con | non | ack | rst] [code <str>] [msgid <u16>] [token <u32>] [uripath <str>] [contentformat <u16>]`.

/// RFC 7252 Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `coap [con | non | ack | rst] [code <str>] [msgid <u16>] [token <u32>] [uripath <str>] [contentformat <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "coap")]

#[doc(alias = "RFC7252")]
#[doc(alias = "5683")]
#[doc(alias = "con")]
#[doc(alias = "non")]
#[doc(alias = "ack")]
#[doc(alias = "rst")]
#[doc(alias = "code")]
#[doc(alias = "msgid")]
#[doc(alias = "token")]
#[doc(alias = "uripath")]
#[doc(alias = "contentformat")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct CoapSpec<'a> {
    /// CoAP message type (`con`, `non`, `ack`, `rst`, default `"CON"`).
    pub msg_type: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Dotted class.detail request/response code (`code <str>`, e.g., `"0.01"` GET, `"2.05"` Content).
    pub code: Option<&'a str>,
    /// 16-bit Message ID for duplicate detection and ACK correlation (`msgid <u16>`).
    pub msgid: Option<u16>,
    /// 32-bit request/response matching Token (`token <u32>`).
    pub token: Option<u32>,
    /// Slash-delimited `Uri-Path` option segments (`uripath <str>`).
    pub uri_path: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Numeric CoAP `Content-Format` option 12 identifier (`contentformat <u16>`, e.g., `50` for JSON, `60` for CBOR).
    pub content_format: Option<u16>,
}

## `src/ast/l7/dhcp.rs`

```rust
//! Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCPv4 / DHCPv6) (RFC 2131 / RFC 2132 / RFC 8415) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCPv4 / DHCPv6) packets over UDP ports 67/68 (DHCPv4) and UDP ports 546/547 (DHCPv6). On the wire, the protocol uses a 236-byte BOOTP fixed header (op, htype, hlen, hops, 32-bit xid, secs, flags, ciaddr, yiaddr, siaddr, giaddr, 16-byte chaddr, 64-byte sname, 128-byte file), 4-byte RFC 1497 magic cookie 0x63825363, and TLV DHCP options (Option 53 Message Type, Option 1 Subnet Mask, Option 3 Router, Option 6 DNS, Option 12 Hostname, Option 51 Lease Time, 0xFF End), or 4-byte DHCPv6 msg-type + 24-bit transaction-id header.
//! Every field in [`DhcpSpec`] is optional so authors can emit zero-configuration default
//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b dhcp [discover | offer | request | ack | release | solicit | advertise | reply] [xid <u32>] [ciaddr <ip>] [yiaddr <ip>] [siaddr <ip>] [chaddr <mac>] [hostname <str>] [dnsserver <ip>] [router <ip>] [subnetmask <ip>] [leasetime <u32>]`

use core::net::IpAddr;
/// Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (v4 / v6) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `dhcp [discover | offer | request | ack | release | solicit | advertise | reply] [xid <u32>] [ciaddr <ip>] [yiaddr <ip>] [siaddr <ip>] [chaddr <mac>] [hostname <str>] [dnsserver <ip>] [router <ip>] [subnetmask <ip>] [leasetime <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "dhcp")]
#[doc(alias = "DHCPV4")]
#[doc(alias = "DHCPV6")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 2131")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC2131")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 8415")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC8415")]
#[doc(alias = "BOOTP")]
#[doc(alias = "discover")]
#[doc(alias = "offer")]
#[doc(alias = "request")]
#[doc(alias = "ack")]
#[doc(alias = "release")]
#[doc(alias = "solicit")]
#[doc(alias = "advertise")]
#[doc(alias = "reply")]
#[doc(alias = "xid")]
#[doc(alias = "ciaddr")]
#[doc(alias = "yiaddr")]
#[doc(alias = "siaddr")]
#[doc(alias = "chaddr")]
#[doc(alias = "hostname")]
#[doc(alias = "dnsserver")]
#[doc(alias = "router")]
#[doc(alias = "subnetmask")]
#[doc(alias = "leasetime")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct DhcpSpec<'a> {
    /// DHCPDISCOVER flag.
    pub is_discover: bool,
    /// DHCPv6 Solicit flag.
    pub is_solicit: bool,
    /// DHCPOFFER flag.
    pub is_offer: bool,
    /// DHCPv6 Advertise flag.
    pub is_advertise: bool,
    /// DHCPREQUEST flag.
    pub is_request: bool,
    /// DHCPACK flag.
    pub is_ack: bool,
    /// DHCPv6 Reply flag.
    pub is_reply: bool,
    /// DHCPRELEASE flag.
    pub is_release: bool,
    /// Transaction ID.
    pub xid: Option<u32>,
    /// Client IP address (ciaddr).
    pub ciaddr: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// 'Your' (client) IP address (yiaddr).
    pub yiaddr: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Next server IP address (siaddr).
    pub siaddr: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Client hardware address override.
    pub chaddr: Option<[u8; 6]>,
    /// Host name option.
    pub hostname: Option<&'a str>,
    /// DNS server option IP.
    pub dns_server: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Router default gateway option IP.
    pub router: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Subnet mask option IP.
    pub subnet_mask: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// IP address lease time in seconds.
    pub lease_time: Option<u32>,
}

```rust
//! Distributed Network Protocol v3 (DNP3, IEEE 1815-2012) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`Dnp3Spec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an IEEE 1815-2012
//! Distributed Network Protocol (DNP3) SCADA frame over TCP or UDP port 20000. On the wire, a
//! DNP3 frame begins with a 10-byte Data Link Layer header (`0x0564` start bytes, length, control
//! byte, 16-bit little-endian destination and source addresses, and 16-bit DNP3 CRC), followed by
//! a 1-byte Transport Header (`0xC0`), an Application Layer header (Application Control + Function
//! Code), and Object Header group/variation descriptors with trailing 16-bit data chunk CRCs.
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `dnp3 [read | write | select | operate | directoperate | confirm | response | unsolicitedresponse | func <str>] [src <u16>] [dst <u16>] [group <u8>] [variation <u8>] [crc <u16>]`.

/// IEEE 1815-2012 Distributed Network Protocol v3 (DNP3) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `dnp3 [read | write | select | operate | directoperate | confirm | response | unsolicitedresponse | func <str>] [src <u16>] [dst <u16>] [group <u8>] [variation <u8>] [crc <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "dnp3")]
#[doc(alias = "IEEE 1815")]
#[doc(alias = "IEEE1815")]
#[doc(alias = "20000")]
#[doc(alias = "read")]
#[doc(alias = "write")]
#[doc(alias = "func")]
#[doc(alias = "src")]
#[doc(alias = "dst")]
#[doc(alias = "group")]
#[doc(alias = "variation")]
#[doc(alias = "crc")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Dnp3Spec<'a> {
    /// Application layer function name (`func <str>`, e.g., `"READ"`, `"WRITE"`, `"SELECT"`, `"OPERATE"`, `"DIRECT_OPERATE"`, `"RESPONSE"`, `"UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE"`, `"CONFIRM"`).
    pub func: Option<&'a str>,
    /// 16-bit Data Link source address (`src <u16>`, default `1`).
    pub src: Option<u16>,
    /// 16-bit Data Link destination address (`dst <u16>`, default `10`).
    pub dst: Option<u16>,
    /// DNP3 Object Group number (`group <u8>`, default `60` for Class Data).
    pub group: Option<u8>,
    /// DNP3 Object Variation number (`variation <u8>`, default `1`).
    pub variation: Option<u8>,
    /// Optional 16-bit Data Link header CRC override (`crc <u16>`).
    pub crc: Option<u16>,
}
```

//! ODVA EtherNet/IP and Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.

//! encapsulation frame over TCP port 44818 (explicit messaging) or UDP port 2222 (implicit I/O).

//! path (Service, Class, Instance, and Attribute). Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `ethernetip [nop | listidentity | registersession | sendrrdata | sendunitdata | cmd <str>] [sessionhandle <u32>] [status <u32>] [context <u64>] [cipservice <u8>] [cipclass <u16>] [cipinstance <u16>] [cipattr <u16>]`.

/// ODVA EtherNet/IP encapsulation and Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `ethernetip [nop | listidentity | registersession | sendrrdata | sendunitdata | cmd <str>] [sessionhandle <u32>] [status <u32>] [context <u64>] [cipservice <u8>] [cipclass <u16>] [cipinstance <u16>] [cipattr <u16>]`

#[doc(alias = "cipattr")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]

## `src/ast/l7/http.rs`

```rust
//! Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1) (RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) / RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1)) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1) packets over TCP port 80 (HTTP) or custom ports (8080, 8000, 8443). On the wire, the protocol uses a CRLF-delimited text message starting with a Request-Line (`<METHOD> <URI> http/<VERSION>\r\n`) or Status-Line (`http/<VERSION> <STATUS> <REASON>\r\n`), followed by `Host:`, `User-Agent:`, `Content-Type:`, `Content-Length:`, and custom `Header: Value\r\n` fields, an empty line (`\r\n`), and an optional entity body.
//! Every field in [`HttpSpec`] is optional so authors can emit zero-configuration default
//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b http [method <str>] [uri <str>] [version <str>] [hosthdr <str>] [useragent <str>] [contenttype <str>] [status <u16>] [reason <str>] [header <key> <val>] [body <str>]`

use alloc::vec::Vec;
/// RFC 9110 / RFC 9112 HTTP/1.1 specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `http [method <str>] [uri <str>] [version <str>] [hosthdr <str>] [useragent <str>] [contenttype <str>] [status <u16>] [reason <str>] [header <key> <val>] [body <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "http")]
#[doc(alias = "HTTP11")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9110")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9110")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9112")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9112")]
#[doc(alias = "method")]
#[doc(alias = "uri")]
#[doc(alias = "version")]
#[doc(alias = "hosthdr")]
#[doc(alias = "useragent")]
#[doc(alias = "contenttype")]
#[doc(alias = "status")]
#[doc(alias = "reason")]
#[doc(alias = "header")]
#[doc(alias = "body")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct HttpSpec<'a> {
    /// HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.).
    pub method: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Request target URI.
    pub uri: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Protocol version string (e.g. "1.1").
    pub version: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Host header value.
    pub host_hdr: Option<&'a str>,
    /// User-Agent header value.
    pub user_agent: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Content-Type header value.
    pub content_type: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Status code for responses.
    pub status: Option<u16>,
    /// Reason phrase for responses.
    pub reason: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Custom HTTP headers.
    pub headers: Vec<(&'a str, &'a str)>,
    /// Message body string.
    pub body: Option<&'a str>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l7/http2.rs`

```rust
//! Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2) (RFC 9113 (HTTP/2) / RFC 7541 (HPACK)) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2) packets over TCP port 443 (h2 over TLS) or TCP port 80 (h2c cleartext). On the wire, the protocol uses a 24-octet client connection preface (`pri * http/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n`) and 9-octet binary frame headers containing 24-bit payload Length, 8-bit Frame Type (`0x0` DATA, `0x1` HEADERS, `0x4` SETTINGS, `0x6` PING, `0x7` GOAWAY, `0x8` WINDOW_UPDATE), 8-bit Flags (`END_STREAM = 0x1`, `END_HEADERS = 0x4`, `ACK = 0x1`), 1-bit Reserved flag, and 31-bit Stream Identifier.
//! Every field in [`Http2Spec`] is optional so authors can emit zero-configuration default
//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b http2 [preface | settings | headers | data | windowupdate | ping | goaway] [streamid <u32>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;
/// RFC 9113 HTTP/2 framing specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `http2 [preface | settings | headers | data | windowupdate | ping | goaway] [streamid <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "http2")]
#[doc(alias = "H2")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9113")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9113")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 7540")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC7540")]
#[doc(alias = "preface")]
#[doc(alias = "settings")]
#[doc(alias = "headers")]
#[doc(alias = "data")]
#[doc(alias = "windowupdate")]
#[doc(alias = "ping")]
#[doc(alias = "goaway")]
#[doc(alias = "streamid")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Http2Spec<'a> {
    /// Connection preface flag.
    pub is_preface: bool,
    /// SETTINGS frame flag.
    pub is_settings: bool,
    /// HEADERS frame flag.
    pub is_headers: bool,
    /// DATA frame flag.
    pub is_data: bool,
    /// WINDOW_UPDATE frame flag.
    pub is_window_update: bool,
    /// PING frame flag.
    pub is_ping: bool,
    /// GOAWAY frame flag.
    pub is_goaway: bool,
    /// Stream identifier.
    pub stream_id: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional phantom reference.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l7/imap.rs`

```rust
//! Internet Message Access Protocol v4rev1/v4rev2 (IMAP, RFC 3501 / RFC 9051) AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`ImapSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an RFC 3501 / RFC 9051
//! Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) client command or server response over TCP port 143
//! (or 993 for IMAPS). On the wire, IMAP frames consist of CRLF-terminated ASCII lines beginning
//! with an alphanumeric client command tag (e.g., `A001`), an untagged server token (`*`), or a
//! command continuation request (`+`), followed by command verbs (`login`, `select`, `FETCH`,
//! `UID`, `SEARCH`, `STORE`, `IDLE`, `LOGOUT`) or tagged completion statuses (`ok`, `NO`, `BAD`).
//! Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax models IMAP traffic with
//! `imap [tag <str>] [cmd <str>] [arg <str>] [status <str>] [response <str>]`.

/// RFC 3501 / RFC 9051 Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP4rev1/v4rev2) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `imap [tag <str>] [cmd <str>] [arg <str>] [status <str>] [response <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "imap")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 9051")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC9051")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 3501")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC3501")]
#[doc(alias = "tag")]
#[doc(alias = "cmd")]
#[doc(alias = "arg")]
#[doc(alias = "status")]
#[doc(alias = "response")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ImapSpec<'a> {
    /// Alphanumeric command tag or `*` / `+` marker (`tag <str>`, default `"A001"`).
    pub tag: Option<&'a str>,
    /// IMAP client command verb (`cmd <str>`, e.g., `"LOGIN"`, `"SELECT"`, `"FETCH"`).
    pub cmd: Option<&'a str>,
    /// IMAP command argument string (`arg <str>`, e.g., `"INBOX"`, `"1:* (FLAGS)"`).
    pub arg: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Server completion status token (`status <str>`, e.g., `"OK"`, `"NO"`, `"BAD"`).
    pub status: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Server response text or untagged status payload (`response <str>`).
    pub response: Option<&'a str>,
}

//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) packets over UDP port 4739. On the wire, the protocol uses a 16-byte IPFIX message header (16-bit Version = `0x000a`, 16-bit Message Length, 32-bit Export Time in epoch seconds, 32-bit Sequence Number, 32-bit Observation Domain ID) followed by Set Header (16-bit Set ID `>= 256` for Data Sets, 16-bit Set Length) and Information Element flow records (sourceIPv4Address, destinationIPv4Address, sourceTransportPort, destinationTransportPort, protocolIdentifier, packetDeltaCount, octetDeltaCount).

#[doc(alias = "dstport")]
#[doc(alias = "proto")]
#[doc(alias = "packets")]
#[doc(alias = "octets")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct IpfixSpec<'a> {
    /// Source IP address in flow record.
    pub srcip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Destination IP address in flow record.

```rust
//! Kerberos Network Authentication Service v5 (RFC 4120) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`KerberosSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an RFC 4120 Kerberos
//! Version 5 authentication message over UDP or TCP port 88. On the wire, Kerberos v5 encodes
//! ASN.1 DER application-tagged PDUs including Authentication Service requests/replies (`AS-REQ`
//! tag `0x6A`, `AS-REP` tag `0x6B`), Ticket-Granting Service exchanges (`TGS-REQ` tag `0x6C`,
//! `TGS-REP` tag `0x6D`), and error messages (`KRB-error` tag `0x7E`) carrying realm strings,
//! client/service principal names, and RFC 3961/8009 encryption types. Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `kerberos [asreq | asrep | tgsreq | tgsrep | krberror] [realm <str>] [cname <str>] [sname <str>] [etype <i32>]`.

/// RFC 4120 Kerberos v5 Authentication Service and Ticket-Granting Service specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `kerberos [asreq | asrep | tgsreq | tgsrep | krberror] [realm <str>] [cname <str>] [sname <str>] [etype <i32>]`
#[doc(alias = "kerberos")]
#[doc(alias = "KRB5")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 4120")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC4120")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 3961")]
#[doc(alias = "asreq")]
#[doc(alias = "asrep")]
#[doc(alias = "tgsreq")]
#[doc(alias = "tgsrep")]
#[doc(alias = "krberror")]
#[doc(alias = "realm")]
#[doc(alias = "cname")]
#[doc(alias = "sname")]
#[doc(alias = "etype")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct KerberosSpec<'a> {
    /// Authentication Service Request flag (`asreq`, msg-type 10).
    pub is_as_req: bool,
    /// Authentication Service Reply flag (`asrep`, msg-type 11).
    pub is_as_rep: bool,
    /// Ticket-Granting Service Request flag (`tgsreq`, msg-type 12).
    pub is_tgs_req: bool,
    /// Ticket-Granting Service Reply flag (`tgsrep`, msg-type 13).
    pub is_tgs_rep: bool,
    /// Kerberos Error message flag (`krberror`, msg-type 30).
    pub is_krb_error: bool,
    /// Kerberos realm string (`realm <str>`, default `"EXAMPLE.COM"`).
    pub realm: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Client principal name string (`cname <str>`, default `"alice"`).
    pub cname: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Server or service principal name string (`sname <str>`, default `"krbtgt"`).
    pub sname: Option<&'a str>,
    /// RFC 3961 / RFC 8009 encryption type code (`etype <i32>`, default `18` for AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96).
    pub etype: Option<i32>,
}
```

//! Lightweight Directory Access Protocol v3 (LDAP, RFC 4511) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`LdapSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an RFC 4511 Lightweight
//! Directory Access Protocol v3 (`LDAPMessage`) envelope over TCP or UDP port 389 (or TCP 636 for
//! LDAPS). On the wire, an `LDAPMessage` is an ASN.1 BER `SEQUENCE` (tag `0x30`) containing an
//! integer `messageid` followed by a protocol operation choice (`BindRequest` `0x60`,
//! `BindResponse` `0x61`, `SearchRequest` `0x63`, `SearchResultEntry` `0x64`,
//! `SearchResultDone` `0x65`, or `UnbindRequest` `0x42`). Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax:
//! `ldap [msgid <i32>] [bindreq | bindres | searchreq | searchentry | searchdone | unbindreq] [basedn <str>] [filter <str>] [resultcode <u32>]`.

/// RFC 4511 Lightweight Directory Access Protocol v3 (LDAP) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `ldap [msgid <i32>] [bindreq | bindres | searchreq | searchentry | searchdone | unbindreq] [basedn <str>] [filter <str>] [resultcode <u32>]`
#[doc(alias = "ldap")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 4511")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC4511")]
#[doc(alias = "389")]
#[doc(alias = "msgid")]
#[doc(alias = "bindreq")]
#[doc(alias = "bindres")]
#[doc(alias = "searchreq")]
#[doc(alias = "searchentry")]
#[doc(alias = "searchdone")]
#[doc(alias = "unbindreq")]
#[doc(alias = "basedn")]
#[doc(alias = "filter")]
#[doc(alias = "resultcode")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct LdapSpec<'a> {
    /// LDAP message identifier (`msgid <i32>`, default `1`).
    pub msgid: Option<i32>,
    /// BindRequest operation flag (`bindreq`, BER tag `0x60`).
    pub is_bind_req: bool,
    /// BindResponse operation flag (`bindres`, BER tag `0x61`).
    pub is_bind_res: bool,
    /// SearchRequest operation flag (`searchreq`, BER tag `0x63`).
    pub is_search_req: bool,
    /// SearchResultEntry operation flag (`searchentry`, BER tag `0x64`).
    pub is_search_entry: bool,
    /// SearchResultDone operation flag (`searchdone`, BER tag `0x65`).
    pub is_search_done: bool,
    /// UnbindRequest operation flag (`unbindreq`, BER tag `0x42`).
    pub is_unbind_req: bool,

    pub result_code: Option<u32>,

//! Memcached Binary and ASCII Caching Protocol Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`MemcachedSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a Memcached key-value
//! cache command over TCP or UDP port 11211. On the wire, the Memcached ASCII protocol transmits
//! human-readable command lines (`get <key>\r\n`, `set <key> <flags> <exptime> <bytes>\r\n`,
//! `stats\r\n`, `version\r\n`), whereas the Memcached Binary Protocol uses a fixed 24-byte header
//! (`0x80` request magic, 1-byte opcode, 2-byte key length, 1-byte extras length, 4-byte total
//! body length, 4-byte opaque token, and 8-byte CAS version). Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `memcached [cmd <str>] [key <str>] [value <str>] [flags <u32>] [exptime <u32>] [opcode <u8>] [opaque <u32>] [cas <u64>]`.

///
/// Syntax mapping: `memcached [cmd <str>] [key <str>] [value <str>] [flags <u32>] [exptime <u32>] [opcode <u8>] [opaque <u32>] [cas <u64>]`
#[doc(alias = "memcached")]
#[doc(alias = "11211")]
#[doc(alias = "cmd")]
#[doc(alias = "key")]
#[doc(alias = "value")]
#[doc(alias = "flags")]
#[doc(alias = "exptime")]
#[doc(alias = "opcode")]
#[doc(alias = "opaque")]
#[doc(alias = "cas")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct MemcachedSpec<'a> {
    /// Memcached command verb (`cmd <str>`, e.g., `"GET"`, `"SET"`, `"ADD"`, `"DELETE"`, `"STATS"`).
    pub cmd: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Cache item key string (`key <str>`).
    pub key: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Client-defined 32-bit flags integer (`flags <u32>`).
    pub flags: Option<u32>,
    /// Expiration time in seconds (`exptime <u32>`).
    pub exptime: Option<u32>,
    /// Cache item value payload (`value <str>`).
    pub value: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional binary protocol opcode override (`opcode <u8>`).
    pub opcode: Option<u8>,
    /// 32-bit binary protocol correlation token (`opaque <u32>`).
    pub opaque: Option<u32>,
    /// 64-bit Compare-And-Swap version identifier (`cas <u64>`).
    pub cas: Option<u64>,
}

//! Modbus TCP Application Protocol v1.1b3 Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`ModbusSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a Modbus Application
//! Protocol (MBAP) frame over TCP or UDP port 502. On the wire, a Modbus TCP ADU begins with a
//! 7-byte MBAP header (16-bit Transaction ID, 16-bit Protocol ID `0x0000`, 16-bit Length, and
//! 8-bit Unit Identifier) followed by a 1-byte Function Code (`0x01` Read Coils, `0x02` Read
//! Discrete Inputs, `0x03` Read Holding Registers, `0x04` Read Input Registers, `0x05` Write
//! Single Coil, `0x06` Write Single Register, `0x10` Write Multiple Registers) and register data.
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `modbus [txid <u16>] [protoid <u16>] [unitid <u8>] [func <str>] [addr <u16>] [count <u16>] [value <u16>] [isresponse]`.

/// Modbus TCP Application Protocol v1.1b3 (MBAP + PDU) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `modbus [txid <u16>] [protoid <u16>] [unitid <u8>] [func <str>] [addr <u16>] [count <u16>] [value <u16>] [isresponse]`
#[doc(alias = "modbus")]

#[doc(alias = "count")]
#[doc(alias = "value")]
#[doc(alias = "isresponse")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ModbusSpec<'a> {
    /// 16-bit MBAP Transaction Identifier (`txid <u16>`, default `1`).
    pub txid: Option<u16>,
    /// 16-bit MBAP Protocol Identifier (`protoid <u16>`, default `0`).
    pub proto_id: Option<u16>,
    /// 8-bit MBAP Unit Identifier addressing a slave device (`unitid <u8>`, default `1`).
    pub unitid: Option<u8>,
    /// Modbus function code name (`func <str>`, default `"READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS"`).
    pub func: Option<&'a str>,

//! Message Queuing Telemetry Transport v3.1.1 / v5.0 (MQTT, OASIS) AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`MqttSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an OASIS MQTT v3.1.1
//! control packet over TCP port 1883 (or 8883 for MQTTS). On the wire, an MQTT packet consists of
//! a 1-byte Fixed Header (4-bit control packet type `1..=14`, DUP, 2-bit QoS level, and RETAIN
//! flag), a variable-length Remaining Length integer, a type-specific Variable Header (protocol
//! name `"MQTT"`, level `4`, topic string, or 16-bit Packet Identifier), and an application
//! payload. Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax models MQTT traffic via
//! `mqtt [connect | connack | publish | puback | subscribe | suback | pingreq | pingresp | disconnect | pkttype <str>] [clientid <str>] [topic <str>] [qos <u8>] [retain] [pktid <u16>] [keepalive <u16>] [returncode <u8>]`.

/// OASIS Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT v3.1.1 / ISO/IEC 20922) specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `mqtt [connect | connack | publish | puback | subscribe | suback | pingreq | pingresp | disconnect | pkttype <str>] [clientid <str>] [topic <str>] [qos <u8>] [retain] [pktid <u16>] [keepalive <u16>] [returncode <u8>]`

#[doc(alias = "connack")]

#[doc(alias = "puback")]
#[doc(alias = "subscribe")]
#[doc(alias = "suback")]
#[doc(alias = "pingreq")]
#[doc(alias = "pingresp")]
#[doc(alias = "pkttype")]
#[doc(alias = "clientid")]
#[doc(alias = "topic")]
#[doc(alias = "qos")]
#[doc(alias = "retain")]
#[doc(alias = "pktid")]
#[doc(alias = "keepalive")]
#[doc(alias = "returncode")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct MqttSpec<'a> {
    /// Control packet type name (`connect`, `connack`, `publish`, `puback`, `subscribe`, `suback`, `pingreq`, `pingresp`).
    pub pkt_type: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Client identifier for `connect` packets (`clientid <str>`, default `"fasm-mqtt"`).
    pub client_id: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Topic filter or publication topic name (`topic <str>`, default `"test/topic"`).
    pub topic: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Quality of Service delivery level `0..=2` (`qos <u8>`).
    pub qos: Option<u8>,

```rust
//! MySQL Client/Server Wire Protocol v10 Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`MysqlSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a MySQL / MariaDB
//! client/server protocol packet over TCP port 3306. On the wire, every MySQL packet starts with a
//! 4-byte header consisting of a 24-bit little-endian payload length and a 1-byte sequence ID,
//! encapsulating Protocol v10 `HandshakeV10` greetings, `HandshakeResponse41` logins, `COM_QUERY`
//! (`0x03`) SQL statements, `OK_Packet` (`0x00`), `EOF_Packet` (`0xFE`), or `ERR_Packet` (`0xFF`).
//! Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax models MySQL frames via
//! `mysql [greeting | login | query | ok | err | eof] [serverversion <str>] [user <str>] [db <str>] [sql <str>] [errcode <u16>]`.

/// MySQL / MariaDB Client/Server Wire Protocol v10 specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `mysql [greeting | login | query | ok | err | eof] [serverversion <str>] [user <str>] [db <str>] [sql <str>] [errcode <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "mysql")]
#[doc(alias = "MySQL v10")]
#[doc(alias = "3306")]
#[doc(alias = "greeting")]
#[doc(alias = "login")]
#[doc(alias = "query")]
#[doc(alias = "sql")]
#[doc(alias = "ok")]
#[doc(alias = "err")]
#[doc(alias = "eof")]
#[doc(alias = "serverversion")]
#[doc(alias = "user")]
#[doc(alias = "db")]
#[doc(alias = "errcode")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct MysqlSpec<'a> {
    /// Server `HandshakeV10` initial greeting packet flag (`greeting`).
    pub is_greeting: bool,
    /// Client `HandshakeResponse41` login packet flag (`login`).
    pub is_login: bool,
    /// Client `COM_QUERY` (`0x03`) command flag (`query`).
    pub is_query: bool,
    /// Server `OK_Packet` (`0x00`) response flag (`ok`).
    pub is_ok: bool,
    /// Server `ERR_Packet` (`0xFF`) response flag (`err`).
    pub is_err: bool,
    /// Server `EOF_Packet` (`0xFE`) response flag (`eof`).
    pub is_eof: bool,
    /// Server version string in `HandshakeV10` (`serverversion <str>`, default `"8.0.35"`).
    pub server_version: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Client username in `HandshakeResponse41` (`user <str>`, default `"root"`).
    pub user: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Initial database schema name (`db <str>`).
    pub db: Option<&'a str>,
    /// SQL statement text for `COM_QUERY` (`sql <str>`).
    pub sql: Option<&'a str>,
    /// 16-bit MySQL error code in `ERR_Packet` (`errcode <u16>`, default `1045`).
    pub errcode: Option<u16>,
}
```

//! Cisco NetFlow Version 5 Telemetry Export (Cisco NetFlow v5 / RFC 3954 (NetFlow v9)) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Cisco NetFlow Version 5 Telemetry Export packets over UDP port 2055. On the wire, the protocol uses a 24-byte NetFlow v5 export header (16-bit version = 5, 16-bit flow count, 32-bit sys_uptime, 32-bit unix_secs, 32-bit unix_nsecs, 32-bit flow_sequence, 8-bit engine_type, 8-bit engine_id, 16-bit sampling_interval) followed by 48-byte fixed flow records containing srcaddr, dstaddr, nexthop, input/output SNMP ifIndex, dPkts, dOctets, first/last timestamps, srcport, dstport, tcp_flags, prot, tos, and src_as/dst_as.

//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b netflow [srcip <ip>] [dstip <ip>] [srcport <u16>] [dstport <u16>] [proto <u8>] [packets <u32>] [octets <u32>]`

#[doc(alias = "dstport")]
#[doc(alias = "proto")]
#[doc(alias = "packets")]
#[doc(alias = "octets")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct NetflowSpec<'a> {
    /// Source IP address in flow record.
    pub srcip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Destination IP address in flow record.
    pub dstip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Source port in flow record.

//! Network File System v2/v3/v4 (NFS, RFC 1094 / RFC 1813 / RFC 7530) AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`NfsSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a Network File System
//! (NFS) call encapsulated in an ONC RPC v2 (RFC 5531) record-marked message over TCP or UDP port

//! bit `0x80000000`), an ONC RPC Call header (XID, Message Type `0`, RPC Version `2`, Program

//! compound tags or filehandle paths. Canonical `.fasm` syntax:

#[doc(alias = "nfs")]

//! Network Time Protocol v4 (NTPv4) (RFC 5905 / RFC 4330 (SNTP)) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Network Time Protocol v4 (NTPv4) packets over UDP port 123. On the wire, the protocol uses a 48-byte fixed NTP packet header starting with packed 8-bit LI (2 bits) / VN (3 bits) / Mode (3 bits) byte, 8-bit Stratum, 8-bit Poll interval (log2 seconds), signed 8-bit Precision, 32-bit Root Delay, 32-bit Root Dispersion, 32-bit Reference ID (ASCII kiss-code or IPv4), and four 64-bit fixed-point timestamps (Reference, Origin, Receive, Transmit).
//! Every field in [`NtpSpec`] is optional so authors can emit zero-configuration default
//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b ntp [li <u8>] [vn <u8>] [mode <u8>] [stratum <u8>] [poll <u8>] [precision <i8>] [refid <str>] [txtimestamp <u64>]`

/// RFC 5905 Network Time Protocol specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `ntp [li <u8>] [vn <u8>] [mode <u8>] [stratum <u8>] [poll <u8>] [precision <i8>] [refid <str>] [txtimestamp <u64>]`
#[doc(alias = "ntp")]
#[doc(alias = "SNTP")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 5905")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC5905")]
#[doc(alias = "li")]
#[doc(alias = "vn")]
#[doc(alias = "mode")]
#[doc(alias = "stratum")]
#[doc(alias = "poll")]
#[doc(alias = "precision")]
#[doc(alias = "refid")]
#[doc(alias = "txtimestamp")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct NtpSpec<'a> {
    /// Leap Indicator (0..=3).
    pub li: Option<u8>,
    /// Version Number (1..=4).
    pub vn: Option<u8>,
    /// Mode (0..=7).
    pub mode: Option<u8>,
    /// Stratum (0..=16).
    pub stratum: Option<u8>,

}

## `src/ast/l7/opcua.rs`

```rust
//! OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA, IEC 62541-6) Binary Protocol AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`OpcuaSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of an IEC 62541-6 OPC
//! Unified Architecture (OPC UA) Connection Protocol (`UACP`) binary frame over TCP port 4840.
//! On the wire, an OPC UA frame starts with a 3-byte ASCII MessageType (`HEL`, `ack`, `err`,
//! `OPN`, `CLO`, or `msg`), a 1-byte ChunkType (`'F'` Final, `'C'` Intermediate, `'A'` Aborted),
//! and a 32-bit little-endian MessageSize, followed by either connection parameters (`EndpointUrl`)
//! or SecureChannel/Sequence headers (`SecureChannelId`, `TokenId`, `SequenceNumber`, `RequestId`)
//! and an ExpandedNodeId service body. Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `opcua [msgtype <str>] [chunktype <str>] [securechannelid <u32>] [tokenid <u32>] [seqnum <u32>] [reqid <u32>] [endpointurl <str>] [nodeid <str>]`.

/// IEC 62541-6 OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA) Binary Protocol specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `opcua [msgtype <str>] [chunktype <str>] [securechannelid <u32>] [tokenid <u32>] [seqnum <u32>] [reqid <u32>] [endpointurl <str>] [nodeid <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "opcua")]
#[doc(alias = "OPC UA")]
#[doc(alias = "IEC 62541")]
#[doc(alias = "4840")]
#[doc(alias = "msgtype")]
#[doc(alias = "chunktype")]
#[doc(alias = "securechannelid")]
#[doc(alias = "tokenid")]
#[doc(alias = "seqnum")]
#[doc(alias = "reqid")]
#[doc(alias = "endpointurl")]
#[doc(alias = "nodeid")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct OpcuaSpec<'a> {
    /// 3-character UACP message type (`msgtype <str>`, e.g., `"HEL"`, `"ACK"`, `"OPN"`, `"CLO"`, `"MSG"`, `"ERR"`).
    pub msg_type: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Single-character chunking indicator (`chunktype <str>`, `'F'`, `'C'`, or `'A'`, default `'F'`).
    pub chunk_type: Option<char>,
    /// 32-bit SecureChannel identifier (`securechannelid <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub secure_channel_id: Option<u32>,
    /// 32-bit Security Token identifier (`tokenid <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub token_id: Option<u32>,
    /// 32-bit chunk Sequence Number (`seqnum <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub seq_num: Option<u32>,
    /// 32-bit service call Request ID (`reqid <u32>`, default `1`).
    pub req_id: Option<u32>,
    /// Server discovery URL for `HEL` messages (`endpointurl <str>`, default `"opc.tcp://localhost:4840"`).
    pub endpoint_url: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Target NodeId string for `msg` service requests (`nodeid <str>`).
    pub node_id: Option<&'a str>,
}

//! PostgreSQL Frontend/Backend Wire Protocol v3.0 Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`PostgresSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a PostgreSQL
//! Frontend/Backend Protocol v3.0 (`0x00030000`) message over TCP port 5432. On the wire, the
//! initial `StartupMessage` begins with a 32-bit length and protocol version `196608` followed by
//! NUL-terminated parameter pairs (`user`, `database`), while all subsequent frontend and backend
//! messages start with a 1-byte type tag (`'Q'` Query, `'R'` AuthenticationOk, `'C'`
//! CommandComplete, `'Z'` ReadyForQuery, `'E'` ErrorResponse) and a 32-bit big-endian length.
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `postgres [startup | query | authok | commandcomplete | readyforquery | errorresponse] [user <str>] [db <str>] [sql <str>]`.

/// PostgreSQL Frontend/Backend Protocol 3.0 specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `postgres [startup | query | authok | commandcomplete | readyforquery | errorresponse] [user <str>] [db <str>] [sql <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "postgres")]
#[doc(alias = "PostgreSQL")]
#[doc(alias = "FEBE")]
#[doc(alias = "5432")]
#[doc(alias = "startup")]
#[doc(alias = "query")]
#[doc(alias = "sql")]
#[doc(alias = "readyforquery")]
#[doc(alias = "commandcomplete")]
#[doc(alias = "errorresponse")]
#[doc(alias = "authok")]
#[doc(alias = "user")]
#[doc(alias = "db")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct PostgresSpec<'a> {
    /// Frontend `StartupMessage` (version 3.0) flag (`startup`).
    pub is_startup: bool,
    /// Frontend simple `Query` (`'Q'`) flag (`query`).
    pub is_query: bool,
    /// Backend `ReadyForQuery` (`'Z'`) message flag (`readyforquery`).
    pub is_ready_for_query: bool,
    /// Backend `CommandComplete` (`'C'`) message flag (`commandcomplete`).
    pub is_command_complete: bool,
    /// Backend `ErrorResponse` (`'E'`) message flag (`errorresponse`).
    pub is_error_response: bool,
    /// Backend `AuthenticationOk` (`'R'`, code 0) message flag (`authok`).
    pub is_auth_ok: bool,
    /// Database user parameter for `StartupMessage` (`user <str>`, default `"postgres"`).
    pub user: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Database name parameter for `StartupMessage` (`db <str>`, default `"postgres"`).
    pub db: Option<&'a str>,
    /// SQL query string for `'Q'` frontend messages (`sql <str>`).
    pub sql: Option<&'a str>,
}

## `src/ast/l7/redis.rs`

```rust
//! Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP2/RESP3) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`RedisSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a Redis Serialization
//! Protocol (RESP2/RESP3) client command array or server reply over TCP port 6379 (or 26379 for
//! Redis Sentinel). On the wire, client commands are encoded as RESP Arrays (`*<count>\r\n`) of
//! Bulk Strings (`$<len>\r\n<bytes>\r\n`), while server replies use type-prefixed frames: Simple
//! Strings (`+ok\r\n`), Errors (`-err ...\r\n`), Integers (`:<n>\r\n`), or Bulk Strings.
//! Canonical FrameAssembly `.fasm` syntax models Redis traffic via
//! `redis [cmd <str>] [args <str>] [replytype <str>] [value <str>]`.

use alloc::vec::Vec;

/// Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP2/RESP3) command or reply specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `redis [cmd <str>] [args <str>] [replytype <str>] [value <str>]`
#[doc(alias = "redis")]
#[doc(alias = "RESP")]
#[doc(alias = "RESP2")]
#[doc(alias = "RESP3")]
#[doc(alias = "cmd")]
#[doc(alias = "args")]
#[doc(alias = "replytype")]
#[doc(alias = "value")]
#[doc(alias = "6379")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct RedisSpec<'a> {
    /// Redis command verb (`cmd <str>`, e.g., `"PING"`, `"SET"`, `"GET"`, `"HSET"`, `"XADD"`).
    pub cmd: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Command arguments list (`args <str>`, split on whitespace into RESP bulk strings).
    pub args: Vec<&'a str>,
    /// Server RESP reply type (`replytype <str>`, e.g., `"STATUS"`, `"ERROR"`, `"INTEGER"`, `"BULK"`).
    pub reply_type: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Server reply value or bulk string payload (`value <str>`).
    pub value: Option<&'a str>,
}
```

## `src/ast/l7/rtp.rs`

```rust
//! Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) (RFC 3550 / RFC 3551 (RTP/AVP Audio and Video Profiles)) Layer 7 AST definitions.
//!
//! This module defines the abstract syntax tree (AST) configuration parameters for synthesizing
//! Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) packets over UDP port 5004 (or negotiated even UDP media port). On the wire, the protocol uses a 12-byte fixed RTP header: Byte 0 packs 2-bit Version (`V = 2`), 1-bit Padding (`P`), 1-bit Extension (`X`), and 4-bit CSRC Count (`CC`); Byte 1 packs 1-bit Marker (`M`) and 7-bit Payload Type (`pt`, e.g. `0` PCMU/G.711u, `8` PCMA/G.711a, `9` G.722, `18` G.729, `96..127` dynamic Opus/H.264); followed by 16-bit Sequence Number, 32-bit Media Timestamp, and 32-bit Synchronization Source (`ssrc`) identifier.
//! Every field in [`RtpSpec`] is optional so authors can emit zero-configuration default
//! frames or override specific protocol header fields and attributes.
//!
//! Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `a -> b rtp [pt <u8>] [seq <u16>] [timestamp <u32>] [ssrc <u32>] [marker <u8>]`

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// RFC 3550 Real-time Transport Protocol specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `rtp [pt <u8>] [seq <u16>] [timestamp <u32>] [ssrc <u32>] [marker <u8>]`
#[doc(alias = "rtp")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 3550")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC3550")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 3551")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC3551")]
#[doc(alias = "pt")]
#[doc(alias = "seq")]
#[doc(alias = "timestamp")]
#[doc(alias = "ssrc")]
#[doc(alias = "marker")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct RtpSpec<'a> {
    /// Payload type (0..=127).
    pub pt: Option<u8>,
    /// Sequence number.
    pub seq: Option<u16>,
    /// Timestamp value.
    pub timestamp: Option<u32>,
    /// Synchronization Source identifier.
    pub ssrc: Option<u32>,
    /// Marker bit (0 or 1).
    pub marker: Option<u8>,
    /// Optional phantom reference.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}
```

#[doc(alias = "cseq")]
#[doc(alias = "transporthdr")]
#[doc(alias = "session")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct RtspSpec<'a> {
    /// RTSP method.

```rust
//! Siemens S7 Communication (S7comm, ISO-on-TCP RFC 1006) Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) definitions.
//!
//! This module defines [`S7commSpec`], the zero-copy AST representation of a Siemens SIMATIC S7
//! PLC communication frame over TCP port 102 (ISO-on-TCP, RFC 1006). On the wire, an S7comm packet
//! encapsulates a 4-byte TPKT header (Version `3`, 16-bit total length) and a 3-byte COTP DT Data
//! header (`0x02 0xF0 0x80`) around a 10-byte S7 header (`0x32` Protocol ID, `rosctr` message type,
//! PDU Reference, parameter length, and data length) plus `Setup_Communication` (`0xF0`),
//! `Read_Var` (`0x04`), `Write_Var` (`0x05`), or `PLC_Control` (`0x28`) parameters. Canonical `.fasm` syntax:
//! `s7comm [rosctr <str>] [pduref <u16>] [func <str>] [area <u8>] [dbnum <u16>] [offset <u32>] [count <u16>]`.

/// Siemens SIMATIC S7 Communication (S7comm over TPKT/COTP) protocol specification.
///
/// Syntax mapping: `s7comm [rosctr <str>] [pduref <u16>] [func <str>] [area <u8>] [dbnum <u16>] [offset <u32>] [count <u16>]`
#[doc(alias = "s7comm")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC 1006")]
#[doc(alias = "RFC1006")]
#[doc(alias = "ISO-on-TCP")]
#[doc(alias = "TPKT")]
#[doc(alias = "COTP")]
#[doc(alias = "rosctr")]
#[doc(alias = "pduref")]
#[doc(alias = "func")]
#[doc(alias = "area")]
#[doc(alias = "dbnum")]
#[doc(alias = "offset")]
#[doc(alias = "count")]
#[doc(alias = "102")]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct S7commSpec<'a> {
    /// Remote Operating Service Control type (`rosctr <str>`, e.g., `"JOB"`, `"ACK"`, `"ACK_DATA"`, `"USERDATA"`).
    pub rosctr: Option<&'a str>,
    /// 16-bit S7 PDU Reference correlation identifier (`pduref <u16>`, default `1`).
    pub pdu_ref: Option<u16>,
    /// S7 parameter function name (`func <str>`, e.g., `"SETUP_COMM"`, `"READ_VAR"`, `"WRITE_VAR"`, `"PLC_CONTROL"`).
    pub func: Option<&'a str>,
    /// S7ANY memory area code (`area <u8>`, default `0x84` for Data Blocks).
